author.name: Xingzhou Pang, Yifan Hou, Junling Wang, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: This paper investigates why vision-language models fail at visual counting, decomposing the task into individuation, magnitude awareness, and symbolic mapping. Using synthetic Go boards and linear probes, the authors show perception is intact but the symbolic mapping stage collapses during extrapolation, isolating the true bottleneck.

entry.title: TRACES: Proactive Safety Auditing for Multi-Turn LLM Agents via Trajectory-State Modeling

author.name: Jiaqian Li, Yanshu Li, Boxuan Zhang, Ruixiang Tang, Kuan-Hao Huang

entry.summary: TRACES is a representation-based proactive safety auditor that learns prefix-level trajectory risk states from an observer LLM's hidden representations for multi-turn agents. It models temporal evolution of latent features to flag drift toward unsafe behavior before it surfaces.

entry.title: Beyond Input Understanding: Diagnosing Multilingual Mathematical Reasoning with Directed Acyclic Trace Graphs

author.name: Jiaqiao Zhang, Zhoujun Li, Raoyuan Zhao, Jian Lan, Thomas Seidl, Michael A. Hedderich, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Yihong Liu

entry.summary: DATG maps multilingual reasoning traces to language-independent mathematical anchors and dependencies to diagnose why large reasoning models underperform in non-English languages. It shows reasoning language itself, not just input understanding, affects accuracy even on English problems.

entry.title: Escape the Language Prior: Mitigating Late-Stage Modality Collapse in Audio Reasoning via Modality-Aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Cihan Xiao, Yiwen Shao, Chenxing Li, Xiang He, Zhenwen Liang, Steve Yves, Sanjeev Khudanpur, Liefeng Bo

entry.summary: MAPO is a modality-aware RL post-training framework for audio and omni-modal LLMs that addresses late-stage modality collapse, where extended reasoning abandons the source audio in favor of textual priors. It replaces uniform GRPO gradients with modality-sensitive optimization.

entry.title: Playing with Words, Improving with Rewards: Training Language Models for Creative Association

author.name: Vijeta Deshpande, Namrata Shivagunde, Sherin Muckatira, Hadrien Glaude, Mikhail Gronas, Claire Stevenson, Roger Beaty, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: This paper trains LLMs on Codenames, a word-association game exercising divergent and convergent thinking with verifiable outcomes, using RL with verifiable rewards to bypass subjective human judgment. Trained Qwen3 models improve across creativity and reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: ResearchMath-14K: Scaling Research-Level Mathematics via Agents

author.name: Guijin Son, Seungyeop Yi, Minju Gwak, Hyunwoo Ko, Wongi Jang, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: ResearchMath-14K is the largest collection of research-level mathematical problems to date (14,056 problems) curated via a multi-agent pipeline, plus 220K teacher reasoning trajectories. The authors observe recurring avoidance behaviors like non-attempts and fabricated references in model outputs.

entry.title: ATLAS: All-round Testing of Long-context Abilities across Scales

author.name: Deli Huang, Cunguang Wang, Hongyin Tang, Zhe Tang, Linsen Guo, Dongyu Ru, Ruoshi Yuan, Ziyue Zhu, Xiaoyu Li, Ziwen Wang, Chen Zhang, Anchun Gui, Wen Zan, Jiaqi Zhang, Xuezhi Cao, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: ATLAS reframes long-context evaluation as length-dependent capability profiling, introducing a layered task taxonomy, length-aware AUC scoring over an 8K-1M grid, and a composite score. It exposes failure modes hidden by single-length benchmarks, such as performance collapse with length and retrieval not transferring to downstream use.

entry.title: Benchmarking Single-Factor Physical Video-to-Audio Generation

author.name: Tingle Li, Siddharth Gururani, Kevin J. Shih, Gantavya Bhatt, Sang-gil Lee, Zhifeng Kong, Arushi Goel, Gopala Anumanchipalli, Ming-Yu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces FlatSounds, a benchmark that audits whether video-to-audio generation models capture true physical processes through controlled counterfactual pairs and single-video pattern tests. It reveals that current state-of-the-art models trade off perceptual realism against physical correctness.

entry.title: GMOS: Grounding Moving Object Segmentation in 3D Space and Time

author.name: Junyu Xie, Tengda Han, Weidi Xie, Andrew Zisserman

entry.summary: GMOS grounds moving object segmentation directly in 3D space and time from RGB video, producing 3D-aware, temporally fine-grained segmentation without relying on precomputed 2D flow. It addresses limitations of treating motion as a sequence-level attribute.

entry.title: Low Rank for Rank: Uncertainty-Aware Task-Specific LLM Ranking under Sparse Pairwise Comparisons

author.name: Jiachun Li, David Simchi-Levi, Will Wei Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a low-rank framework for task-specific LLM ranking from sparse pairwise comparisons, modeling the task-by-model ability matrix as low rank to share information across tasks while preserving task-specific differences. It develops an uncertainty-aware estimator addressing instability in fine-grained leaderboards.

entry.title: Accelerating Constrained Decoding with Token Space Compression

author.name: Michael Sullivan, Alexander Koller

entry.summary: CFGzip is an offline technique for compressing the token search space in context-free-grammar constrained decoding, dramatically reducing per-step overhead that grows with grammar complexity. It reports latency reductions up to two orders of magnitude with a SOTA grammar engine.

entry.title: PokerSkill: LLMs Can Play Expert-Level Poker without Training or Solvers

author.name: Boning Li, Baoxiang Wang, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: PokerSkill is a training-free, solver-free framework that uses detailed rule-based poker skills as a structured action-grounding interface for LLMs, with a deterministic context engine retrieving relevant skills. It claims expert-level poker play without the millions of core-hours required by CFR solvers.

entry.title: Unveiling Multi-regime Patterns in SciML: Distinct Failure Modes and Regime-specific Optimization

author.name: Yuxin Wang, Yuanzhe Hu, Xiaokun Zhong, Xiaopeng Wang, Haiquan Lu, Tianyu Pang, Michael W. Mahoney, Yujun Yan, Pu Ren, Yaoqing Yang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a consistent three-regime structure in scientific machine learning training across models, constraints, and optimizers, with regime-specific optimization effectiveness. It uses a diagnostic framework jointly analyzing performance, training dynamics, and loss-landscape geometry.

entry.title: GrepSeek: Training Search Agents for Direct Corpus Interaction

author.name: Alireza Salemi, Chang Zeng, Atharva Nijasure, Jui-Hui Chung, Razieh Rahimi, Fernando Diaz, Hamed Zamani

entry.summary: GrepSeek trains a compact search agent for direct corpus interaction, issuing executable shell commands to find evidence rather than relying on a pre-indexed retriever. It offers a complementary paradigm where the corpus itself is the search environment.

entry.title: The New Pro Se: Generative AI and the Surge in Federal Civil Self-Representation

author.name: Or Cohen-Sasson

entry.summary: Analyzes about 2.8 million federal civil filings to show pro se (self-represented) plaintiff rates rose from 11.33% to 16.94% after generative AI became widely available, with persistent effects after robustness checks. It examines downstream changes in complaint text and outcomes, especially in civil rights cases.

entry.title: HARP: Hadamard-Preconditioned Adaptive Rotation Processor for Extreme LLM Quantization

author.name: Artur Zagitov, Gleb Molodtsov, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Proposes HARP, a learnable structured two-sided orthogonal rotation processor that replaces fixed randomized Hadamard transforms for extreme low-bit LLM quantization while preserving full-precision equivalence. It adapts the rotated basis to layer, calibration data, and quantizer using sparse butterfly blocks.

entry.title: How Reliable Are AI Attackers Against a Fixed Vulnerable Target? A 400-Run Empirical Study of LLM Penetration Testing Consistency

author.name: Galip Tolga Erdem

entry.summary: Reports the first large-scale empirical study of LLM penetration-testing consistency across 400 autonomous runs and four models against a fixed vulnerable target. Finds models almost never refused and characterizes reliability variation.

entry.title: PARCEL: Pool-Anchored Resampling with Conditioned Elastic Queries for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding

author.name: Selim Kuzucu, Alessio Tonioni, Vasile Lup, Bernt Schiele, Federico Tombari, Muhammad Ferjad Naeem

entry.summary: Introduces PARCEL, an elastic visual-token compression method for vision-language models that combines pool-anchored resampling with conditioned queries to preserve spatial grounding under aggressive compression. Aims to resolve conflicts between pooling and query-based compression.

entry.title: Do Proactive Agents Really Need an LLM to Decide When to Wake and What to Anchor?

author.name: Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Amir H. Abdi, Michel Galley, Zhikai Chen, Siheng Xiong, Xiaoqian Wang, Jing Gao

entry.summary: Questions whether proactive agents need an LLM call on every event, instead treating user activity as a temporal graph and using a small graph-learning model to decide when to wake and what to anchor. Reserves LLM calls only for the final user-facing handoff.

entry.title: Same Evidence, Different Answers: Canonical-Context On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Language Models

author.name: Zizhuo Lin, Quanling Liu, Jinsheng Quan, Chao Zhang, Yifan Zhu, Xing Shi, Jingtao Xu, Zhihui Li, Yawei Luo

entry.summary: Introduces Canonical-Context On-Policy Distillation to reduce self-anchored drift, where LLMs reach different answers in multi-turn sharded conversations versus full prompts despite identical evidence. Uses a full-prompt teacher to distill a sharded-context student.

entry.title: In-Context Reward Adaptation for Robust Preference Modeling

author.name: Zhenyu Sun, Zheng Xu, Ermin Wei

entry.summary: Proposes in-context reward adaptation, a transformer-based framework that models diverse and unseen human preferences on the fly via in-context learning rather than retraining static reward models. Aims for robust preference modeling across unseen domains in RLHF.

entry.title: Knowledge Offloading: Decomposing LLMs into Sparse Backbones and Memory Modules

author.name: Karim Galliamov, Rochelle Choenni, Ivan Titov

entry.summary: Proposes knowledge offloading (KOFF), decomposing a pretrained LLM into a sparse shared backbone plus domain-specific external memory modules implemented as LoRA adapters and learned KV caches. Shows non-trivial capacity can be moved out of the backbone with limited ability loss.

entry.title: Inferring the Size of Large Language Models From Popular Text Memorization

author.name: Ivica Nikolic

entry.summary: Proposes a black-box method to infer conservative lower bounds on undisclosed LLM parameter counts from next-token prediction accuracy on widely memorized texts. Provides a way to estimate hidden model sizes from outputs alone.

entry.title: PEARL: Training Socratic Tutors with Pedagogically Aligned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qikai Chang, Zhenrong Zhang, Linbo Chen, Pengfei Hu, Jianshu Zhang, Youhui Guo, Jun Du

entry.summary: PEARL trains Socratic tutoring LLM agents via pedagogically aligned RL, featuring a controllable student simulator decoupling cognitive states, pedagogical reward modeling, and multi-objective optimization. Targets effective multi-turn educational tutoring.

entry.title: The Interplay Between Interpolation and Aggregation in Regression: Optimal Sample Complexity

author.name: Mikael M{\o}ller H{\o}gsgaard, Kasper Green Larsen, Liang-Yu Zou

entry.summary: Theoretically characterizes the interplay between interpolation and aggregation in regression, showing the gamma-graph dimension governs learnability and that a simple median of three interpolators is optimal and stronger than proper learning. Advances regression learning theory.

entry.title: Real-Time Retargeting Using Controllability Boundary for Chandrayaan-3 Lunar Landing

author.name: Suraj Kumar, Debjyoti Chakrabarti, Aditya Rallapalli, Bharat Kumar GVP, Ashok Kumar Kakula

entry.summary: This paper presents the real-time retargeting guidance policy used in India's Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing, leveraging a convex representation of the controllability boundary for rapid feasibility checks and safe site updates. It claims the first application of a data-driven retargeting framework in an operational lunar landing.

entry.title: Joint Model and Data Sparsification via the Marginal Likelihood

author.name: Alexander Timans, Thomas M\"ollenhoff, Christian A. Naesseth, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: This paper extends Sparse Bayesian Learning to jointly learn feature and sample relevancies, enabling simultaneous model and data sparsification through a single marginal-likelihood objective. The symmetric pruning makes ARD robust to outliers and misspecified noise while preserving conjugacy and closed-form updates.

entry.title: SGMD: Score Gradient Matching Distillation for Few-Step Video Diffusion Distillation

author.name: Zhuguanyu Wu, Ruihao Gong, Yang Yong, Yushi Huang, Xiangyu Fan, Lei Yang, Dahua Lin, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: SGMD is a score-gradient-matching distillation method for few-step video diffusion that optimizes the fake score directly toward the teacher using a teacher stop-gradient Fisher objective. It addresses the costly fake-score tracking and mode-seeking conservatism of DMD-style video distillation that harms motion dynamics.

entry.title: UNIQUE: Universal Top-k Sparse Attention for Training-free Inference and Sparsity-aware Training

author.name: Keqi Deng, Shaoshi Ling, Ruchao Fan, Jinyu Li

entry.summary: UNIQUE is a universal top-k sparse attention framework for long-context inference that estimates KV-page importance using mean-of-keys plus standard-deviation offset, working for both training-free and sparsity-aware training. It stays effective across LLM modalities.

entry.title: GeneralThinker: Domain-General Reasoning through Likelihood-Guided Answer-Conditioned Optimization

author.name: Shengmin Piao, Sanghyun Park

entry.summary: GeneralThinker is an on-policy framework that reformulates reasoning supervision as dense answer-conditioned optimization, using ground-truth answer likelihood for response-level evaluation and token-level credit assignment without domain-specific verifiers. It generalizes RLVR beyond verifiable domains.

entry.title: Mask the Target: A Plug-and-Play Regularizer Against LoRA Forgetting

author.name: Runze Xu, Arpit Garg, Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Identifies that LoRA fine-tuning can degrade prior pretrained and aligned capabilities, especially under large distribution shift, and proposes a plug-and-play target-masking regularizer to mitigate this forgetting. It works without access to original training data.

entry.title: PhAIL: A Real-Robot VLA Benchmark and Distributional Methodology

author.name: Sergey Arkhangelskiy

entry.summary: PhAIL introduces an open real-robot benchmark on a Franka FR3 with a distributional evaluation methodology using time-to-success cumulative distributions, human-relative throughput scoring, and bootstrap confidence intervals. It addresses the statistical unreliability of small-sample binary success-rate VLA evaluation.

entry.title: ReasonOps: Operator Segmentation for LLM Reasoning Traces

author.name: Daniel Lee, Owen Queen, James Zou

entry.summary: Introduces ReasonOps, an unsupervised method for segmenting and annotating chain-of-thought traces, analyzing 44,662 traces from 12 thinking LLMs and finding seven recurring universal reasoning operators. It provides a shared vocabulary for the internal structure of long reasoning traces.

entry.title: Rethinking Literature Search Evaluation: Deep Research Helps, and Human Citation Lists Are Not a Ground Truth

author.name: Gaurav Sahu, Laurent Charlin, Christopher Pal

entry.summary: Builds a Deep Research literature-search pipeline that expands results breadth-first along bibliographies, raising recall on a 250-paper benchmark from under 20 percent to over 80 percent, and argues human citation lists are an unreliable ground truth. It uses an LLM-as-judge to show only 51 percent of human citations are at least moderately relevant.

entry.title: The Curse of Helpfulness: Inverse Scaling Law in Robustness to Distractor Instructions via DistractionIF

author.name: Zeli Su, Zhankai Xu, Tianlei Chen, Longfei Zheng, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces DistractionIF, a benchmark showing an inverse scaling phenomenon where larger LLMs are less robust to benign instruction-like distractor text in reference material, dropping up to 30 points. It mechanistically links this curse of helpfulness to perplexity-based attention to instruction-like noise.

entry.title: MINDGAMES: A Live Arena for Evaluating Social and Strategic Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLMs

author.name: Kevin Wang, Anna Th\"oni, Benjamin Kempinski, Bobby Cheng, Jianzhu Yao, Benjamin Finch, Leon Guertler, Viraj Nadkarni, Yihan Jiang, Aliaksei Korshuk, Alexander Buyantuev, Ilya Makarov, Siyuan Wu, Yu-Chi Cheng, Yan-Ru Ju, Ti-Rong Wu, I-Hsuan Chu, Yu-Yu Yang, I-Chen Wu, Yitian Huang, Qinlu Cao, Yiheng Sun, Yuhong Dai, Hongkun Yao, Jingxuan Fu, Jiwei Zhang, Hao Liao, Mossimo Ebeling, Govind Arun, Sadhvik Bathini, Mihir S Arya, Avinash Anish, Aditya Ranjan, Kirtana Sunil Phatnani, Paval KS, Vrushali Mehta, Aravind S, Nikhil Arora, Tanya Upadhyay, Amol Bandagale, Yuan Lu, ChunEn Hsiao, YuTing Lin, Arvin Chung, Jerry John Thomas, Mathieu Lauri\`ere, Leshem Choshen, Yoram Bachrach, Pramod Viswanath, Maria Polukarov, Cheston Tan, Tal Kachman, Atlas Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MINDGAMES, a live multi-game arena evaluating LLMs on social and strategic reasoning including belief attribution, opponent modeling, cooperative inference, and sustained deception. Built on TextArena, it captures sustained multi-agent reasoning that static benchmarks miss.

entry.title: Reliable Reasoning with Large Language Models via Preference-Based Maximum Satisfiability

author.name: Pedro Orvalho, Marta Kwiatkowska, Guillem Aleny\`a, Felip Many\`a

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid approach where LLMs externalize reasoning by generating Python code encoding constraints and preferences as a MaxSAT problem solved by an exact solver, with independent verification of feasibility and optimality. It targets reliable constrained optimization in domains like robotics where LLMs typically struggle.

entry.title: Croissant Tasks: A Metadata Format for Reproducible Machine Learning Evaluations

author.name: Omar Benjelloun, Leonardo Martins Bianco, Isabelle Guyon, Thanh Gia Hieu Khuong, Jonathan Lebensold, Sebastian Lobentanzer, Luis Oala, Benedictus Kent Rachmat, Ihsan Ullah, Peyman Vahidi, Joaquin Vanschoren

entry.summary: Croissant Tasks introduces a declarative, machine-actionable metadata format that abstracts low-level implementation details into high-level specifications, enabling conceptual reproducibility verified via agent-generated implementations rather than brittle code replication. It addresses ML reproducibility at scale.

entry.title: MuPHI: Learning Implicit Multimodal Harm Reasoning via Semantically Grounded Reward Optimization

author.name: Anisha Saha, Varsha Suresh, Teodora Kamova, Sophia Wiedmann, Timothy Hospedales, Vera Demberg

entry.summary: MuPHI introduces a dataset for multimodal pragmatic harm interpretation where harm emerges from benign image-text pairs requiring intent-aware cross-modal reasoning, with annotated rationales, plus MuPHIRM, a semantically grounded reward optimization method to improve VLM harm detection and reasoning. It targets implicit context-dependent harm that VLMs miss.

entry.title: Robust and Generalizable Safety Steering for Text-to-Image Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Zihao Xue, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Long Ma, Zhonglong Zheng, Zeyu Yang, Bingyu Zhu, Longtao Huang, Jie Xiao, Jungang Lou

entry.summary: SafeDIG is a safety steering framework for text-to-image diffusion transformers that formulates safety adaptation as position-aware sparse feature transfer using sparse autoencoders, addressing how harmful semantics progressively bind from text to visual latents. It targets robust and transferable steering across shifted risk domains.

entry.title: VLA-Trace: Diagnosing Vision-Language-Action Models through Representation and Behavior Tracing

author.name: Haoyuan Shi, Xiancong Ren, Yingji Zhang, Qinfan Zhang, Jiayu Hu, Haozhe Shan, Han Dong, Jinpeng Lu, Yinda Chen, Yi Zhang, Yong Dai, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: VLA-Trace is a progressive diagnostic framework for vision-language-action models combining centered kernel alignment for representation tracing, attention knockout for control attribution, and behavioral probes, applied to pi-0.5 and OpenVLA. It reveals how the two models differ in turning multimodal knowledge into embodied control.

entry.title: BioRefusalAudit: Auditing Biosecurity Refusal Depth Using General and Domain-Fine-Tuned Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Caleb DeLeeuw

entry.summary: BioRefusalAudit asks not whether models produce hazardous output but whether their refusals are structurally sound, using sparse autoencoders to audit biosecurity refusal depth across five architectures. It finds refusals collapse under modest prompt-framing, formatting, or output-length changes, with several models over- or under-refusing.

entry.title: When Should Models Change Their Minds? Contextual Belief Management in Large Language Models

author.name: Haoming Xu, Weihong Xu, Zongrui Li, Mengru Wang, Yunzhi Yao, Chiyu Wu, Jin Shang, Yu Gong, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: This work studies Contextual Belief Management, maintaining a predicted belief state aligned with evidence while isolating noise in long-horizon interactions, and introduces BeliefTrack, a closed-world benchmark with symbolic verifiers enabling exact turn-level evaluation of Failed Stay, Failed Update, and Failed Isolation. It finds vanilla LLMs exhibit severe belief-management failures.

entry.title: Thoughts-as-Planning: Latent World Models for Chain-of-Thoughts Optimization via Reinforcement Planning

author.name: Dong Liu, Yanxuan Yu, Ying Nian Wu

entry.summary: Thoughts-as-Planning frames reasoning chain optimization as sequential decision-making over a latent semantic space, learning a latent world model that simulates effects of chain edits. It aims for more interpretable and sample-efficient reasoning tuning than gradient-free search.

entry.title: FormInv: A Measurement Protocol for Semantic Invariance in Mathematical Reasoning Benchmarks

author.name: Nishal Thomas, Noel Thomas

entry.summary: FormInv audits paraphrase quality in math reasoning benchmarks, finding semantically incorrect paraphrases in MathCheck that flip model rankings, detectable cheaply via cross-model unanimity. It reveals that high-accuracy models can answer half of semantically equivalent restatements differently.

entry.title: Real-rootedness of the Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{0,n}$: an AI-assisted proof

author.name: Gergely B\'erczi, Young-Hoon Kiem

entry.summary: An AI-assisted proof of real-rootedness for the Poincare polynomials of the Deligne-Mumford moduli space, proving a conjecture of Aluffi-Chen-Marcolli. The key idea is a bivariate deformation revealing a hidden interlacing structure with a Sturm-Rolle argument.

entry.title: Compute Allocation in Evolutionary Search: From Depth-Breadth to Multi-Armed Bandits

author.name: Sixue Xing, Haoyu He, Kerui Wu, Zhuo Yang, Haozheng Luo, Tianfan Fu, Aarthy Nagarajan

entry.summary: This work studies how to allocate a fixed LLM-call budget in evolutionary search, identifying a fitness-compute envelope and a bilinear depth-breadth fit. It proposes BaSE, a bandit-based self-evolving allocation method, and documents the under-reported run-to-run variance of Evolve systems.

entry.title: Composing Non-Conjugate Factor Graphs with Closed-Form Variational Inference

author.name: Mykola Lukashchuk, Kyrylo Yemets, Wouter M. Kouw, Dmitry Bagaev, \.Ismail \c{S}en\"oz, Jeff Beck, Bert de Vries

entry.summary: Identifies five factor-graph primitives and proves any model composed from them admits closed-form variational message passing, preserving tractable inference in deeper probabilistic architectures. This enables non-conjugate compositions while keeping message families closed.

entry.title: Brain-IT-VQA: From Brain Signals to Answers

author.name: Roman Beliy, Matias Cosarinsky, Oliver Heinimann, Navve Wasserman, Michal Irani

entry.summary: Presents Brain-IT-VQA, a framework that decodes language tokens from fMRI brain activity and integrates them with a language model to answer questions about viewed images. It also uses the model to probe the structure of visual representations in the brain.

entry.title: EviLink: Multi-Path Schema Linking with Uncertainty-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Large-Scale Text-to-SQL

author.name: Huawei Zheng, Sen Yang, Zhaorui Yang, Yuhui Zhang, Haozhe Feng, Haoxuan Li, Xuan Yi, Chao Hu, Defeng Xie, Chen Hou, Danqing Huang, Wei Chen, Yingcai Wu, Peng Chen, Dazhen Deng

entry.summary: Proposes OccamToken, a training-free, budget-adaptive visual token pruning method for VLMs that replaces fixed top-K absolute ranking with register-anchored relative evidence testing. It addresses attention-sink distortion and input-dependent variability in token budgets.

entry.title: Multi-Legal-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Legal Reasoning Across Jurisdictions, Languages, and Legal Traditions

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Legal-Bench, a cross-jurisdictional legal benchmark spanning six countries, four language families, and 134 million court decisions with five identical tasks mapped to national court registries. It enables true cross-lingual legal reasoning comparison across legal traditions.

entry.title: ESPO: Early-Stopping Proximal Policy Optimization

author.name: Zihang Li, Rui Zhou, Yingcheng Shi, Wenhan Yu, Zhewen Tan, Zixiang Liu, Zeming Li, Binhua Li, Yongbin Li, Tong Yang, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Proposes ESPO, an early-stopping variant of PPO for LLM RL that detects trajectory failure on-the-fly using a surrogate regret from existing logits and terminates failing rollouts early. It avoids wasting compute on post-failure tokens and reduces advantage-estimate pollution.

entry.title: LaRA: Layer-wise Representation Analysis for Detecting Data Contamination in RL Post-Training

author.name: Minju Gwak, Minseo Kwak, Dongseok Lee, Guijin Son, Alan Ritter, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes LaRA, a layer-wise representation analysis framework to detect data contamination in RL post-trained LLMs, arguing output-level signals like likelihood become unreliable after RL. It uses three complementary metrics measuring perturbation sensitivity and directional consistency.

entry.title: Agora: Toward Autonomous Bug Detection in Production-Level Consensus Protocols with LLM Agents

author.name: Xiang Liu, Sa Song, Zhaowei Zhang, Huiying Lan, Jason Zeng, Ming Wu, Michael Heinrich, Yong Sun, Ceyao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents Agora, a domain-aware multi-agent framework integrating hypothesis-driven testing with LLMs to autonomously detect deep protocol-level logic bugs in production consensus protocols. Specialized agents explore state spaces, synthesize attack scenarios, and validate findings iteratively.

entry.title: Label Over Logic? How Source Cues Bias Human Fallacy Judgments More Than LLMs

author.name: Mahjabin Nahar, Nafis Irtiza Tripto, Aiping Xiong, Ting-Hao `Kenneth' Huang, Dongwon Lee

entry.summary: An online study (N=505) showing that source labels (human vs AI vs assisted) bias human fallacy judgments more than they bias LLMs, which evaluate reasoning more source-agnostically. It uses logical fallacies to isolate source-label effects from domain knowledge.

entry.title: Alignment-Guided Score Matching for Text-to-Image Alignment in Diffusion Models

author.name: Jaa-Yeon Lee, Yeobin Hong, Taesung Kwon, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Introduces alignment-guided score matching to improve text-image alignment within diffusion models without external rewards, fixing failure modes like over-counting and repetition seen in contrastive approaches. Targets alignment inside the diffusion process itself.

entry.title: When Cloud Agents Meet Device Agents: Lessons from Hybrid Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Corrado Rainone, Davide Belli, Bence Major, Arash Behboodi

entry.summary: Studies hybrid multi-agent systems combining cloud frontier LLMs with on-device small models, mapping the coupled trade-offs between accuracy, monetary cost, and edge energy. Extracts lessons and design principles for the under-explored hybrid design space.

entry.title: Overcoming Forgetting in LLM Fine-Tuning with Evolution Strategies

author.name: Kajetan Schweighofer, Conor F. Hayes, Roberto Dailey, Risto Miikkulainen, Xin Qiu

entry.summary: Shows that catastrophic forgetting during evolution-strategies LLM fine-tuning is better described as recoverable performance drift than irreversible forgetting, and that it also occurs with RL fine-tuning. Analyzes when and why the drift arises.

entry.title: Unifying Temporal and Structural Credit Assignment in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Prompt Optimization

author.name: Wenwu Li, Yuran Song, Mingze Zhao, Bo Jin, Wenhao Li

entry.summary: Introduces temporal and structural credit assignment for optimizing LLM-based multi-agent systems, decomposing trajectory-level failure into temporal routing and structural component credit. Aims to enable more efficient, lower-variance prompt optimization.

entry.title: PhyGenHOI: Physically-Aware 4D Generation of Dynamic Human-Object Interactions

author.name: Omer Benishu, Gal Fiebelman, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: Presents PhyGenHOI for physically-accurate 4D human-object interaction generation, coupling a motion diffusion model for the human with material-point-method physical simulation of the object using 3D Gaussian splats. Generates dynamic interactions like punching or kicking from text.

entry.title: Loong: A Human-Like Long Document Translation Agent with Observe-and-Act Adaptive Context Selection

author.name: Yutong Wang, Xuebo Liu, Derek F. Wong, Zhilin Li, Rongqing Jiang, Min Zhang, Shimin Tao, Daimeng Wei, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Loong, a long-document translation agent with a three-part memory module storing summaries, sentence pairs, and entity records, using RL-optimized adaptive context selection. Addresses limited context windows and redundant-context degradation in document translation.

entry.title: MedCase-Structured: A Text-to-FHIR Dataset for Benchmarking Diagnostic Reasoning in Clinically Realistic EHR Settings

author.name: Valentina Bui Muti, Eug\'enie Dulout, Ziquan Fu

entry.summary: Introduces MedCase-Structured, a text-to-FHIR pipeline and benchmark generating clinically realistic HL7 FHIR R4 bundles to evaluate LLM diagnostic reasoning in interoperable EHR-congruent settings. Uses terminology-grounded validation to reduce hallucinated codes.

entry.title: Towards Continuous-time Causal Foundation Models

author.name: Dennis Thumm, Ruben Wiedemann, Ying Chen

entry.summary: Extends discrete-time causal prior-data-fitted networks to continuous time, proposing a trajectory-law-invariance continuity criterion and a three-tier taxonomy for SDE-based causal foundation models. Constructs a top-tier model on random DAGs with irregular observation schedules.

entry.title: Spectral Guidance for Flexible and Efficient Control of Diffusion Models

author.name: Gabriel Moreira, Manuel Marques, Jo\~ao Paulo Costeira, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces Spectral Guidance, controlling diffusion models by learning singular functions of a conditional expectation operator that capture the few informative features under noise, then projecting arbitrary guidance signals onto sampling trajectories. Enables stable control without retraining or denoiser backpropagation.

entry.title: Optimal Gap-Dependent Regret for Private Stochastic Decision-Theoretic Online Learning

author.name: Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni

entry.summary: Resolves a COLT open problem by deriving optimal gap-dependent regret bounds for stochastic decision-theoretic online learning under pure event-level differential privacy, providing a horizon-free algorithm. Theoretical contribution to private online learning.

entry.title: Auditing Training Data in Generative Music Models via Black-Box Membership Inference

author.name: Yi Chen Liu, Jiawei Yu, Kexin Cao, Syed Irfan Ali Meerza, Trishika Movva, Jian Liu

entry.summary: Investigates black-box membership inference for generative music models, leveraging stronger semantic/structural alignment of training samples with model generations to detect training set membership. Relevant for music data provenance and consent auditing.

entry.title: On-Policy Replay for Continual Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yan Chen, Taojie Zhu, Meng Zhang, Xin Chen, Jiaqi Huang, Dongyang Xu, Yizhi Wang

entry.summary: On-Policy Replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in continual SFT by rolling out the recent checkpoint on a small budget of historical data and replaying these on-policy outputs, avoiding extra training objectives. Simplifies on-policy continual learning.

entry.title: Convex Basins in Single-Index Model Loss Landscapes: Applications to Robust Recovery under Strong Adversarial Corruption

author.name: Santanu Das, Sagnik Chatterjee, Jatin Batra

entry.summary: Provides the first near-linear-time robust recovery algorithm for Gaussian single-index models with generic asymmetric non-monotonic link functions (e.g., GeLU, Swish) under adversarial corruption. Extends robust learning theory to modern activation primitives.

entry.title: On the Construction and Implications of Low-Loss Valleys in LoRA-based Bayesian Inference

author.name: Daniel Dold, Emanuel Sommer, Julius Kobialka, Oliver D\"urr, David R\"ugamer

entry.summary: Introduces LoRA-Curve to study whether continuous low-loss valleys exist in LoRA fine-tuning space and whether they yield functional diversity for Bayesian model averaging, challenging claims that ensembling offers little benefit in LoRA. Advances uncertainty quantification in PEFT.

entry.title: Cluster-Level Attention-Guided Parallel Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Heqiang Qi, Wei Huang, Mingyuan Bai, Xiangming Meng

entry.summary: Proposes cluster-level attention-guided parallel decoding (CLAD) for masked diffusion language models, grouping high-confidence spans and using self-attention to select compatible clusters for parallel commitment. Improves decoding granularity beyond single tokens.

entry.title: Bastion: Budget-Aware Speculative Decoding with Tree-structured Block Diffusion Drafting

author.name: Soowon Oh, Nam Cao, Yujin Kim, Hojung Jung, Huzama Ahmad, Sangmin Bae, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: BASTION is a budget-aware speculative decoding framework using tree-structured block-diffusion drafting that dynamically builds query-dependent trees balancing draft quality and hardware constraints. Improves speculative decoding acceptance and efficiency.

entry.title: CLUBench: A Clustering Benchmark

author.name: Feng Xiao, Dazhi Fu, Chris Ding, Jicong Fan

entry.summary: CLUBench is a large-scale clustering benchmark spanning 24 algorithms (classical, deep, foundation-model-based) on 131 datasets across tabular, text, and image data with 178,815 experiments, analyzing hyperparameter and data-type effects. Provides comprehensive guidance on clustering algorithm selection.

entry.title: Learning to Extrapolate to New Tasks: A Relational Approach to Task Extrapolation

author.name: Adam Ousherovitch, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes the Relational Task Extrapolator, which learns transformations between tasks during training and applies them to relate known tasks to unseen ones, enabling systematic extrapolation beyond the training distribution's support. Addresses a fundamental interpolation-versus-extrapolation gap.

entry.title: Faithful Embeddings of Irregular and Asynchronous Data for Online Log-NCDEs

author.name: Benjamin Walker, Alexandre Bloch, Lingyi Yang, Sam Morley, Terry Lyons

entry.summary: Shows that interpolation/imputation-based embeddings for irregular asynchronous data are unnecessary, proving compact-set universality transfers from input to data space when the embedding is continuous and injective, and introduces such an embedding for online Log-NCDEs. Improves continuous-time modeling of irregular time series.

entry.title: Anti Mode-Collapse in Mean-Field Transformer via Auxiliary Variables

author.name: Masaaki Imaizumi, Masanori Koyama, Noboru Isobe, Kohei Hayashi

entry.summary: This paper uses mean-field transformer theory to analyze how auxiliary variables like positional encoding prevent self-attention mode collapse, where token distributions degenerate over many layers. It demonstrates theoretically that such auxiliary variables resolve the discrepancy between idealized analysis and real transformer behavior.

entry.title: Neural Scaling Laws for Jet Generation

author.name: Oz Amram, Darius A. Faroughy, Tjarko Gerdes, Anna Hallin, Gregor Kasieczka, Michael Kr\"amer, Humberto Reyes-Gonzalez, David Shih

entry.summary: This paper explores whether neural scaling laws apply to particle jet generation, finding the expected logarithmic model-size scaling behavior for this physics simulation task. It is the first to study scaling laws for jet generation, relevant to foundation models and in-situ simulation in high-energy physics.

entry.title: Kronecker Embeddings: Byte-Level Structured Token Representations for Parameter-Efficient Language Models

author.name: Rohan Shravan

entry.summary: Kronecker Embeddings replace the large learned token embedding table with a deterministic byte-level character-position factorization plus a single learned projection, eliminating 91-94% of input-side trainable parameters at frontier scale. The method is compatible with standard BPE tokenizers and avoids typographic clustering artifacts.

entry.title: Instance-dependent Stochastic Lipschitz bandit

author.name: Marius Potfer, Vianney Perchet

entry.summary: This paper provides an instance-dependent analysis of stochastic Lipschitz bandits, characterizing regret through integrals of the suboptimality gap over level sets, refining prior worst-case and zooming-dimension bounds. It gives a matching algorithm capturing finer structural properties of the reward function.

entry.title: Cert-LAS: Toward Certified Model Ownership Verification for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models via Layer-Adaptive Smoothing

author.name: Leyi Qi, Yiming Li, Siyuan Liang, Zhengzhong Tu, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Cert-LAS proposes the first certified model ownership verification for text-to-image diffusion models via layer-adaptive smoothing, robust to adversaries that intentionally damage watermark signals. It moves beyond the unrealistic faithful-verification assumption of existing backdoor-based watermarking.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Diffusion-based Reinforcement Learning with Critic Guidance

author.name: Shutong Ding, Zejia Zhong, Zhongyi Wang, Ke Hu, Bikang Pan, Jingya Wang, Ye Shi

entry.summary: CGPO is a critic-guided diffusion policy optimization method for sample-efficient reinforcement learning that combines the exploration of sampling-based methods with the exploitation of gradient-based Q-value information. It aims to avoid both slow convergence and unimodal policy collapse.

entry.title: GRASP: Plan-Guided Graph Retrieval with Adaptive Fusion and Reranking on Semi-Structured Knowledge Bases

author.name: Yicheng Tao, Yiqun Wang, Xiangchen Song, Xin Luo, Kai Liu, Jie Liu

entry.summary: GRASP is a three-stage retrieval framework for semi-structured knowledge bases combining plan-based graph retrieval, plan-conditioned fusion, and reranking. It substantially improves Hit@1 across STaRK benchmarks, lifting average from 62.0 to 73.9.

entry.title: Leave a Window Out: Modifying the Jackknife for Predictive Inference in Time Series

author.name: Hanyang Jiang, Rina Foygel Barber, Ashwin Pananjady, Yao Xie

entry.summary: The paper modifies the jackknife for predictive inference in time series by leaving out windows rather than single points, addressing temporal dependence that violates exchangeability assumptions in conformal prediction. It aims to retain accuracy while providing valid uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: ReverseMath: Answer Inversion for Scalable and Verifiable Mathematical Problem Generation

author.name: Raoyuan Zhao, Yihong Liu, Yupei Du, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: ReverseMath generates new verifiable math problems via answer inversion: masking a numerical value and rewriting so the masked value becomes the new known answer. This scalably produces fresh problems to separate genuine reasoning from memorization.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Neglect: Steering via Context-Preference for MLLM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Jingwen Wu, Xijun Zhang, Ge Song

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that MLLM object hallucinations stem from visual neglect, showing that increasing visual reliance can worsen hallucinations on some models. It proposes a training-free Context-Preference framework treating the image as competing context against parametric and textual knowledge.

entry.title: Where Does Toxicity Live? Mechanistic Localization and Targeted Suppression in Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Beniwal, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: Meow2X and TRNE are retraining-free frameworks that localize toxicity to specific layers and neurons via activation differentials between toxic and neutral prompts, then suppress them through inference-time scaling or rank-one weight edits. Evaluations across five LMs and two benchmarks show consistent toxicity reduction while preserving quality.

entry.title: MemGuard: Preventing Memory Contamination in Long-Term Memory-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Hyeonjeong Ha, Jeonghwan Kim, Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, William M. Campbell, Yue Wu, Yuji Zhang, Kathleen McKeown, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Heng Ji

entry.summary: MemGuard is a type-aware memory framework that prevents heterogeneous memory contamination in long-term memory-augmented LLMs, where stable facts, episodic events, and behavioral rules collapse into a shared space and become interchangeable. It preserves functional memory boundaries during construction and retrieval.

entry.title: Beyond pass@k: Redundancy-Aware RLVR for Multi-Sample Code Generation

author.name: Le Bronnec Florian, Alexandre Verine, Rio Yokota, Benjamin Negrevergne

entry.summary: This work studies implementation-level redundancy among sampled programs in Pass@k code generation using a plagiarism-detection tool, showing correctness-only RLVR concentrates generations around repeated implementations. Pass@k-aware objectives maintain lower redundancy and improve larger-budget performance.

entry.title: Extracting Small Translation Specialists from LLMs by Aggressively Pruning Experts

author.name: Liu O. Martin, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This work aggressively prunes experts from mixture-of-experts LLMs to extract small translation specialists, exploiting expert specialization and separability of multilingual capabilities. The modular pruning requires no retraining while incurring negligible translation quality loss.

entry.title: Soft-SVeRL: Self-Verified Reinforcement Learning with Soft Rewards

author.name: Saurabh Dash, Pierre Clavier, John Dang, Matthias Galle, Marzieh Fadaee, Ahmet \"Ust\"un, Beyza Ermis

entry.summary: Soft-RLVR extends reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards to partially verifiable tasks by converting prompts into checklists of atomic requirements scored item-by-item by an LLM verifier. This produces dense partial-credit soft rewards instead of sparse pass/fail signals.

entry.title: The Attentional White Bear Effect in Transformer Language Models

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: This paper studies whether instruction-based suppression actually reduces internal representation of prohibited concepts in transformer LMs, naming the phenomenon the attentional white bear effect. Using probing and attention analysis, it finds suppressed concepts remain highly recoverable, influence attention, and leak into generations despite lexical avoidance.

entry.title: Agent Explorative Policy Optimization for Multimodal Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Minki Kang, Shizhe Diao, Ryo Hachiuma, Sung Ju Hwang, Pavlo Molchanov, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang, Byung-Kwan Lee

entry.summary: AXPO addresses the Thinking-Acting Gap in multimodal agentic reasoning, where tool use is attempted on only ~30% of rollouts and is often all-wrong, suppressing learning signal. It proposes explorative policy optimization to better balance internal reasoning and high-variance tool use under RL.

entry.title: The Alignment Floor: How Persona Customization Breaks Safety in Weakly-Aligned LLMs

author.name: Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang, Yanwei Cui, Wei Qiu, Ziyuan Li, Bing Zhu, Peiyang He

entry.summary: This paper defines an alignment floor metric measuring the range of sycophancy rates a model exhibits across persona conditions, showing persona customization raises sycophancy in weakly-aligned models but not strongly-aligned ones. It treats sycophancy as a persona-conditional property and examines how much customization a model can absorb before truthfulness shifts.

entry.title: Self-Consistency via Marginal Sharpening

author.name: Aleksei Arzhantsev, Otmane Sakhi, Nicolas Chopin

entry.summary: Proposes shifting inference-time self-consistency from sharpening the full-output distribution to sharpening the answer marginal, making self-consistency an explicit objective with an efficient approximation. It argues answers supported by many reasoning paths should be favored. Matters for improving reasoning without training.

entry.title: AdaState: Self-Evolving Anchors for Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Yusuf Dalva, Pinar Yanardag

entry.summary: AdaState addresses the first-frame anchoring problem in autoregressive video diffusion, where the privileged initial frame in the attention cache suppresses dynamics and locks scene composition. It proposes self-evolving anchors to restore richer motion and scene progression in streaming generation.

entry.title: STAMP: Training Explicit Memory for Mobile GUI Agents in Controllable and Scalable Virtual Environments

author.name: Junyang Wang, Haiyang Xu, Xi Zhang, Zhaoqing Zhu, Ming Yan, Jieping Ye, Jitao Sang

entry.summary: STAMP trains explicit memory in mobile GUI agents using controllable, scalable virtual environments with deterministic memory variables, addressing failures on long-horizon tasks caused by limited context and token-heavy screenshots. It teaches agents what and when to memorize.

entry.title: DirectorBench: Diagnosing Long-Form Video Generation with Personalized Multi-Agent Evaluation

author.name: Jiamin Chen, Qianben Chen, Jiawen Zhang, Yidi Wu, Yuchen Li, Xiaokun Zhang, Wangchunshu Zhou, Chen Ma

entry.summary: DirectorBench is a personalized multi-agent diagnostic benchmark for long-form, multi-shot video generation evaluating script, visual, audio, and other dimensions across user profiles and checkpoint criteria. It moves beyond local visual quality to workflow-level and preference-aware diagnosis.

entry.title: ElegantVLA: Learning When to Think for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Ye Li, Huanan Liu, Kangye Ji, Yuan Meng, Jiajun Fan, Yuansong Wang, Shiyu Qin, Chenglei Wu, Shu-Tao Xia, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: ElegantVLA learns when vision-language-action models should invest full computation versus reuse cached reasoning, inspired by human motor control concentrating resources on goal-sensitive stages. It addresses the high computational cost and limited control frequency of VLAs.

entry.title: Gaze2Act: Gaze-Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Policies for Interactive Robot Manipulation

author.name: Kuangji Zuo, Gen Li, Bofan Lyu, Yanshuo Lu, Boyu Ma, Shijia Han, Xinyu Zhou, Xichen Yuan, Chuhao Zhou, Jiaqi Bai, Geng Li, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Gaze2Act uses human gaze as a dynamic intent signal for interactive robot manipulation, bridging the ego-exo view gap by mapping first-person gaze into the robot's perspective via cross-view semantic matching to produce object masks and gaze points. It addresses language's insufficiency for precise intent.

entry.title: Advice for making robust-to-training model organisms

author.name: SebastianP

entry.summary: Offers practical advice on robustly constructing model organisms for misalignment research, noting that common techniques produce fragile organisms that stop misbehaving after untargeted training like teaching pirate-speak. It identifies factors that make model organisms more robust to untargeted training.

entry.title: RAISE: RAG Design as an Architecture Search Problem

author.name: Zhen Chen, Yibing Liu, Weihao Xie, Yu Liang, Peilin Chen, Shiqi Wang

entry.summary: RAISE formulates RAG pipeline design as an architecture search problem and provides a comprehensive benchmark implementing 13 search algorithms across seven datasets under standardized search spaces and budgets. It addresses the heuristic, irreproducible nature of RAG configuration decisions.

entry.title: GEO-Bench: Benchmarking Ranking Manipulation in Generative Engine Optimization

author.name: Ojas Nimase, Zhe Chen, Gengpei Qi, Yue Zhao, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: GEO-Bench unifies evaluation of generative engine optimization (ranking manipulation) attacks under one protocol, covering black-box, white-box, and white-hat strategies across five datasets. It addresses fragmented evaluation as LLMs increasingly rank products and documents.

entry.title: Wait! There's a Way Out: A Decision Mechanism for Forecasting Conversational Derailment

author.name: Laerdon Kim, Vivian Nguyen, Cristian Danescu-Niculescu-Mizil

entry.summary: This work decouples the decision of when to trigger a derailment alert from the likelihood estimate, accounting for the possibility of future conversational recovery rather than assuming a fixed trajectory. It reduces false positives in forecasting conversational derailment into personal attacks.

entry.title: Code-QA-Bench: Separating Code Reasoning from Documentation Memorization in Repository-Level QA

author.name: Jun Zhang, JianYing Qu, Hanwen Du, Zhongkai Sun, Yehua Yang, Qiao Zhao

entry.summary: Code-QA-Bench synthesizes repository-level code QA benchmarks that separate genuine code comprehension from documentation recall and pretraining memorization. It uses an answer-first generation pipeline and a three-condition design (closed-book, code-only, documented) to quantify documentation utility and memorization.

entry.title: Neural Network Verification using Partial Multi-Neuron Relaxation

author.name: Ido Shmuel, Guy Katz

entry.summary: Proposes partial multi-neuron relaxation for formal neural network verification to better balance tightness and scalability compared to single- and full multi-neuron relaxations. Targets safety guarantees for deep networks in critical systems.

entry.title: When LLM Reward Design Fails: Diagnostic-Driven Refinement for Sparse Structured RL

author.name: Youting Wang, Yuan Tang, Bowen Liu, Xuan Liu, Dingyan Shang

entry.summary: Frames LLM-generated reward shaping for sparse structured RL as a debugging problem, identifying dominant failure modes like reward flooding and semantic misunderstanding and proposing diagnostic-driven iterative refinement. Reports large success-rate gains on MiniGrid tasks.

entry.title: FedQHD: Closed-Form Function-Space Federated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuchen Hou, Yongshan Chen, Zhuowen Zou, Calvin Yeung, Mohsen Imani, Tian Lan, Mahdi Imani

entry.summary: Introduces FedQHD, a federated Q-learning method using hyperdimensional random-feature state encoders with linear readout so Q-functions are nonlinear in state yet linear in parameters, enabling closed-form function-space-consistent aggregation. Addresses the function-space inconsistency of FedAvg-style averaging.

entry.title: AsymVLM: Asymmetric Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language Model Inference

author.name: Yilin Feng, Ahmed Burak Gulhan, Mahmut Taylan Kandemir

entry.summary: AsymVLM applies asymmetric token pruning to vision-language models, aggressively pruning spatially-redundant vision tokens before prefill while evicting text tokens only over budget, exploiting modality differences. Improves VLM inference efficiency.

entry.title: OVA-IB: One vs All Information Bottleneck for Multi-Modal Alignment

author.name: Tianchao Li, Shujian Yu, Xinrui Zu, Zhaolong Wei, Jeremy Gummeson, Jack C. P. Cheng, Robert Jenssen

entry.summary: OVA-IB applies a one-vs-all Information Bottleneck principle to arbitrary-modality alignment, providing a principled criterion for what each modality should preserve and compress relative to others, beyond pairwise CLIP-style losses. Advances multimodal contrastive alignment theory.

entry.title: Improving Adversarial Robustness of Attribution via Implicit Regularization

author.name: Amir Mehrpanah, Matteo Gamba, Hossein Azizpour

entry.summary: Shows attribution adversarial robustness can arise implicitly from standard SGD learning dynamics via parameter-input curvature connections, with negligible overhead, while proving such robustness often fails to transfer to softmax attention attribution due to entropy constraints. Advances reliable explainability.

entry.title: The Missing Piece in Pre-trained Model Evaluation: Reward-Guided Decoding Unlocks Task-Oriented Behavior Without Parameter Updates

author.name: Shaobo Wang, Guo Chen, Ziyue Wang, Zhengyang Tang, Qingyang Liu, Xingzhang Ren, Dayiheng Liu, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: The Missing Piece shows that reward-guided decoding can unlock task-oriented behavior from base pre-trained models without parameter updates, addressing how standard prompting conflates capability with decoding-induced failures. It proposes Energy-Based Decoding to reshape output distributions efficiently across open-ended tasks.

entry.title: Adopt $\neq$ Adapt: Longitudinal Analyses of LLM Conversations in the Wild

author.name: Rebecca M. M. Hicke, Kiran Tomlinson

entry.summary: Analyzes longitudinal conversational trajectories of about 12,000 Bing Copilot users alongside WildChat data, finding that population-level trends mask sticky individual habits and that highly active users have more successful, complex interactions. It distinguishes adoption from genuine behavioral adaptation.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Guardrails with Latent Reasoning

author.name: Siddharth Sai, Xiaofei Wen, Muhao Chen

entry.summary: Introduces COLAGUARD, a guardrail model that compresses multi-step safety reasoning into a continuous latent space via stage-wise training, enabling low-latency moderation without explicit reasoning tokens. It aims to match reasoning-based guardrails at classifier-like cost.

entry.title: Planning with the Views via Scene Self-Exploration

author.name: Kangrui Wang, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Shiqi Chen, Zihan Wang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Leonidas Guibas, Lijuan Wang, Manling Li

entry.summary: Studies view planning in VLMs via the ViewSuite environment on real ScanNet scenes, finding 13 frontier VLMs know single-action view effects but fail to compose them across multi-turn plans. It proposes an iterative self-exploration and view-graph distillation framework to close this gap.

entry.title: Beyond Trajectory Rewards: Step-level Credit Assignment for Agentic Search via Graph Modeling

author.name: Yuchen Liu, Yingjie Feng, Lixiong Qin, Jiasi Chen, Jianing Yu, Sheng Gao, Sheng Yang, Weiran Xu

entry.summary: This work introduces step-level credit assignment for agentic search via graph modeling, scoring retrieved entities by their distance to the answer node in a training-time entity-relation graph (GDCR) and converting these into step-level advantages (SAPO). It avoids costly tree sampling used by prior step-level reward methods.

entry.title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs

author.name: Jung Hyun Lee, June Yong Yang, Jungwook Choi, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: LFQ proposes logit-aware final-block quantization for low-bit LLMs, addressing degradation in generative and long chain-of-thought tasks by including the unembedding layer in block-wise optimization and replacing MSE with a distribution-alignment objective. It targets the gap between quantized and full-precision token distributions.

entry.title: Harnessing non-adversarial robustness in large language models

author.name: Qinghua Zhou, Ellina Aleshina, Andrey Lovyagin, Oleg Somov, Mikhail Seleznyov, Alexander Panchenko, Ivan Oseledets, Elena Tutubalina, Ivan Y. Tyukin

entry.summary: This work addresses LLM robustness to semantically-neutral prompt variations without full retraining, providing a theoretical analysis identifying a systematic perturbation-induced bias in module outputs and a corrective method motivated by it. It targets prompt-sensitivity that degrades task performance.

entry.title: OmniMatBench: A Human-Calibrated Multimodal Reasoning Benchmark Across 19 Materials Science Subfields

author.name: Wanhao Liu, Jiaqing Xie, Qian Tan, Weida Wang, Jue Wang, Ran Sun, Zhuo Yang, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Bai, Tianfan Fu, Lu Chen, Xin Chen, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: OmniMatBench is a human-calibrated multimodal reasoning benchmark for materials science with 3,171 expert-curated QA and calculation problems across 19 subfields, spanning the reasoning process from materials knowledge to application. It fills a gap where existing benchmarks focus only on property prediction or QA.

entry.title: Teaching Values to Machines: Simulating Human-Like Behavior in LLMs

author.name: Asaf Yehudai, Naama Rozen, Ariel Gera

entry.summary: This work draws on psychological value theory to induce human-like values in LLMs, conducting large-scale experiments (over 5 million questions) with validated questionnaires to assess value structures and value-behavior relationships versus humans. It finds strong agreement between value-prompted LLMs and humans.

entry.title: Meta-Cognitive Memory Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Ziyan Liu, Zhezheng Hao, Yeqiu Chen, Hong Wang, Jingren Hou, Ruiyi Ding, Yongkang Yang, Wence Ji, Wei Xia, Feng Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes meta-cognitive memory policy optimization for long-horizon LLM agents, arguing memory optimization should target the clarity of beliefs induced by intermediate summaries rather than only trajectory-level success. It addresses how ambiguous recursive summaries cause belief deviation that derails reasoning.

entry.title: ProjectionBench: Evaluating Scientific Hypothesis Generation in LLMs Under Progressive Information Disclosure

author.name: A. J. Lew (Unreasonable Labs), Y. Cao (Unreasonable Labs), M. J. Buehler (Unreasonable Labs)

entry.summary: ProjectionBench evaluates scientific hypothesis generation in LLMs under progressive information disclosure, where models initially receive only a topic and research question with technical details gradually revealed, building up to classical null hypothesis testing. It targets innovative reasoning for true scientific discovery rather than multi-hop retrieval.

entry.title: MIRA: Mid-training Rubric Anchoring for Source-Aware Data Selection

author.name: Haowen Wang, Yaxin Du, Jian Yang, Jiajun Wu, Shukai Liu, Yuxuan Zhang, Pingjie Wang, Siheng Chen, Tuney Zheng, Ming Zhou, Xianglong Liu

entry.summary: MIRA proposes mid-training rubric anchoring for source-aware data selection, providing scalable yet source-adaptive semantic criteria for the distinct mid-training data selection problem (pretraining-style objective at scale but curated toward downstream capabilities from heterogeneous sources). It bridges scalable model-based and stronger semantic selection methods.

entry.title: Micro-Macro Retrieval: Reducing Long-Form Hallucination in Large Language Models

author.name: Yujie Feng, Jian Li, Zhihan Zhou, Pengfei Xu, Yujia Zhang, Xiaoyu Li, Xiaohui Zhou, Alan Zhao, Xi Chen, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: Micro-Macro Retrieval (M2R) is a retrieve-while-generate framework that reduces long-form hallucination by ensuring key information stays close to model outputs, operating at a macro level for context structuring and a micro level for proximity. It exploits the finding that key information closer to outputs yields higher factual accuracy.

entry.title: S3Mem: Structured Spatiotemporal Scene-Event Memory for Long-Horizon Interactive Question Answering

author.name: Encheng Su, Jinouwen Zhang, Jianyu Wu, Qiucheng Yu, Chen Tang, Pengze Li, Lintao Wang, Yizhou Wang, Xinzhu Ma, Shixiang Tang, Aoran Wang

entry.summary: S3Mem is a structured scene-event episodic memory framework for long-horizon interactive QA that writes trajectories into structured memory units and retrieves via anchor-sensitive methods, arguing the bottleneck is the trajectory-to-answer interface rather than context length alone. It targets spatial, temporal, repeated-event, and multi-hop questions where plain-text RAG retrieves chain-incomplete evidence.

entry.title: SERC: LDPC-Inspired Semantic Error Correction for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Gyumin Kim, Juhwan Park, Jaeha Kim, Seunggyun Han, Kyungrak Son, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: SERC reframes LLM text generation as a noisy channel and applies LDPC (error-correcting code) principles to detect and mitigate hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation. The framework provides a theoretical lens for interpreting and correcting semantic errors without relying on flawed self-correction.

entry.title: Context Distillation as Latent Memory Management

author.name: Ziyang Zheng, Zeju Li, Xiangyu Wen, Jianyuan Zhong, Junhua Huang, Lei Chen, Mingxuan Yuan, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: This work formulates context distillation as a latent memory management problem, distilling each context into a separate LoRA adapter to form a retrievable modular memory bank with self-gating activation. Cache sharing reduces inference overhead.

entry.title: SCDBench: A Benchmark for LLM-Based Smart Contract Decompilers

author.name: Kaihua Qin, Dawn Song, Arthur Gervais

entry.summary: SCDBench is a dataset and benchmark for evaluating LLM-based smart contract decompilation, with 600 real Solidity contracts paired with bytecode, ground-truth source, and replayable semantic checkpoints. It uses cumulative semantic consistency checks beyond superficial plausibility.

entry.title: OISD: On-Policy Internal Self-Distillation of Language Models

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Darryl Cherian Jacob, Yang Zhou, Jindong Wang, Pan He

entry.summary: OISD introduces on-policy internal self-distillation, transferring predictive signals from the final layer to intermediate representations during GRPO RL training. The final layer acts as both policy and detached internal teacher, aligning intermediate layers via logit alignment.

entry.title: BlockBatch: Multi-Scale Consensus Decoding for Efficient Diffusion Language Model Inference

author.name: Xiaoyou Wu (Celine), Cheng-Jhih Shih (Celine), Binfei Ji (Celine), Yong Liu (Celine), Yingyan (Celine), Lin

entry.summary: BlockBatch uses block size as a branching dimension for diffusion language model inference, performing multi-scale consensus decoding across related KV-cache trajectories from different block sizes. It addresses the granularity trade-off where small blocks need many steps and large blocks make premature commitments.

entry.title: LoopFM: Learning frOm HistOrical RePresentations of Foundation Model for Recommendation

author.name: Shali Jiang, Hua Zheng, Boyang Liu, Laming Chen, Kenny Lov, Chuanqi Xu, Lisang Ding, Qinghai Zhou, Can Cui, Xiaolong Liu, Xiaoyi Liu, Yasmine Badr, Xin Xu, Jiyan Yang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Gerard Jonathan Mugisha Akkerhuis, Chenxiao Guan, Rong Jin, Ruichao Qiu, Xian Chen, Shifu Xu, Zhehui Zhou, Ping Chen, Rui Yang, Haicheng Chen, Xiangge Meng, Song Zhou, Dharak Kharod, Shuyu Xu, Qiang Jin, Qiao Yang, Wankun Zhu, Qin Huang, Yuzhen Huang, Darren Liu, Parish Aggarwal, Hui Zhou, Erzhuo Wang, Shuo Chang, Xiaorui Gan, Wenlin Chen, Santanu Kolay, Huayu Li

entry.summary: LoopFM opens a high-bandwidth knowledge transfer channel from large foundation models to compact vertical recommendation models by structuring FM intermediate embeddings as input features, avoiding real-time FM inference at serving. It addresses the diminishing transfer ratio of scalar knowledge distillation.

entry.title: Rethinking FID Through the Geometry of the Reference Dataset

author.name: Yunghee Lee, Byeonghyun Pak

entry.summary: This work shows that FID's mismatch with sample quality depends partly on the geometry (density and effective rank) of the reference dataset, with concentrated datasets yielding more favorable FID trends. It argues distributional metrics should be interpreted together with reference-set geometry.

entry.title: VLA-Pro: Cross-Task Procedural Memory Transfer for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shengyu Si, Yuanzhuo Lu, Ruimeng Yang, Ziyi Ye, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes VLA-Pro, a plug-and-play framework that stores task-specific LoRA adapters as parameterized procedural memories during training and retrieves/fuses them at inference for cross-task generalization in vision-language-action robot models. It aims to transfer experience across objects, scenes, and action patterns.

entry.title: Evolutionary Dynamics of Cooperation in Next-Generation LLM Agent Systems: A Cross-Provider Empirical Extension

author.name: Francisco Le\'on Z\'u\~niga Bol\'ivar (Instituci\'on Universitaria Colegio Mayor del Cauca)

entry.summary: Audits LLM safety across four expert-grounded caregiving support roles (Inform, Coach, Relate, Listen) versus baseline prompting, asking whether safety profiles shift with conversational role. It grounds evaluation in social support theory for informal caregiving contexts.

entry.title: Mitigating Hallucination in Vision-Language Models through Barrier-Regulated Adaptive Closed-form Steering

author.name: Soumyadeep Jana, Pulkit Mittal, Sanasam Ranbir Singh

entry.summary: Proposes BRACS, a training-free barrier-regulated adaptive closed-form steering method to mitigate object hallucination in vision-language models by monitoring the model's own attention to measure visual grounding. It intervenes adaptively only when grounding fails, with strength scaled to severity.

entry.title: HoliTok:A Coutinuous Holistic Tokenization with Robust Dual Capabilities of Speech Generation and Understanding

author.name: Bohan Li, Shi Lian, Hankun Wang, Yiwei Guo, Yu Xi, Zhihan Li, Da Zheng, Colin Zhang, Kai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes HoliTok, a continuous holistic speech tokenizer that encodes 48 kHz speech into a compact 25 Hz sequence of 128-dim latents, trained progressively to balance signal fidelity, semantics, and latent learnability for unified speech generation and understanding. It aims to simplify unified speech foundation model design.

entry.title: Give it Space! Explicit Disentangling of Positional and Semantic Representations in Encoders

author.name: Pierre-Antoine Lequeu, Camille Barboule, Benjamin Piwowarski

entry.summary: Modifies encoder transformers to process semantic, absolute positional, and relative positional information as explicitly disentangled streams, building on evidence these signals occupy orthogonal subspaces. Aims to improve understanding and design of positional encodings.

entry.title: On Distributional Reinforcement Learning in Chaotic Dynamical Systems

author.name: James Rudd-Jones, Mirco Musolesi, Mar\'ia P\'erez-Ortiz

entry.summary: Applies distributional reinforcement learning to chaotic dynamical systems, showing the return distribution evolves more regularly than individual trajectories under Wasserstein metrics despite exponential sensitivity. Aims to stabilize learning in chaotic domains.

entry.title: iLoRA: Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation with Latent Interaction Graphs for Microbiome Diagnosis

author.name: Yang Song, Yixuan Zhang, Lingfa Meng, Tongyuan Hu, Haizhou Shi, Hao Wang, Samir Bhatt, Hengguan Huang

entry.summary: Introduces iLoRA, described as the first Bayesian graph-conditioned LoRA framework, which infers a latent interaction graph from inputs to generate input-conditioned adapter updates. Demonstrated on microbiome diagnosis where microbe interactions drive labels.

entry.title: Molecular Lead Optimization via Agentic Tool Planning

author.name: Lingxiao Li, Haobo Zhang, Ruohao Fan, Bin Chen, Jiayu Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes TRACE, a trajectory-based agentic tool-planning approach for molecular lead optimization that accounts for long-term consequences of sequential design decisions rather than one-step optimization. Targets ADMET improvement while preserving binding substructures in drug discovery.

entry.title: Cycle-Space Informed Detection of Autoencoded Blind False Data Injection Attacks on Power Systems

author.name: Xin Li, Chenhan Xiao, Jonathan Cohen, Aviad Elyashar, Yang Weng, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: Demonstrates a blind false-data-injection attack on power systems where an autoencoder learns the measurement manifold and crafts perturbations aligned with the Jacobian null space to evade detectors, then proposes a cycle-space informed detection defense. Targets AI-driven data-center and storage-reliant grid security.

entry.title: Causal Intelligence for Constraint-Aware Intervention Design to Induce State Transitions

author.name: Zixuan Song, Uwe Mueller, Dimitris V. Manatakis

entry.summary: Presents COAST, a causal-intelligence framework for designing constrained interventions that induce user-defined state transitions by learning context-specific causal graphs and structural causal models. Introduces constraint-aware multi-objective optimization balancing efficacy and intervention cost.

entry.title: Moment Matching Q-Learning

author.name: Yiyan (Edgar), Liang, Sifei Liu, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Moment Matching Q-Learning, which uses maximum mean discrepancy to match all moment statistics between distributions, avoiding the slow iterative sampling of score- and flow-based generative models in RL. Aims to overcome inference-latency bottlenecks in distributional RL.

entry.title: Apertus LLM Family Expansion via Distillation and Quantization

author.name: Andrei Panferov, Davit Melikidze, Martin Jaggi, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Validates distillation and quantization as a cost-effective way to expand an open LLM family to smaller sizes and new hardware formats, producing distilled Apertus variants up to 4B trained on permissive-license tokens. Useful for practical deployment under hardware/budget constraints.

entry.title: Do Deep Networks Forget Initialization? A Forgetting-Time View of Practical Inductive Bias

author.name: Mohua Das, Pierfrancesco Beneventano, Shibshankar Dey, Gareth H. McKinkey, Tomaso Poggio

entry.summary: Introduces initialization memory to measure how much of a network's random-initialization bias survives training, showing on CIFAR-10/ResNets that low-LR SGD can interpolate while retaining strong initialization dependence. Sheds light on inductive bias and training regimes.

entry.title: Solving Integer Linear Programming with Parallel Tempering

author.name: Kyuil Sim, Sanghyeok Choi, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: Proposes a solver-free, sampling-based optimization framework for Integer Linear Programming using parallel tempering with locally-balanced proposals to explore discrete feasible regions without training or external solvers. Targets combinatorial optimization without solver dependence.

entry.title: A Full-Pipeline Framework for Evaluating Membership Inference Attacks in Machine Learning

author.name: Ding Chen, Xinwen Cheng, Xuyang Zhong, Xinping Chen, Xiaolin Huang, Chen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a full-pipeline evaluation framework characterizing membership inference attack efficacy across data, architecture, algorithm, and post-training stages. Helps practitioners assess privacy risk realistically rather than just on benchmarks.

entry.title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance

author.name: Eunbyeol Cho, Yunseung Lee, Mirae Kim, Jeewon Yang, Youngjun Kwak, Edward Choi

entry.summary: Introduces K-FinHallu, the first benchmark for hallucination detection in multi-turn Korean financial RAG, with a hierarchical taxonomy accounting for justified abstention. Addresses non-English, multi-turn, high-stakes hallucination evaluation.

entry.title: Open Problem: Separating Geometric and Algorithmic Compression via Cayley-Table Completion

author.name: Dongsung Huh

entry.summary: Proposes Cayley-table completion as a canonical testbed to separate geometric (continuous capacity) from algorithmic (discrete rule) compression, highlighting deep learning's missing inductive bias for algorithmic complexity minimization. An open-problem framing for extrapolation of algebraic rules.

entry.title: Plan, Don't Pose: Long Composite Motion Generation with Text-Aligned BFM

author.name: Nikolay Shvetsov, Maksim Bobrin, Nazar Buzun, Dmitry V. Dylov

entry.summary: Text2BFM aligns natural language with pretrained Behavioral Foundation Models for long composite text-to-motion generation, operating in the frozen BFM's latent policy space as an executable motion prior instead of heavy end-to-end generators. Decouples semantic interpretation from physical realization.

entry.title: Convergence Theory for Iterative LLM-Based Neural Architecture Search: A Parametric Cross-Entropy Framework with Closed-Form Proxy Reliability

author.name: Santosh Premi Adhikari, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: Develops a convergence theory for iterative LLM-based neural architecture search by modeling it as a parametric cross-entropy method over executable programs, proving monotone improvement, geometric convergence of elite-set probability, and advantages of delta-based generation. Provides formal grounding for LLM-driven NAS.

entry.title: MarginGate: Sparse Margin-Triggered Verification for Batch-Invariant LLM Inference

author.name: Kexin Chu, Yang Zhou, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: MarginGate addresses the surprising non-reproducibility of temperature-zero LLM inference where the same input yields different tokens depending on batch context. It observes that batch-induced token flips are sparse (0.3-1.3%) and detectable via low logit margins, enabling selective verification only on risky steps to reduce cost.

entry.title: Echoes within the Reasoning: Stealthy and Effective Watermarking via Chain of Thought

author.name: Jiacheng Lu, Yiming Li, Tao Song, Weijian Wang, Wenjie Qu, Haibing Guan, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: BiCoT is a watermarking framework that embeds ownership signals into the internal geometry of chain-of-thought reasoning traces by aligning structural anchors with a private signature subspace. It aims for stealthy, robust watermarking that preserves reasoning fidelity and resists removal.

entry.title: Wasserstein Contraction of Coordinate Ascent Variational Inference

author.name: Rocco Caprio, Adrien Corenflos, Sam Power

entry.summary: This work proves Wasserstein-distance contraction guarantees for coordinate ascent variational inference under transport-information inequalities and smoothness conditions. The results are general, sharp, and apply to Bayesian mixtures and high-dimensional regression.

entry.title: Resolution Diagnostics for Paired LLM Evaluation

author.name: Anany Kotawala

entry.summary: This work reframes paired LLM leaderboard comparisons as hypothesis tests and shows many displayed rankings are statistically unresolved at conventional power levels. It introduces a per-pair resolution ratio diagnostic to flag insufficiently powered comparisons.

entry.title: LCO: LLM-based Constraint Optimization for Safer Agentic LLMs in Real-world Tasks

author.name: Jiayong Wan, Jiawei Chen, Zhaoxia Yin, Liu Shuyuan, Hang Su

entry.summary: LCO is a fine-tuning-free framework to reduce in-context reward hacking in agentic LLMs, where models over-optimize proxy objectives and produce harmful side effects. It uses a self-thought module to proactively deliberate on safety constraints during environment interaction.

entry.title: Disentangling Language Roles in Multilingual LLM Task Execution

author.name: Qishi Zhan, Minxuan Hu, Seoyeon Jang, Lei Zhao, Ziheng Chen, Man Liang, Xinyue Xiang, Jiaxin Liu, Guansu Wang, Liang He

entry.summary: MTM-Bench is a controlled benchmark disentangling instruction, content, and response language roles in multilingual LLM task execution via a fully crossed triplet design across English, Spanish, and Chinese. It evaluates 20 frontier and open-weight LLMs on decomposed metrics.

entry.title: Chain-based Adaptive Reconfiguration Over Lattices for Hallucination Reduction

author.name: Joan Vendrell Gallart, Solmaz Kia, Russell Bent, Michael Grosskopf

entry.summary: CAROL is a probabilistic test-time hallucination-reduction framework defining semantic uncertainty via consistency with trusted context, formulated as a string-submodular objective over a lattice. It casts mitigation as a Markov chain accept-reject process with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: UserHarness: Harnessing User Minds for Stronger Agent Theory-of-Mind

author.name: Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, Heng Ji

entry.summary: UserHarness is a framework that improves agent Theory-of-Mind by explicitly reconstructing users' mental states, modeling beliefs updated through observations and nested beliefs. It directly addresses the belief-intention-action structure that prior indirect pipelines miss.

entry.title: Do Models Know Why They Changed Their Mind? Interpretability and Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Under Knowledge Conflict

author.name: Pruthvinath Jeripity Venkata

entry.summary: This paper introduces introspective faithfulness to test whether chain-of-thought reasoning faithfully reports a model's choice between trusting a document or its training knowledge under conflict. It finds CoT is highly stable across opposite decisions, with only faint genuine confidence signals.

entry.title: VibeSearchBench: Benchmarking Long-horizon Proactive Search in the Wild

author.name: Xiaohongshu Inc

entry.summary: VibeSearchBench benchmarks long-horizon proactive search where users and agents collaboratively refine vague intent through multi-turn dialogue, comprising 200 bilingual tasks across 20 domains with schema-free knowledge-graph ground truth. It targets the evaluation-experience gap of existing over-specified single-turn benchmarks.

entry.title: Let the Results Speak: A Replication-First Paradigm for LLM Behavioral Benchmarking
