author.name: Yuming (Rapheal), Huang, Yao Liu, Lei Wang, Junchen Wan

entry.summary: This work proposes a replication-first paradigm for subjective LLM behavioral benchmarking, certifying instruments via reliability across runs, cross-instrument replication across distinct judges, historical-footprint calibration, and pre-registration. It avoids circularity from anchoring on a single human-rater consensus.

entry.title: Semantic Flow Regularization: Teaching LLMs to Generate Diverse Yet Coherent Responses

author.name: Kerui Peng, Feifei Li, Xingyu Fan, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Semantic Flow Regularization addresses Cross-Style Collapse where persona/tone fine-tuning suppresses output diversity, tracing it to the cross-entropy objective. SFR adds a flow-matching auxiliary objective supervising the backbone with future-segment embeddings, preserving multi-modality at zero inference cost.

entry.title: Beyond Chunk-Local Extraction: Cross-Chunk Graph Augmentation for GraphRAG

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Yibo Zhao, Jing Yu, Jianxiang Yu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: CrossAug is a GNN-guided method that enriches GraphRAG indices with cross-chunk relational structure as an offline step, addressing the systematic absence of relations whose evidence spans multiple passages. It uses self-supervised graph corruption for training supervision, avoiding combinatorial LLM extraction.

entry.title: DEPART: DEcomposing PARiTy across Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Manan Uppadhyay, Prashant Kodali, Pranjal Chitale, Reshma Ramaprasad, Himanshu Beniwal, Sunayana Sitaram

entry.summary: DEPART introduces a Bayesian hierarchical framework to decompose multilingual LLM performance disparities into interpretable components, showing that observable language features explain most cross-language variance. It first establishes that gaps are systematic rather than sampling noise via distribution-free statistical tests.

entry.title: You Only Align Once: Propagating Cooperative Behaviors in Multi-Agent Systems through Seed Agents

author.name: Nicole Hsing, Asuka Yuxi Zheng, Yi Zhao, Haoqin Tu, Jen-Tse Huang

entry.summary: Demonstrates Alignment Propagation, where a single aligned seed agent spreads cooperative behavior to untrained agents purely via natural language in an iterated Prisoner's Dilemma game, doubling cooperation rates. It suggests scalable ways to align large open multi-agent populations. Matters for multi-agent alignment and emergent cooperation.

entry.title: The Importance of Being Statistically Earnest: A Critical Re-evaluation of GSM-Symbolic

author.name: Dominika Agnieszka D{\l}ugosz, Arlindo Oliveira, Natalia D\'iaz-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Critically re-evaluates the GSM-Symbolic benchmark using Generalized Linear Mixed Models, finding only half of 20 models show statistically significant performance drops and that the dataset has a confounding shifted distribution of larger integers. It challenges the conclusion that LLMs lack genuine reasoning. Matters for statistical rigor in reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: Extrapolative Weight Averaging Reveals Correctness-Efficiency Frontiers in Code RL

author.name: Kunhao Zheng, Pierre Chambon, Juliette Decugis, Jonas Gehring, Taco Cohen, Benjamin Negrevergne, Gabriel Synnaeve

entry.summary: Studies whether extrapolative weight averaging between fine-tuned checkpoints can extend the correctness-efficiency Pareto front to new inference-time models without extra RL training in competitive programming. It reveals a correctness-efficiency frontier emerging from nested unit-test coverage rewards. Matters for efficient model merging in code RL.

entry.title: D\'ej\`a View: Looping Transformers for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Alessandro Burzio, Tobias Fischer, Sven Elflein, Qunjie Zhou, Riccardo de Lutio, Jiawei Ren, Jiahui Huang, Shengyu Huang, Marc Pollefeys, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Zan Gojcic, Haithem Turki

entry.summary: DejaView applies a single looped transformer block recurrently to per-view features for multi-view 3D reconstruction, making the iteration implicit in deep transformers explicit in architecture. The loop count K becomes an inference-time compute knob trained once.

entry.title: minWM: A Full-Stack Open-Source Framework for Real-Time Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Min Zhao, Hongzhou Zhu, Bokai Yan, Zihan Zhou, Yimin Chen, Wenqiang Sun, Kaiwen Zheng, Guande He, Xiao Yang, Chongxuan Li, Fan Bao, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: minWM is a full-stack open-source framework converting bidirectional video foundation models into real-time, camera-controllable, few-step autoregressive interactive world models. It spans data construction, controllable fine-tuning, autoregressive training, distillation, and streaming inference.

entry.title: Uncertainty-driven 3D Gaussian Splatting Active Mapping via Anisotropic Visibility Field

author.name: Shangjie Xue, Jesse Dill, Dhruv Ahuja, Frank Dellaert, Panagiotis Tsiotras, Danfei Xu

entry.summary: Presents GAVIS, a method for uncertainty quantification and active mapping in 3D Gaussian Splatting using an anisotropic visibility field represented with spherical harmonics. It enables real-time 200 FPS uncertainty-aware rendering for guiding view exploration.

entry.title: EvoGM: Learning to Merge LLMs via Evolutionary Generative Optimization

author.name: Tao Jiang, Xinmeng Yu, Chenhao Yi, Yiling Wu, Yan Li, Ran Cheng, Dongmei Jiang, Jianguo Zhang

entry.summary: EvoGM replaces hand-crafted operators in evolutionary LLM model merging with a learnable dual-generator architecture using cycle-consistent learning and winner-loser pairs to optimize merging coefficients. It aims for training-free, automated composition of LLMs.

entry.title: The Open Motion Planning Library 2.0

author.name: Weihang Guo, Theodoros Tyrovouzis, Emiliano Flores, Clayton W. Ramsey, Zachary K. Kingston, Ioan A. \c{S}ucan, Mark Moll, Lydia E. Kavraki

entry.summary: Announces OMPL 2.0, a major update to the widely used Open Motion Planning Library adding hardware acceleration for real-time planning and integration with modern AI research workflows. It reflects on nearly two decades of the library's evolution.

entry.title: VE2VF: Vision-Enabled to Vision-Free Distillation via Real-world Reinforcement Learning for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Victor Kowalski, Chengxi Li, Dongheui Lee

entry.summary: VE2VF distills a vision-enabled teacher policy into a vision-free student relying only on pose, twist, and wrench sensing for robust contact-rich manipulation, trained entirely in the real world without domain randomization. It combines fast training with strong robustness.

entry.title: VLAConf: Calibrated Task-Success Confidence for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Dehao Huang, Aoxiang Gu, Chengjie Zhang, Bolin Zou, Wenlong Dong, Zilang Cen, Yue Wang, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: VLAConf provides calibrated task-success confidence estimation for vision-language-action models using a one-class discriminative approach that avoids repeated sampling and works for continuous action spaces. It improves efficiency and cross-architecture generalizability over ensemble methods.

entry.title: Do Models Lie More to Other Models?

author.name: keith_wynroe

entry.summary: Reports an initial experiment testing whether GPT-5 deceives an overseer more in agent-agent settings than human-agent settings, motivated by concerns that alignment training may not generalize to AI-AI interactions. It frames a potentially important alignment-generalization problem.

entry.title: Beyond Consensus: Trace-Level Synthesis in Mixture of Agents

author.name: Shreyas Fadnavis, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Felix Wyss

entry.summary: Shows that aggregating full LLM reasoning traces, rather than majority voting, recovers correct solutions even when agents unanimously agree, an effect termed the aggregation paradox. It introduces Self-Consistent Mixture of Agents leveraging trace-level complementarity.

entry.title: GTA: Generating Long-Horizon Tasks for Web Agents at Scale

author.name: Tenghao Huang, Kung-Hsiang Huang, Prafulla Kumar Choubey, Yilun Zhou, Muhao Chen, Jonathan May, Chien-Sheng Wu

entry.summary: Presents GTA, a scalable framework for automatically generating realistic long-horizon web-agent tasks with executable trajectories via crawling, retrieval seeding, in-context generation, and quality control. It addresses the lack of process-level supervision for training web agents.

entry.title: MiraBench: Evaluating Action-Conditioned Reliability in Robotic World Models

author.name: Tianzhuo Yang, Zihan Shen, Zirui Mi, Zhaoyi Zhang, Jiayi Zhou, Jiaming Ji, Juntao Dai, Jiawei Chen, Boyuan Chen, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: Introduces MiraBench, a hierarchical benchmark defining action-conditioned reliability for robotic world models across physics adherence, action faithfulness, and failure calibration. It moves evaluation beyond visual fidelity toward whether predicted futures are physically plausible and correctly fail.

entry.title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Temporal Logit Observability for LLM Safety Failures

author.name: Junyoung Park, Sunghwan Park, Seongyong Ju, Jaewoo Lee

entry.summary: Introduces Temporal Logit Observability, a training-free diagnostic that tracks a compliance-refusal margin during decoding to distinguish how jailbreaks unfold rather than just whether they succeed. It places model-attack conditions on a calibrated 2D plane, adding information where attack success rate is least informative.

entry.title: NaRA: Noise-Aware LoRA for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Shuaidi Wang, Zhan Zhuang, Ruping Huang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: NaRA introduces noise-aware LoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of diffusion LLMs, generating a low-rank core matrix conditioned on the noise level to capture the dynamics of the denoising trajectory. It addresses the mismatch of static PEFT methods designed for autoregressive models.

entry.title: MEMENTO: Leveraging Web as a Learning Signal for Low-Data Domains

author.name: Ashutosh Ojha, Vinay Aggarwal, Ashutosh Srivastava, Siddharth Yedlapati, Yaman K Singla, Jitendra Ajmera

entry.summary: MEMENTO treats the open web as a learning signal rather than a stateless retrieval interface for low-data domains, using an Adaptive Exploration Tree for within-session exploration and accumulating refined domain knowledge and search strategies across sessions. It mimics how human practitioners build expertise through self-directed web interaction.

entry.title: SAAS: Self-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Over-Search Mitigation in Agentic Search

author.name: Yunbo Tang, Chengyi Yang, Shiyu Liu, Zhishang Xiang, Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: SAAS is an RL framework that cultivates self-awareness in agentic search to mitigate over-search, helping agents recognize knowledge boundaries so they avoid unnecessary searches and terminate when evidence suffices. It targets reduced latency and cost without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: PRAIB: Peer Review AI Benchmark of Behaviour of LLM-Assisted Reviewing

author.name: Krzysztof \.Zurawicki, Julia Farganus, Arkadiusz Gawe{\l}, Mateusz Bystro\'nski, Tomasz Jan Kajdanowicz

entry.summary: PRAIB introduces a benchmark and large-scale empirical study (11,000 reviews across five models for 1,000+ papers) examining whether LLMs engage with manuscripts like human reviewers or merely produce review-looking text, measuring specificity, style, and engagement behavior. It addresses the rising use of LLMs in peer review.

entry.title: Moment-KV: Momentum-Based Decode-Time KV Cache Compression for Long Generation

author.name: Soumyadeep Jana, Sagar Nishad, Sanasam Ranbir Singh

entry.summary: Moment-KV is a momentum-based decode-time KV cache compression method for long generation, exploiting observed temporal attention patterns where critical tokens get sustained attention versus short-lived local bursts. It avoids compressing the prefill cache and improves on rigid recency-window heuristics.

entry.title: Cookie-Bench: Continuous On-screen Key Interaction Evaluation for Web Generation

author.name: Haoyue Yang, Zhangxiao Shen, Fan Ding, Hangting Lou, Yifeng Kou, Haoqing Yu, Jingyao Li, Zhengfan Wu, Siqi Bao, Jing Liu, Hua Wu

entry.summary: Cookie-Bench articulates a reference-free, autonomously driven, holistically reasoned evaluation regime for LLM-generated front-end web code, instantiated via an 11-domain, 1,000-query WebDev benchmark covering static and interactive tasks. It addresses the unscalable cost of human-judged web-generation leaderboards.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Data Synthesis for LLMs via Minimal Sufficient Representation Learning

author.name: Tong Ye, Hang Yu, Tengfei Ma, Xuhong Zhang, Jianguo Li, Peng Di, Peiyu Liu, Jianwei Yin, Wenhai Wang

entry.summary: This work tackles domain-specific data synthesis through an inductive paradigm where the target domain is defined only by reference examples rather than explicit natural-language descriptions, using minimal sufficient representation learning. It addresses real scenarios where domains are hard to articulate formally.

entry.title: Selective QA over Conflicting Multi-Source Personal Memory: A Diagnostic Testbed and Method Comparison

author.name: Tiancheng Yang, Matthias Schonlau, Ilia Sucholutsky

entry.summary: This work studies selective QA over conflicting multi-source personal memory, providing a diagnostic benchmark (18 templates, 8 reasoning types, 480 personas, 34,560 instances) with controlled source distortions to separate evidence errors from conflict-resolution errors. It targets emerging persistent personal AI agents.

entry.title: Enhancing Multi-Agent Communication through Attention Steering with Context Relevance

author.name: Hongxiang Zhang, Yuan Tian, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Agent-Radar is a training-free context management method for multi-agent LLM systems that dynamically steers each agent's attention toward relevant context using temporal and spatial decay, combating dilution from long accumulating conversation histories. It reports gains up to 7.64 points across five benchmarks.

entry.title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training

author.name: Yalun Dai, Yangyu Huang, Tongshen Yang, Yonghan Wang, Xin Zhang, Wenshan Wu, Qihao Zhao, Hao Li, Yuanyuan Gao, Kim-Hui Yap, Scarlett Li

entry.summary: This work systematically explores how data organization (not just selection) influences LLM training by reusing pre-computed sample-level scores, identifying four guidelines: Boundary Sharpening, Cyclic Scheduling, Curriculum Continuity, and Local Diversity. It targets the underexplored ordering question for single-epoch training with minimal overhead.

entry.title: SchGen: PCB Schematic Generation with Semantic-Grounded Code Representations

author.name: Qinpei Luo, Ruichun Ma, Xinyu Zhang, Lili Qiu

entry.summary: SchGen is presented as the first LLM that generates editable PCB schematics from natural-language requests, introducing a semantically grounded code representation encoding schematic editing primitives to replace verbose tool-specific geometry-heavy formats. It addresses the lack of an LLM-suited representation and dataset for PCB design.

entry.title: Benchmarking Open-Source Safety Guard Models: A Comprehensive Evaluation

author.name: Reetu Raj Harsh, Bhaskarjit Sarmah, Stefano Pasquali

entry.summary: This work comprehensively evaluates 14 open-source safety guard models on a curated 79,331-sample benchmark spanning 8 NIST AI Risk Framework categories, aggregating four datasets and emphasizing recall as the critical metric since missing harmful content poses greater risk than false positives. It compares moderation performance across guard models.

entry.title: First head-to-head comparison of agentic AI applied to the analysis of simulated data of the Einstein Telescope

author.name: Gianluca Inguglia

entry.summary: A head-to-head comparison of Claude Code and OpenAI Codex autonomously executing an end-to-end gravitational wave analysis pipeline on Einstein Telescope simulated data, including manuscript writing. Both received identical specs and compute, run twice.

entry.title: Return-to-Go Is More Than a Number: Q-Guided Alignment for Return-Conditioned Supervised Learning

author.name: Yuxiao Yang, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: Q-Align DT enforces alignment between return-to-go inputs and the Q-value of output policies in return-conditioned supervised learning, using a Q-function for dense guidance plus RTG-perturbation fine-tuning. It provides theoretical guarantees for near-optimal policy learning.

entry.title: Structured Prompt Optimization Meets Reinforcement Learning for Global and Local Interpretability over Complex Text

author.name: Tianyang Zhou, Wenbo Chen, Pierre Jinghong Liang, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: eXTC is an explainable text classifier with three stages: learning a natural-language rulebook via structured prompt optimization, distilling SOP-grounded reasoning into a compact model, and expanding reasoning via RL. It targets the trade-off between scalable fine-tuning and interpretable prompt optimization.

entry.title: SafeRx-Agent: A Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Safe and Explainable Medication Recommendation

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Hanwei Wu, Zhenghan Tai, Sicheng Lyu, Qincheng Lu, Ziyu Zhao, Jijun Chi, Jingrui Tian, Xiao-Wen Chang, Ziyang Song

entry.summary: SafeRx-Agent is a knowledge-grounded multi-agent framework for safe, explainable medication recommendation using fine-grained fourth-level ATC code generation with safety verification and traceability. It addresses the limited grounding of structured methods and the lack of safety checks in LLM agents.

entry.title: Stochastic Lifting for Generating Trajectories of Stochastic Physical Systems

author.name: Jules Berman, Tobias Blickhan, Benjamin Peherstorfer

entry.summary: Stochastic Lifting generates trajectories of stochastic physical systems by attaching high-dimensional random labels to state transitions and fitting a transition map with standard regression, avoiding mean-collapse. The labels act as auxiliary coordinates enabling multiple plausible next states.

entry.title: DLM-SWAI: Steering Diffusion Language Models Before They Unmask

author.name: Hyeseon An, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Proposes DLM-SWAI, a training-free inference-time steering method that biases token distributions during denoising of diffusion language models before tokens are unmasked. It enables controllable generation without auxiliary models, unlike autoregressive-oriented steering methods.

entry.title: Opir: Efficient Multi-Task Safety Classification for Toxicity, Jailbreaks, Hate Speech, and Harmful Content

author.name: Ihor Stepanov, Aleksandr Smechov

entry.summary: Introduces Opir, a family of efficient encoder-based guardrail models on the GLiClass architecture for multi-task safety classification covering toxicity, jailbreaks, hate speech, and harmful content. It releases edge variants under 100M parameters for real-time safety filtering.

entry.title: Evolve as a Team: Collaborative Self-Evolution for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhezheng Hao, Tianfu Wang, Huanshuo Dong, Ziyan Liu, Hong Wang, Xiankun Lin, Qiang Lin, Can Wang, Hande Dong, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Meta-Team, an experience-driven collaborative self-evolution framework for LLM multi-agent systems that learns to improve from prolonged, interleaved execution experience. It addresses the difficulty of identifying what to improve in complex multi-agent trajectories.

entry.title: CB-SLICE: Concept-Based Interpretable Error Slice Discovery

author.name: Yael Konforti, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Elaf Almahmoud, Mateja Jamnik

entry.summary: Introduces CB-SLICE, which leverages Concept Bottleneck Models to discover interpretable error slices grounded in the model's own inference process via concept mispredictions. It addresses the gap where existing slice discovery methods produce explanations disconnected from inference.

entry.title: Towards Verifiable Multimodal Deep Research: A Multi-Agent Harness for Interleaved Report Generation

author.name: Chenghao Zhang, Guanting Dong, Yufan Liu, Tong Zhao, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Proposes Ptah, a multi-agent harness for verifiable multimodal deep research that orchestrates planning, research, and writing to generate interleaved text-and-image web reports with claim-grounded evidence. It addresses open-ended synthesis without deterministic ground truth.

entry.title: CRITIC-R1: Learning Structured Critics for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Wenhan Xiao, Ziwei Zhang, Chuanyue Yu, Xingcheng Fu, Qingyun Sun, Runhua Xu, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: Proposes CRITIC-R1, a structured critic framework that formulates RAG critique as explicit error diagnosis across multiple dimensions and learns it via reinforcement learning. It addresses coarse, over-aggressive, and unreliable feedback from existing RAG critics.

entry.title: What drives performance in molecular MPNNs? An operator-level factorial benchmark

author.name: Panyu Jiao, Shuizhou Chen, Yiheng Shen, Yuyang Wang, Runhai Ouyang, Wei Xie

entry.summary: Presents an operator-level factorial benchmark decomposing molecular message-passing networks into message-seed initialization, fusion, and update operators across 84 configurations on ten datasets. Finds performance driven mainly by message construction rather than update complexity.

entry.title: LLUMI: Improving LLM Writing Assistance for Mental Health Support with Online Community Feedback

author.name: Jiwon Kim, Maya Ajit, Sherry Gong, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Dong Whi Yoo, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Introduces LLUMI, an in-house hostable LLM setup for mental health support with a generation model and an improvement model trained on online community feedback. Addresses privacy and data-governance concerns of cloud-based mental health AI.

entry.title: PROTOCOL: Late Interaction Retrieval for Protein Homolog Search

author.name: Gabrielle Cohn, Rohan Gumaste, Minh Hoang, Vihan Lakshman

entry.summary: ProtoCol applies ColBERT-style late interaction over residue-level protein embeddings to improve remote homolog detection in the difficult twilight zone. Brings retrieval techniques to bioinformatics for better alignment sensitivity.

entry.title: Access Sets Matter: Budgeting Expert Reads for Scalable Weight-Space Model Merging

author.name: Yuanyi Wang, Yanggan Gu, Su Lu, Yifan Yang, Zhaoyi Yan, Congkai Xie, Jianmin Wu, Hongxia Yang

entry.summary: MergePipe reframes LLM weight-space merging as an expert access-set problem under explicit I/O budgets, indexing parameter blocks and building deterministic, replayable budgeted merge plans. Addresses the practical I/O bottleneck of large-scale model merging.

entry.title: Feedback-to-Rubrics: Can We Learn Expert Criteria from Inline Comments?

author.name: Kotaro Yoshida, So Kuroki, Yuki Imajuku, Taishi Nakamura, Ryunosuke Iwai, Haruki Goda, Takuya Akiba

entry.summary: Studies learning reusable natural-language rubrics from accumulated inline comments on drafts, inferring and iteratively refining rubrics by observing comment-wise mismatches. Aims to capture tacit expert review criteria for LLM writing support.

entry.title: Active Continual Learning with Metaplastic Binary Bayesian Neural Networks

author.name: Kellian Cottart, Th\'eo Ballet, Djohan Bonnet, Damien Querlioz

entry.summary: BiMU is a metaplastic binary Bayesian neural network derived from a bounded-memory variational objective balancing stability, plasticity, and forgetting, with uncertainty-dependent step sizes preventing posterior saturation and enabling buffer-free active querying via Monte Carlo disagreement. Targets always-on edge continual learning.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Finetuning of LLMs via Convex Reconstruction and Gradient Caching

author.name: Alaa Khamis, Alaa Maalouf

entry.summary: HullFT accelerates test-time finetuning of LLMs by representing a query embedding as a sparse convex combination of training sequences via Frank-Wolfe optimization, plus gradient caching. It aims to remove both retrieval and finetuning bottlenecks that make per-query adaptation impractical.

entry.title: Anytime-Valid Federated Conformal RAG for LLM Swarms

author.name: Prasanjit Dubey, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This work extends Federated Conformal RAG to anytime-valid sequential coverage guarantees for swarms of weak language models under bandwidth limits. It introduces a summable calibration-deviation budget to convert marginal coverage into valid sequential e-process bounds at no extra assumptions.

entry.title: Modeling Community Attitude through Reaction Tone: A Human-AI Collaborative Framework for Evaluating LLM Alignment with Linguistic Behaviors in Online Communities

author.name: Nuan Wen, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: EvoSpec evolves speculative decoding in real time via dynamic vocabulary and parameter adaptation, addressing acceptance-rate drops in specialized or topic-switching scenarios. It retrieves critical long-tail tokens through context-aware semantic and statistical signals.

entry.title: Reading or Guessing? Visual Grounding Failures of Vision-Language Models for OCR in Ancient Greek Editions

author.name: Antonia Karamolegkou, Nicolas Angleraud, Beno\^it Sagot, Thibault Cl\'erice

entry.summary: This work shows VLMs used for OCR on Ancient Greek critical editions generate plausible but visually unsupported text, relying on language priors rather than reading. It introduces controlled image perturbations and token-level grounding measures to detect this behavior.

entry.title: TARQ: Tail-Aware Reconstruction Quantization for Rare-Word Robust Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Ziyu Zhao, Ke Bai, Silin Meng, Dongming Shen, Xiao-Wen Chang, Yixuan HE

entry.summary: TARQ is a label-free post-training quantization framework for ASR that shifts calibration mass toward the lexical tail (names, numerals, rare words) via a closed-form per-layer rule. It improves rare-word robustness without entity labels or validation decoding.

entry.title: DecomposeRL: Learning to Ask Useful, Informative, and Diverse Questions for Semi-Supervised, Traceable Claim Verification

author.name: Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Ankur Padia, Francis Ferraro

entry.summary: DecomposeRL trains a claim-verifier that produces inspectable traces by framing decomposition as an RL policy with GRPO and a multi-faceted reward, supporting semi-supervised learning. A data-curation funnel distills 115K claims into a dense 5K subset for efficient training.

entry.title: Periodic RoPE for Infinite Context LLMs

author.name: Simin Huo

entry.summary: Periodic RoPE (P-RoPE) is a positional encoding mechanism designed to circumvent position exhaustion when sequence length exceeds the pretrained RoPE range, working with sliding window attention for local dependencies plus a global no-position attention layer. It targets truly infinite context.

entry.title: SuperValid: Capability-Aligned OOD Validation for Generalizable Downstream Scaling

author.name: Quanen Sun, Changxin Tian, Ke Shi, Cai Chen, Cunyin Peng, Jia Liu, Kunlong Chen, Zhiqiang Zhang

entry.summary: SuperValid argues that downstream scaling laws should be studied at the capability level rather than benchmark level, synthesizing OOD capability-aligned validation data to better track skill improvements as training distributions vary. It addresses limitations of IID validation loss for predicting downstream performance.

entry.title: Framing Matters: Addressing Framing Sensitivity in Decision-Making through Behaviorally-Grounded Value Alignment

author.name: Seojin Hwang, Minju Kim, Junhyuk Choi, JeongHyun Park, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: This work shows LLM decisions are highly sensitive to framing of factually equivalent inputs, with an average 28.6% decision flip rate across value-tinted, temporal, and vividness dimensions in a benchmark called Fragile. It finds simple prompt- and activation-level interventions fail and pursues behaviorally grounded value alignment.

entry.title: Skill0.5: Joint Skill Internalization and Utilization for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiapeng Zhu, Jianxiang Yu, Yibo Zhao, Chengcheng Han, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Li, Weining Qian

entry.summary: Skill0.5 is an agentic RL framework that differentiates skill treatments by combining general skill internalization with task-specific skill utilization, avoiding the rigid choice between full externalization (context overhead) and full internalization (overfitting). It targets out-of-distribution generalization for autonomous agents.

entry.title: MemTrace: Tracing and Attributing Errors in Large Language Model Memory Systems

author.name: Xinle Deng, Ruobin Zhong, Hujin Peng, Xiaoben Lu, Yanzhe Wu, Guang Li, Buqiang Xu, Yunzhi Yao, Jizhan Fang, Haoliang Cao, Junjie Guo, Yuan Yuan, Ziqing Ma, Yuanqiang Yu, Rui Hu, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: MemTrace studies error tracing and attribution in LLM memory systems by transforming memory pipelines into executable memory evolution graphs for fine-grained tracing of information flow. It introduces MemTraceBench from representative systems like RAG, Mem0, and EverMemOS to study memory failure modes.

entry.title: Rethinking Memory as Continuously Evolving Connectivity

author.name: Jizhan Fang, Buqiang Xu, Zhixian Wang, Haoliang Cao, Xinle Deng, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ruohui Huang, Gang Yu, Ying Wei, Guozhou Zheng, Feiyu Xiong, Haofen Wang, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: FluxMem models LLM agent memory as a continuously evolving heterogeneous graph, progressively refining its topology through initial connection formation, feedback-driven refinement, and long-term consolidation. It repairs missing links, prunes interference, and distills recurrent successful trajectories during execution.

entry.title: OmniVerifier-M1: Multimodal Meta-Verifier with Explicit Structured Recalibration

author.name: Xinchen Zhang, Bowei Liu, Jiale Liu, Chufan Shi, Yizhen Zhang, Junhong Liu, Youliang Zhang, Zhiheng Li, Yujiu Yang, Ling Yang

entry.summary: OmniVerifier-M1 is a multimodal meta-verifier that leverages verifier-generated rationales rather than decision-only signals, finding symbolic outputs like bounding boxes outperform textual explanations as rationales. It decouples reinforcement learning to incorporate meta-verification feedback for fine-grained visual verification.

entry.title: Where Rollouts Begin: Low-Load, High-Leverage First-Token Diversification for RLVR

author.name: Soeun Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: Identifies the first token after the reasoning marker as a high-leverage, low-cost position to broaden rollout diversity in RLVR, exploiting its sharply peaked yet correctness-decoupled distribution. It improves exploration efficiency in reasoning RL. Matters for efficient RLVR training.

entry.title: Why Far Looks Up: Probing Spatial Representation in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Cheolhong Min, Jaeyun Jung, Daeun Lee, Hyeonseong Jeon, Yu Su, Jonathan Tremblay, Chan Hee Song, Jaesik Park

entry.summary: This paper probes spatial representations in VLMs, revealing a consistent vertical-distance entanglement where models conflate vertical image position with distance, mirroring photographic perspective bias. The bias creates an accuracy gap and intensifies under data scaling.

entry.title: FreeForm: Reduced-Order Deformable Simulation from Particle-Based Skinning Eigenmodes

author.name: Donglai Xiang, Vismay Modi, Rishit Dagli, Ty Trusty, Gilles Daviet, Anka He Chen, Nicholas Sharp, David I. W. Levin

entry.summary: FreeForm introduces mesh-free reduced-order simulation of deformable hyperelastic objects using Reproducing Kernel Particle Method representations, building skinning eigenmodes from the elastic energy Hessian. It achieves 40x training speedup over per-shape neural field optimization.

entry.title: Phase-Conditioned Imitation Learning with Autonomous Failure Recovery for Robust Deformable Object Manipulation

author.name: Dayuan Chen, Kai Tang, Yukuan Zhang, Kazuhiro Kosuge, Yasuhisa Hirata

entry.summary: Proposes a phase-conditioned, force-aware imitation learning framework with autonomous failure recovery for deformable object manipulation, using FiLM-conditioned ACT and a multimodal phase predictor to overcome Markovian state-aliasing. It enables phase-specific behaviors and recovery within a single policy.

entry.title: EXACT-MPPI: Exact Signed-Distance Navigation for Arbitrary-Footprint Robots from Point Clouds via Path Integral Control

author.name: Chen Peng, Zhikang Ge, Wenwu Lu, Haiming Gao, Stavros Vougioukas, Peng Wei

entry.summary: EXACT-MPPI is a training-free local navigation framework for arbitrary-footprint robots that embeds an exact analytic signed-distance evaluator directly on point clouds within MPPI control, avoiding occupancy-grid or distance-field rasterization. It enables safe navigation for complex non-convex footprints in clutter.

entry.title: MARS Policy: Multimodality Only When It Matters

author.name: Jindou Jia, Tuo An, Yuxuan Hu, Gen Li, Jingliang Li, Bohan Hou, Xiangyu Chen, Jiaqi Bai, Bofan Lyu, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: MARS Policy adaptively invokes stochastic generative sampling only at task phases that truly need behavioral diversity, using deterministic actions elsewhere to reduce training complexity and improve inference efficiency. It is motivated by the observation that not all task phases require multimodality.

entry.title: PRO-CUA: Process-Reward Optimization for Computer Use Agents

author.name: Yifei He, Rui Yang, Hao Bai, Tong Zhang, Han Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes PRO-CUA, a process-reward optimization framework for computer-use agents that uses iterative step-level reinforcement learning to overcome imitation bottlenecks and sparse trajectory rewards. It decouples on-policy training to improve long-horizon GUI task performance.

entry.title: The Confidence Shortcut: A Reasoning Failure Mode of Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Dueun Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: Identifies a confidence-shortcut failure in masked diffusion language models where confidence-based decoding predicts easy tokens before resolving long-range dependencies, causing high-confidence errors on reasoning tasks like multi-digit addition. It argues confidence-aligned training entrenches this misalignment.

entry.title: OpenClawBench: Benchmarking Process-side Anomalies in Real-world Agent Execution Trajectories

author.name: Yibing Liu, Yangze Liu, Xiaolong Yin, Bin Wang, Chong Zhang, Hao Yin, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: Introduces OpenClawBench, a 31,264-trajectory dataset for detecting process-side anomalies in real agent executions that pass final task oracles but accumulate unsafe writes, unresolved ambiguity, or overcommitment. It frames this Outcome-Process Gap and provides structured anomaly supervision.

entry.title: PassNet: Scaling Large Language Models for Graph Compiler Pass Generation

author.name: Yiqun Liu, Yingsheng Wu, Ruqi Yang, Enrong Zheng, Honglei Qiu, Sijun He, Tai Liang, Jingjing Wu, Yuhan Zhou, Yiwei Zhang, Dongyan Chen, Weihan Yi, Xinqi Li, Siqi Bao

entry.summary: Presents PassNet, a large-scale ecosystem for LLM-based compiler pass generation, where models author structured graph transformations integrated into tensor-compiler pipelines, plus a dataset of 18K graphs from 100K real models. It targets long-tail workloads where default compilation causes slowdowns.

entry.title: Aligned but Fragile: Enhancing LLM Safety Robustness via Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Yifan Wu, Jian Lou, Di Wang, Yuxi Zhou, Yuke Hu

entry.summary: Studies LLM safety-alignment robustness from the optimizer perspective, proposing zeroth-order optimization to make alignment more resistant to lightweight post-alignment manipulations like parameter/activation noise and quantization. It is the first to examine the base optimizer's role in alignment fragility.

entry.title: Why Specialist Models Still Matter: A Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Paradigm for Medical Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Yanan Wang, Shuaicong Hu, Jian Liu, Guohui Zhou, Aiguo Wang, Cuiwei Yang

entry.summary: HetMedAgent proposes a heterogeneous medical multi-agent framework combining generalist LLMs, domain-specific specialist models, and clinicians with conflict-aware evidence fusion and uncertainty-based intervention triggering. It argues specialist models remain essential rather than obsolete in the age of strong generalist LLMs.

entry.title: SkillsInjector: Dynamic Skill Context Construction for LLM Agents

author.name: Yanchao Li, Wanhao Liu, Ben Gao, Jiaqing Xie, Zhehong Ai, Na Zou, Yuqiang Li, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: SkillsInjector is a two-stage adaptive method for LLM agents that learns execution-grounded skill preferences, admits an adaptive number of skills per task, and refines how skills are presented. It argues against static skill injection where adding more skills can degrade performance.

entry.title: Redundant or Necessary? A Benchmark for Detecting Redundant Steps in Agent Trajectories

author.name: Minyang Hu, Bo Yang, Zhinuo Zhou, Jiachen Liang, Guo Jiahao, Yiyang Yin, Xiongwei Han

entry.summary: This work formulates redundant step detection for agent trajectories as a new research area and introduces RedundancyBench, a benchmark with annotated trajectories labeling each step's contribution to task completion. It shifts evaluation focus from task success to execution efficiency.

entry.title: On the Geometry of Games and their Solvers

author.name: Yaqi Sun, Julian Ma, David Mguni

entry.summary: This work studies equilibrium computation through a solver-game map linking game classes to effective solver dynamics, proposing that solvability is governed by latent structural properties forming a continuous landscape rather than discrete taxonomies. It aims to unify fragmented solver-by-solver guarantees in game theory and GAN-style learning.

entry.title: KairosAgent: Agentic Time Series Forecasting with Fused Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Kun Feng, Ziwei Shan, Yuchen Fang, Yiyang Tan, Sihan Lu, Shuqi Gu, Lintao Ma, Xingyu Lu, Kan Ren

entry.summary: KairosAgent is an agentic framework for cross-domain multimodal time series forecasting combining an LLM-based reasoner with a time-series-foundation-model forecaster, unifying numerical comprehension with semantic reasoning. It addresses the complementary weaknesses of TSFMs and LLMs.

entry.title: Aryabhata 2: Scaling Reinforcement Learning for Advanced STEM Reasoning

author.name: Ritvik Rastogi, Vishal Singh, Tejas Chaudhari, Sandeep Varma

entry.summary: Aryabhata 2 is a reasoning-focused LLM for competitive STEM exams (JEE, NEET) post-trained from GPT-OSS-20B via reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using PhysicsWallah's question banks. It targets deployable, consistently structured problem solving for millions of student doubts.

entry.title: Emergent Semantic Representations in World Models through Physical Interaction without Linguistic Supervision

author.name: Jiayi Fang

entry.summary: This work shows that a VAE-based world model trained on random embodied exploration develops latent spatial structure mirroring physical geometry, without any linguistic supervision. It argues that semantic representations emerge from the geometric structure of the physical world.

entry.title: unix-ctf: Procedural Environments for Unix-Competence Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Geoffrey Bradway, Roger Creus Castanyer, Lorenz Wolf, Maxwill Lin, Matthew James Sargent, Augustine N. Mavor-Parker

entry.summary: unix-ctf is a procedural capture-the-flag generator for training shell agents on genuine Unix competence, distinguishing shell/OS skill from general programming. Each task hides a flag using a single Unix feature inside a fresh Linux container via an LLM-assisted synthesis pipeline.

entry.title: DynSess: Dynamic Session-Level Evaluation and Optimization Framework for Role-Playing Agents

author.name: Rongsheng Zhang, Jiji Tang, Junnan Ren, Zuyi Bao, Weijie Chen, Ruofan Hu, Zhou Zhao, Tangjie Lv, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: DynSess is a session-level evaluation and optimization framework for role-playing agents, scoring complete dialogue sessions and training characters via multi-turn lookahead search with off-policy and on-policy variants. It addresses the turn-level limitation of existing methods for long-horizon role-play quality.

entry.title: MusTBENCH: Benchmarking and Advancing Temporal Grounding in Music LLMs

author.name: Daeyong Kwon, Qiyu Wu, Shinobu Kuriya, Junghyun Koo, Shuyang Cui, Zhi Zhong, Wei-Hsiang Liao, Hiromi Wakaki, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: MusTBENCH is a music-expert-validated benchmark evaluating temporal grounding in large audio-language models through five temporally grounded QA tasks. It also proposes MusT, a four-stage temporal optimization recipe to improve grounding of musical events like instrument entries and rhythmic transitions.

entry.title: Quotient DAGs for Off-Policy Evaluation:Forward-Flow Importance Sampling and Exact Slate Propensities

author.name: Ziwen Xie, Shaowen Xiang, Hongyu He, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a quotient-DAG view for off-policy evaluation that merges generation-history details irrelevant to the reward, enabling forward-flow importance sampling and exact unordered slate propensities. It reduces nuisance variance and computational cost in slate recommendation evaluation.

entry.title: Singularity-aware Optimization via Randomized Geometric Probing: Towards Stable Non-smooth Optimization

author.name: Ruoran Xu, Borong She, Xiaobo Jin, Qiufeng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Singularity-aware Adam, an optimizer that stabilizes training on non-smooth loss landscapes (from ReLU, quantization) by modulating step sizes via a Local Geometric Instability metric. It addresses gradient chattering caused by conflicting subdifferential signals in Adam.

entry.title: Inferring Code Correctness from Specification

author.name: Tambon Florian, Papadakis Mike

entry.summary: Proposes TRAILS, which validates LLM-generated code correctness by grounding reasoning in concrete input-output pairs generated via specification-based category partitioning and execution. It aims to avoid the cost of dynamic consensus and the brittleness of pure static reasoning.

entry.title: Towards Localized and Disentangled Knowledge Editing for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Leijiang Gu, Zhen Zeng, Feng Li, Xinjian Gao, Zenglin Shi

entry.summary: Proposes Localized and Disentangled Knowledge Editing for multimodal LLMs, identifying causal misalignment and feature entanglement as failure modes that prevent edits from generalizing or cause collateral changes. It aims to make multimodal edits both generalizable and localized.

entry.title: Does The Way You Plan Matter? An Empirical Study of Planning Representations for LLM Web Agents

author.name: Alejandra Zambrano, Sara Vera Marjanovic, Imene Kerboua, Xing Han L\`u, Leila Kosseim

entry.summary: Introduces PlanAhead, a static planner-executor framework that systematically evaluates how different natural language plan representations (sequential subgoals, narrative, pseudocode) affect LLM web agent performance on hard WebArena tasks. It also auto-categorizes task difficulty without human annotation.

entry.title: CityGen: Structure-Guided City-Style Synthesis for Cross-City Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zezhong Qian, Zhao Yang, Lu Tan, Zhihao Yan, Weiyi Hong, Haizhuang Liu, Yawei Jueluo

entry.summary: Introduces CityTransfer-Bench, a geographically disjoint benchmark for cross-city autonomous driving generalization across perception, segmentation, and planning, plus CityGen, a structure-guided city-style synthesis method. It avoids reliance on labeled target data or city-specific annotations.

entry.title: Masked Diffusion Modeling for Anomaly Detection

author.name: Lixing Zhang, Yuchen Liang, Liyan Xie

entry.summary: Proposes MaskDiff-AD, a forward-only anomaly detection method using masked diffusion models trained on nominal data, scoring anomalies by reconstruction difficulty of masked coordinates. Targets categorical, mixed-type, and discrete sequence data.

entry.title: City-Mesh3R: Simulation-Ready City-Scale 3D Mesh Reconstruction from Multi-View Images

author.name: Sayan Paul, Sourav Ghosh, Siddharth Katageri, Soumyadip Maity, Sanjana Sinha, Brojeshwar Bhowmick

entry.summary: Presents City-Mesh3R, a scalable framework reconstructing watertight, simulation-ready 3D surface meshes directly from large unordered image collections of urban scenes. Addresses incomplete geometry and noisy surfaces that hinder NeRF and Gaussian-splatting city reconstruction.

entry.title: Information-Directed Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Keru Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes residual uncertainty in offline-to-online RL via conditional mutual information and applies information-directed sampling with a generic Bayesian regret bound. Provides a principled exploration framework for warm-started policies.

entry.title: Relational Rank Geometry in Transformers: Detecting and Steering Hidden-State Relation Frames

author.name: Mazen Kobrosly

entry.summary: Studies rank-indexed geometry of relations in transformer hidden states using Plucker sign entropy, finding that true r-argument relation tuples show arity-matched orientation signatures across Llama 8B/70B/405B. A novel interpretability probe for relational structure.

entry.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Molecular Mixture Behavior Prediction

author.name: Roel J. Leenhouts, Nathan K. Morgan, William Green, Jan G. Rittig, Florence H. Vermeire

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation framework that decomposes molecular mixture-property prediction error into pure-component and non-ideal interaction components, with leakage-aware splits and excess-property metrics, plus curated benchmarks. Improves rigor in mixture ML evaluation.

entry.title: EMAG: Differentiable 4D Gaussian Mixture Splatting for EEG Spatial Super-Resolution

author.name: Alex Lazarovich, Ofir Itzhak Shahar, Gur Elkin, Ohad Ben-Shahar

entry.summary: EMAG reconstructs high-density EEG from sparse low-density electrodes using a differentiable mixture of anisotropic 4D space-time Gaussians with a physically-motivated forward rendering model. Enables EEG spatial super-resolution.

entry.title: Treatment-Conditioned Diffusion for Forecasting Neurodegenerative Disease Progression

author.name: Danylo Boiko, Viktoriia Mishkurova

entry.summary: Proposes a treatment-conditioned diffusion framework that forecasts high-fidelity future brain states for Parkinson's progression by conditioning on screening DaTscan images and levodopa dosage over a year, using a transformer encoder. Moves beyond scalar clinical scores to imaging-level forecasting.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Set Representation Learning Under Inference-Time Element Corruption

author.name: Yankai Chen (Steve), Hanrong Zhang (Steve), Bowei He (Steve), Philip S. Yu (Steve), Xue (Steve), Liu

entry.summary: SW-DRSO is a distributionally robust set representation learning framework that optimizes a tractable surrogate of worst-case loss over plausible inference-time element corruptions using a differentiable barycentric adversary. Improves robustness to outliers and missing set elements at deployment.

entry.title: Striding Across Reynolds Numbers: Representation Geometry in Neural PDE Generalisation

author.name: Jianing Shi

entry.summary: Investigates cross-Reynolds generalization in neural PDE solvers, finding representation geometry is a major organizing variable; ConvAE-Relay matches latent states and borrows dynamics from a source database to achieve strong out-of-distribution error without target fitting. Reframes PDE generalization through representation geometry.

entry.title: OOD-GraphLLM: Graph Large Language Model for Out-of-Distribution Generalized Drug Synergy Prediction

author.name: Xin Wang, Linxin Xiao, Yang Yao, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: OOD-GraphLLM applies a graph large language model to out-of-distribution generalized drug synergy prediction, addressing topological distribution shifts from novel compounds. It claims to be the first to tackle OOD-generalized drug synergy prediction with graph LLMs.

entry.title: Generative Spatiotemporal Intent Sequence Recommendation via Implicit Reasoning in Amap

author.name: Sicong Wang, Ruiting Dong, Yue Liu, Bowen Zheng, Jun Meng, Jie Li, Shuaijun Guo, Yu Gu, Fanyi Di, Xin Li

entry.summary: GPlan is a generative spatiotemporal intent sequence recommendation framework deployed in Amap that internalizes LLM reasoning into lightweight models to produce logically coherent, physically executable intent sequences. It addresses high LLM inference latency and physically infeasible plans for industrial recommendation.

entry.title: Implicit Identity Technologies for LLMs: Fingerprinting and Watermarking across Datasets, Models, and Generated Content

author.name: Bing Liu, Shunping Wang, Yufan Zhu, Xinyi Yu, Jing Huang, Linkang Du, Hongbin Pei, Wei Luo

entry.summary: This survey introduces implicit identity as a unifying abstraction to organize LLM fingerprinting and watermarking across datasets, models, and generated content for ownership, provenance, and attribution. It addresses a fragmented field with inconsistent terminology and isolated asset-specific methods.

entry.title: Deep Optimal Individualized Treatment Rules for Bivariate Survival Outcomes via Adaptive Prediction-Powered Learning

author.name: Kun Ren, Yifan Cui, Wen Su

entry.summary: This paper derives deep optimal individualized treatment rules for bivariate survival outcomes under right censoring, maximizing joint survival probability via stochastic policies and coupled accelerated failure time models. It introduces an adaptive prediction-powered method leveraging auxiliary ML predictions for robustness.

entry.title: Bridging the Stability-Expressivity Gap: Synthetic Data Scaling and Preference Alignment for Low-Resource Spoken Language Models

author.name: Yizhong Geng, Yanliang Li, Jinghan Yang, Tianhan Jiang, Boxun An, Ya Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: This paper identifies a Stability-Expressivity Gap when scaling spoken language models with synthetic data in low-resource settings: synthetic data improves phonetic accuracy but suppresses prosodic variability, causing expressivity collapse. It proposes preference alignment to bridge the trade-off.

entry.title: Keyphrase Generative Representation of Youth Crisis Conversations Beyond Static Taxonomies

author.name: Abeer Badawi, Will Aitken, Lydia Sequeira, Jocelyn Rankin, Maia Norman, Elham Dolatabadi

entry.summary: This work analyzes over 700K youth crisis SMS conversations, expanding a 19-label taxonomy into a 39-label hierarchical schema, and introduces Keyphrase Generative Representation, a constrained LLM that generates conversation-specific keyphrases. It captures evolving youth distress language beyond fixed taxonomies.

entry.title: DisasterBench: Benchmarking LLM Planning under Typed Tool Interface Constraints

author.name: Zhitong Chen, Kai Yin, Weifeng Zhang, Zhiyuan Wang, Xiangjue Dong, Chengkai Liu, Zhewei Liu, Yiming Xiao, Ali Mostafavi, James Caverlee

entry.summary: DisasterBench evaluates LLM planning over semantically similar but operationally distinct disaster-response tools, testing executable workflows with correct parameter binding and dependency propagation. It introduces First-Point-of-Failure for step-level failure attribution.

entry.title: Boundary Suppression Asymmetry in Post-trained Assistants: Over-expansion as a Controllability Cost

author.name: Jiarui Han

entry.summary: This work studies boundary-suppression asymmetry in post-trained assistants, asking which behaviors remain suppressible when users request narrower answers. It finds anti-underanswering policies (over-completion, extra help) are selectively resistant to suppression, a controllability cost of helpfulness optimization.

entry.title: Auditing Stance Asymmetry in Generative Explanations

author.name: Jiarui Han

entry.summary: This work audits stance-bearing asymmetry in generative explanations, where models avoid hostile language but make one side structurally understandable and another personally at fault. It proposes Symmetry Decomposition Evaluation testing paired situations with group labels, role rewrites, and support/counter-evidence.

entry.title: Knowledge Dependency Estimation for Reliable Question Answering

author.name: Chaodong Tong, Qi Zhang, Nannan Sun, Lei Jiang, Yanbing Liu

entry.summary: Knot is a structured rank-aware estimator of knowledge dependency, measuring how sensitive a black-box QA model is to different candidate knowledge units drawn from context, retrieval, decomposition, or reasoning. It models redundancy, substitutability, and complementarity without exhaustive perturbation.

entry.title: Ask Now, Use Later: Benchmarking the Proactivity Gap in Long-Lived LLM Agents

author.name: Bin Wu, Guanyun Zou, Bingbing Wang, Huan Zhao, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks a proactivity gap in long-lived LLM agents, focusing on whether agents proactively ask for reusable user preferences not needed by the current task but useful later. It introduces the Ask-to-Remember setting and addresses the difficulty of evaluating deferred, underdetermined payoffs.

entry.title: When Helpful Context Leaks: Privacy Risks in Domain-Adapted ASR

author.name: Maike Z\"ufle, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: This paper identifies a privacy risk in domain-adapted speech LLMs where context customization can nudge the model to transcribe phonetically similar terms from its context or training data, leaking private information. It measures leakage across prompting and fine-tuning, finding both cause measurable and compounding leakage.

entry.title: Routing-Aligned Fine-Tuning for Multilingual Downstream Tasks in Mixture-of-Experts Models

author.name: Guanzhi Deng, Kuan Wu, Haibo Wang, Shing Yin Wong, Sichun Luo, Linqi Song

entry.summary: RA-MoE proposes routing-aligned fine-tuning for multilingual downstream tasks in MoE models, validating that middle layers form a language-universal alignment zone where routing divergence predicts per-language performance gaps. It uses a four-way correctness taxonomy across English and target languages to guide adaptation.

entry.title: AdaDPO: Self-Adaptive Direct Preference Optimization with Balanced Gradient Updates

author.name: Shaolong Chen, Madalina Ciobanu, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: AdaDPO is a self-adaptive variant of Direct Preference Optimization that introduces per-pair stop-gradient coefficients to balance gradient magnitudes between preferred and dispreferred responses. It addresses an asymmetric gradient behavior where DPO suppresses bad answers faster than it promotes good ones.

entry.title: Functional Entropy: Predicting Functional Correctness in LLM-Generated Code with Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Dylan Bouchard, Mohit Singh Chauhan, Zeya Ahmad, Ho-Kyeong Ra

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates uncertainty quantification methods for predicting functional correctness in LLM-generated code across three languages, five LLMs, and over 1,700 problems. It finds token-probability methods transfer well while NLI-based sampling methods fail because NLI cannot distinguish functionally different code.

entry.title: GUI-CIDER: Mid-training GUI Agents via Causal Internalization and Density-aware Exemplar Reselection

author.name: Zheng Wu, Chengcheng Han, Zhengxi Lu, Tianjie Ju, Yanyu Chen, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: GUI-CIDER is a mid-training approach for GUI agents that enables explicit learning of GUI-operation world knowledge through causal internalization and density-aware exemplar reselection, rather than implicit absorption via SFT or RL. It targets the world-knowledge bottleneck limiting real-world task completion.

entry.title: Can LLMs Use Linguistic Uncertainty Markers to Reliably Reflect Intrinsic Confidence?

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This paper studies whether LLMs can use linguistic uncertainty markers (e.g., it is likely) to stably and generalizably reflect their intrinsic confidence, formalizing marker internal confidence with seven stability metrics. It is the first systematic study of how models map epistemic markers to specific confidence levels.

entry.title: The Abstraction Gap in Vision-Language Causal Reasoning

author.name: Chinh Hoang, Mohammad Rashedul Hasan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a dual-probe methodology to separate linguistic plausibility from faithful causal reasoning in VLMs, with a Chain-Text Probe requiring explicit causal chains and an Abstraction Gap metric. Evaluating eight VLMs on a large causal benchmark, it finds most exhibit large abstraction gaps that fine-tuning fails to close.

entry.title: Agents that Matter: Optimizing Multi-Agent LLMs via Removal-Based Attribution

author.name: Mingyu Lu, Yushan Huang, Chris Lin, Su-In Lee

entry.summary: Formalizes agent attribution in multi-agent LLM systems as a cooperative game and shows Leave-One-Out identifies bottleneck agents as effectively as combinatorial methods at lower cost, while LLM judges fail to approximate ablation. It provides a rigorous framework for credit assignment in MAS. Matters for optimizing and debugging multi-agent pipelines.

entry.title: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?

author.name: Yuan Tian, Bing Hu, Fang Wu, Xiaomin Li, Binghang Lu, Neil Zhenqiang Gong

entry.summary: Studies how different think-with-image reasoning paradigms in vision-language models affect multimodal jailbreak robustness, finding explicit external image-tool invocation yields the lowest attack success rates. It investigates why certain reasoning designs improve safety. Matters for safe multimodal reasoning systems.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Lean-as-Judge for Natural-Language Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Pauline Bourigault, Xiaotong Ji, Matthieu Zimmer, Rasul Tutunov, Haitham Bou Ammar

entry.summary: Proposes COVCAL, a risk-controlled selector that uses Lean proof-trace diagnostics to certify a finite-sample selective-risk bound on accepted natural-language math answers or abstain. It addresses that Lean-as-judge signals are coverage-dependent and often unfaithful. Matters for reliable automated math verification.

entry.title: Verified Misguidance: Measuring Structural Citation Failures in Search-Augmented LLMs

author.name: Yongsik Seo, Wooseok Jeong, Eunyoung Kim, Hyeonseo Jang, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: Constructs CITETRACE, a large-scale dataset tracing the full citation chain from query through retrieved source to answer with 761k evaluable citation pairs across ten models, to measure structural citation failures in search-augmented LLMs. It reveals citation quality as a silent determinant of whether users are informed or misled. Matters for trustworthy search-augmented AI.

entry.title: PEFT-Arena: Understanding Parameter-Efficient Finetuning from a Stability-Plasticity Perspective

author.name: Yangyi Huang, Ruotian Peng, Zeju Qiu, Jiale Kang, Yandong Wen, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Weiyang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces PEFT-Arena, a benchmark assessing parameter-efficient fine-tuning through the stability-plasticity dilemma, jointly measuring target-task adaptation and retention of pretrained capabilities, finding orthogonal fine-tuning achieves the best Pareto frontier. It explains differences via geometric analysis. Matters for choosing PEFT methods that avoid forgetting.

entry.title: Guidance Contrastive Token Credit Assignment for Discrete Policy Optimization

author.name: Shufan Li, Konstantinos Kallidromitis, Akash Gokul Yusuke Kato, Kazuki Kozuka, Aditya Grover

entry.summary: Proposes GCPO, a guidance contrastive policy optimization method that assigns per-token credit by contrasting model predictions under positive and negative prompts, addressing uniform sample-level credit assignment in GRPO and DAPO. It applies to math reasoning and text-to-image generation. Matters for fine-grained credit assignment in RL.

entry.title: DVSM: Decoder-only View Synthesis Model Done Right

author.name: Cheng Sun, Jaesung Choe, Min-Hung Chen, Ryo Hachiuma, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang

entry.summary: DVSM shows that a decoder-only architecture representing scenes implicitly as a KV-cache outperforms encoder-decoder Large View Synthesis Models with fewer parameters. It uses weight sharing between reconstruction and rendering networks plus foundation priors.

entry.title: Towards Consistent Video Geometry Estimation

author.name: Zhu Yu, Jingnan Gao, Runmin Zhang, Lingteng Qiu, Zhengyi Zhao, Rui Peng, Yichao Yan, Kejie Qiu, Siyu Zhu, Si-Yuan Cao, Hui-Liang Shen

entry.summary: ViGeo is a feed-forward foundation model recovering spatially dense, temporally consistent geometry from video, supporting streaming, full-sequence, and long-video inference in one model. It uses dynamic chunking attention and a completion-based data refinement framework.

entry.title: VideoFDB: Evaluating Full-Duplex Vision-Speech Capabilities in Conversational Agents

author.name: Amrita Mazumdar, Seonwook Park, Rajarshi Roy, Nikhil Srihari, Shengze Wang, Yuhao Zhou, Julia Wang, Koki Nagano, Shalini De Mello

entry.summary: VideoFDB is the first benchmark for evaluating full-duplex audio-visual conversational agents, covering simultaneous speaking, listening, and nonverbal cues. It provides 237 dyadic clips, a perception-vs-generation taxonomy, and a rubric-based LM-as-judge framework.

entry.title: Colored Noise Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Hadar Davidson, Noam Issachar, Sagie Benaim

entry.summary: Colored Noise Sampling is a training-free stochastic diffusion solver that reconsiders SDE inference as frequency-decoupled energy transfer, injecting timestep-adaptive colored noise rather than uniform white noise. It aligns noise injection with the spectral bias of diffusion trajectories.

entry.title: CCS: Clinical Consensus Selection for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Xi Zhang, Yingshu Li, Zaiqiao Meng, Jake Lever, Edmond S. L. Ho

entry.summary: CCS is a decoder-agnostic inference-time selection framework for radiology report generation that picks clinically stronger reports from a candidate pool rather than relying on default decoding. It exploits the observation that better reports often already exist within model samples.

entry.title: FLIP: Real-Time and Resilient Formation Planning for Large-Scale DIstributed Swarms via Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Yuan Zhou, Guangtong Xu, Zhenyu Hou, Jialiang Hou, Fei Gao

entry.summary: FLIP reformulates large-scale swarm formation planning as a spatiotemporal point cloud registration problem, with each agent distributively computing optimal formation positions using robust registration with outlier rejection. It targets real-time, resilient formation for large distributed swarms.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Future Hypotheses for Horizon-Aware Exploration in Multi-Step Robot Manipulation

author.name: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Andrew Melnik, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: Introduces Future-Experience Conditioning, where short LLM-guided, task-consistent future videos generated via task ontology reasoning, digital-twin rollout, and video diffusion serve as structured priors for control and RL fine-tuning in multi-step manipulation. It explores using generated futures to aid horizon-aware exploration.

entry.title: Saddle Networks: Structure-Preserving Architectures for Convex-Concave Functions

author.name: Xavier Warin

entry.summary: Introduces Saddle Networks, structure-preserving neural architectures that maintain convex-concave geometry by construction for saddle-point functions, with a proven one-dimensional approximation theorem under a Monge-type convexity condition. It supports tractable min-max formulations in optimization and optimal transport.

entry.title: Review Arcade: On the Human Alignment and Gameability of LLM Reviews

author.name: Hans Ole Hatzel, Sebastian Steindl, Jan Strich

entry.summary: Empirically evaluates LLM-generated peer reviews against human reviews using 2025 ACL Rolling Review papers, finding limited and prompt-dependent alignment. It also examines how authors might game reviews through iterative LLM-assisted drafting.

entry.title: Provably Secure Agent Guardrail

author.name: Benlong Wu, Weiming Zhang, Kejiang Chen, Han Fang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Proposes an executable Proof-Constrained Action framework using a neural-symbolic isolation paradigm to give agents deterministic security lower bounds against semantic decoupling attacks. It moves beyond empirical semantic guardrails toward provable safety constraints.

entry.title: When and How Human Curation Backfires: Preference Alignment under Multi-Model Self-Consuming Loop

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiukun Wei, Xueru Zhang

entry.summary: Extends self-consuming training analysis to a multi-model regime where models train on each other's outputs, formalizing when human curation helps or backfires for preference alignment. It shows curation effects differ from the single-model collapse setting studied previously.

entry.title: DeepTool: Scaling Interleaved Deliberation in Tool-Integrated Reasoning via Process-Supervised Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yang He, Xiao Ding, Bibo Cai, Yufei Zhang, Kai Xiong, Zhouhao Sun, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Proposes DeepTool, a framework that scales deliberate interleaved thinking across thinking-action-observation turns in tool-integrated reasoning using process-supervised reinforcement learning with adversarial perturbations. It addresses sparse outcome rewards that fail to supervise intermediate tool invocations.

entry.title: NICE: A Theory-Grounded Diagnostic Benchmark for Social Intelligence of LLMs

author.name: Yunjin Qi, Zhaojun Jiang, Xuan Wu, Hanxi Pan, Yixuan Wang, Yanfang Liu, Xiang Ji, Churu Yu, Chunyuan Zheng, Yingze Chen, Jie He, Liuqing Chen, Zaifeng Gao

entry.summary: NICE introduces a theory-grounded diagnostic benchmark for social intelligence of LLMs, built on a psychometrically validated framework of 4 categories and 11 dimensions developed via expert review. It enables fine-grained diagnosis of social abilities relevant to companionship and customer service applications.

entry.title: From XXLTraffic to EvoXXLTraffic: Scaling Traffic Forecasting to Sensor-Evolving Networks

author.name: Du Yin, Hao Xue, Arian Prabowo, Shuang Ao, Flora Salim

entry.summary: This work introduces the XXLTraffic dataset family spanning up to 27 years of California and NSW traffic data, and EvoXXLTraffic, a sensor-evolving reorganization with yearly active sensors and graph snapshots. It defines a yearly streaming forecasting protocol that reflects real growing road-sensor networks.

entry.title: OptSkills: Learning Generalizable Optimization Skills from Problem Archetypes via Cluster-Based Distillation

author.name: Haochen Yang, Ke Zhao, Mengyuan Ma, Xingyu Lu, Xiangfeng Wang, Hong Qian

entry.summary: OptSkills is an archetype-centric skill learning agent for optimization modeling that clusters problems by underlying archetypes rather than surface narratives, exploring diverse modeling paradigms to improve generalization. It addresses sensitivity to narrative variations in LLM-based optimization formulation.

entry.title: Make LLM Learn to Synthesize from Streaming Experiences through Feedback

author.name: Zhenlin Hu, Yan Wang, Zhen Bi, Zihao Xue, Bingyu Zhu, Longtao Huang, Xiongtao Zhang, Zeyu Yang, Zhixuan Chu, Jungang Lou

entry.summary: StreamSynth introduces a setting where synthesis tasks arrive sequentially and SynLearner enables LLMs to accumulate reusable synthesis experience across a task stream rather than generating data independently per task. It addresses whether models can learn to synthesize from accumulated feedback.

entry.title: AgentSchool: An LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Simulation for Education

author.name: Yulei Ye, Wenhao Li, Zhong Wen, Yunshu Huang, Yichen Hu, Zifan Wei, Yige Wang, Xinyu Xie, Haoxuan Yang, Yanjun Huang, Ruijia Li, Hong Qian, Yu Song, Bo Jiang, Bingdong Li, Lijun Li, Bo Zhang, Pinlong Cai, Xingcheng Xu, Shuangye Chen, Xia Hu, Liang He, Aimin Zhou, Jingjing Qu, Jing Shao, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: AgentSchool is an LLM-driven multi-agent education simulator modeling learning as state transition rather than persona-conditioned role-play, aiming to validate pedagogical interventions without slow, ethically constrained real-world trials. It avoids structurally penalizing the institutional novelty that reform requires.

entry.title: Locally Coherent, Globally Incoherent: Bounding Compositional Incoherence in Multi-Component LLM Agents

author.name: Anany Kotawala

entry.summary: This single-author work formalizes locally-coherent-but-globally-incoherent failures in multi-component LLM agents via a compositional residual measuring distance from the joint coherent polytope, with a product-structure dichotomy and a hierarchical projection that deterministically repairs incoherence. It bounds when local coherence suffices for global coherence.

entry.title: Tiny but Trusted: Efficient Vision-Language Reasoning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiaona Zhou, Muntasir Wahed, Tianjiao Yu, Constantin Brif, Ismini Lourentzou

entry.summary: This work builds VisAnomBench, a time-series anomaly benchmark augmented with high-quality anomaly explanations selected from large VLMs via task-specific rewards, then fine-tunes a small VLM (VisAnomReason) to produce grounded, interpretable anomaly decisions. It addresses the lack of natural-language rationales in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: GenesisFunc: Multi-Agent Data Generation for Accurate and Generalizable Function-Calling

author.name: Hao-Xiang Xu, Chong Deng, Jiaqing Liu, Wen Wang, Qian Chen, Lujia Bao, Xiangang Li, Zhen-Hua Ling

entry.summary: GenesisFunc is an automated multi-agent pipeline for generating function-calling training data starting from reliable tools in public benchmarks, producing diverse multi-turn conversations with quality control. It addresses unreliable APIs, limited tool scalability, and weak quality control in existing synthetic FC data pipelines.

entry.title: How Consistent Are LLM Agents? Measuring Behavioral Reproducibility in Multi-Step Tool-Calling Pipelines

author.name: Abel Yagubyan

entry.summary: This paper empirically measures behavioral reproducibility of LLM tool-calling agents, checking whether identical invocations yield the same tools, order, and arguments. It addresses a practical reliability gap in production agent deployments with structured tool interfaces.

entry.title: Balancing Multimodal Learning through Label Space Reshaping

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Weijie Zhang, Yuanhao Gao, Han Miao, Yongjian Deng, Hao Chen

entry.summary: This paper addresses modality imbalance in multimodal learning via label space reshaping, arguing that learning-pace discrepancies arise from differing mapping difficulty between modality features and the shared label space. The approach avoids penalizing the strong modality unlike prior compensation methods.

entry.title: A Minimal Bifurcation Model of Load Imbalance in a Softmax Mixture-of-Experts Router

author.name: O. M. Kiselev (Innopolis University, Innopolis, Russia)

entry.summary: This paper proposes a minimal dynamical model of softmax routing load imbalance in a two-expert Mixture-of-Experts layer, derived as a mean-field limit. It shows a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation explaining the emergence of expert imbalance under feedback.

entry.title: Toward Ethical Facial Age Estimation: A Generalized Zero-Shot Benchmark Without Training on Children's Data

author.name: Caio Petrucci, Leo Sampaio Ferraz Ribeiro, Sandra Avila

entry.summary: This work proposes a generalized zero-shot benchmark for facial age estimation that explicitly excludes children's data during training while still evaluating on younger populations. It introduces standardized age-group splits with strict separation to address ethical and privacy concerns.

entry.title: AliMark: Enhancing Robustness of Sentence-Level Watermarking Against Text Paraphrasing

author.name: Yuexin Li, Wenjie Qu, Linyu Wu, Yulin Chen, Yufei He, Tri Cao, Bryan Hooi, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AliMark, a sentence-level text watermarking method that reframes detection as bit-sequence encoding and alignment to resist structural paraphrasing attacks like sentence splitting and merging. It uses a two-stage detection with restructured text variants.

entry.title: MOOSE-Copilot: A Web-Based Interactive Assistant for Unified Exploratory and Fine-Grained Scientific Hypothesis Discovery

author.name: Hongran An, Zonglin Yang

entry.summary: Presents MOOSE-Copilot, a web-based interactive assistant unifying exploratory ideation and fine-grained refinement in LLM scientific hypothesis discovery through a formalized human-AI interaction protocol. Structured expert signals like blueprints and feedback outperform autonomous baselines.

entry.title: Source-Grounded Semantic Reinforcement Learning for Low-Resource Target-Language Generation

author.name: Zeli Su, Ziyin Zhang, Zewei Pan, Zhou Liu, Dingcheng Huang, Dehan Li, Zhankai Xu, Longfei Zheng, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes SG-SRL, which converts abundant high-resource source-language monolingual data into cross-lingual semantic supervision for low-resource target-language generation via reference-free RL with a cross-lingual reranker reward. It addresses verbosity-based reward hacking that the approach initially induces.

entry.title: GUITestScape: Towards Open-set Evaluation on Exploratory GUI Testing

author.name: Xiaoyi Chen, Yifei Gao, Yang Xu, Xingxing Song, Yi Zhang, Jitao Sang

entry.summary: Presents GUITestScape, an interactive open-set benchmark over 61 real Android apps and 508 preset defects covering both interaction and display defects for exploratory GUI testing by MLLM agents. It moves beyond single end-state judgments to capture distinct failure modes.

entry.title: Selection Hyper-heuristics Can Automatically Adjust the Learning Period to Optimally Solve Pseudo-Boolean Problems

author.name: Benjamin Doerr, Pietro S. Oliveto, John Alasdair Warwicker

entry.summary: Proves how to automatically set the learning-period parameter of the Random Gradient selection hyper-heuristic so it selects the optimal neighbourhood size for nearly all iterations when optimizing LeadingOnes. It relieves users from manually tuning this novel parameter.

entry.title: Projectional Decoding: Towards Semantic-Aware LLM Generation

author.name: Boqi Chen, Jos\'e Antonio Hern\'andez L\'opez, Aren A. Babikian

entry.summary: Proposes projectional decoding, a framework that maintains a partial graph model alongside generated text to enforce domain semantics during LLM code/artifact generation. Aims to bridge generation with semantic validation in software engineering.

entry.title: Representation Signatures and Risk-Feedback Alignment in LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Weicheng Xue

entry.summary: Studies behavioral alignment and representation dynamics of LLM trading agents using the TradeArena testbed, finding measurable pre-failure signatures like planning-embedding drift and effective-rank contraction before drawdowns. Suggests representations predict failures under market stress.

entry.title: Feature Geometry of LoRA Adapters: A Sparse Autoencoder Analysis of Representational Divergence in Fine-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Prasanth K K

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoders and a delta-activation framework to analyze the representational geometry of LoRA adapters in fine-tuned language models, comparing learned feature spaces across LoRA ranks with pretrained SAE dictionaries. Investigates how fine-tuning diverges from base representations.

entry.title: Sequential Physics-Constrained Neural Operator Forward Modeling for the $\textit{Norne}$ Reservoir System

author.name: Clement Etienam, Juntao Yang, Oleg Ovcharenko, Nick Luiken, Tsubasa Onishi, Nefeli Moridis, Issam Said

entry.summary: Develops a physics-constrained neural-operator framework for sequential surrogate modeling of three-phase black-oil reservoir dynamics on the Norne benchmark, with detailed functional-analytic theory and covariate-shift analysis. Emphasizes Fourier neural operators and physics-informed variants.

entry.title: Learning Robust and Task-Invariant Functional Representation from fMRI through Siamese Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Jiyao Wang, Peiyu Duan, Nicha C. Dvornek, Lawrence H. Staib, Denis Sukhodolsky, Pamela Ventola, James S. Duncan

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight Siamese self-supervised framework for learning robust, task-invariant functional representations from fMRI, mitigating overfitting from small samples and noisy psychiatric labels without expensive foundation-model pretraining. Demonstrates value for neurological-condition analysis.

entry.title: Designing Active Tether-Net Systems for Space Debris Capture with Graph-Learning-Aided Mixed-Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Feng Liu, Achira Boonrath, Gishnu Madhu, Eleonora M. Botta, Souma Chowdhury

entry.summary: Designs active tether-net systems for space-debris capture using graph-learning-aided mixed-combinatorial optimization over continuous, integer, and categorical design variables. Addresses limitations of binary encoding for highly nonlinear multimodal engineering optimization.

entry.title: Ensemble Score Filtering for Real-Data Energy Consumption Forecast Correction

author.name: Ruoyu Hu, Dahai Yu, Feng Bao, Guang Wang, Guannan Zhang

entry.summary: Applies ensemble score filtering for sequential correction of real energy-consumption forecasts, treating a pretrained black-box spatio-temporal model as the state propagator in a high-dimensional data-assimilation procedure. Handles partial, noisy, or delayed measurements.

entry.title: Bridging Chemists and AI: An Expert-Augmented Framework for Interpretable Route Evaluation

author.name: Yujia Guo, Mikhail Kabeshov, Tat Hong Duong Le, Samuel Genheden, Marco V. Mijangos, Varvara Voinarvoska, Giulia Bergonzini, Ola Engkvist, Samuel Kaski

entry.summary: Proposes an expert-augmented, data-driven scoring framework that combines a DeepSets model trained on tree edit distance with chemists' domain knowledge to evaluate multi-step synthetic routes interpretably. It matters for medicinal and process chemistry where route selection affects cost and feasibility.

entry.title: Deep Adaptive Dimension Reduction for Bayesian Inference in Inverse Problems

author.name: Yueyang Wang, Xili Wang, Kejun Tang, Xiaoliang Wan, Tao Zhou, Chao Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a deep adaptive dimension-reduction Bayesian inference framework using variational flows combining VAE-based nonlinear reduction with dual normalizing flows for high-dimensional PDE inverse problems. Aims for flexible posterior approximation with tighter ELBO.
