entry.title: A Novel Tensor Product-Based Neural Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Qihong Yang, Yangtao Deng, Qiaolin He, Shiquan Zhang

entry.summary: TPNet constructs PDE solutions as linear combinations of tensor-product basis functions integrated into the network with coefficients found by least-squares, bypassing gradient training, plus block time-marching. A novel architecture for efficient PDE solving.

entry.title: From Short Histories to Long Futures: Horizon-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Long Horizon Forecasting

author.name: Zesheng Liu, Maryam Rahnemoonfar

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-horizon graph neural network emulator that learns state-to-state transitions from one current time to multiple future lead times in a unified model to combat error accumulation in long-horizon geophysical forecasting. Aims for stable decade-scale rollouts.

entry.title: MIC: Maximizing Informational Capacity in Adaptive Representations via Isotropic Subspace Alignment

author.name: Dang Hong Nguyen, Nhi Ngoc-Yen Nguyen, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: MIC optimizes multi-granular nested embeddings via isotropic subspace alignment, using soft collapse and spectral isotropy regularization plus self-distillation to mitigate redundancy and spectral collapse. Improves Matryoshka-style elastic representations.

entry.title: An End-to-End PyTorch Interface for Differentiable PDE Solvers: A RANS Model-Correction Study

author.name: Luca Saverio (MONHADE), Michele Alessandro Bucci (MONHADE), Gianmarco Farro (MONHADE), C\'edric Content (MONHADE), Denis Sipp (MONHADE)

entry.summary: This work presents an end-to-end differentiable PyTorch interface for PDE solvers, reformulating PDEs as implicit layers to enable gradient-based inverse problem solving and model correction. It is demonstrated on RANS turbulence closure modeling within a fully differentiable workflow.

entry.title: Three-dimensional Conditional Diffusion Models for Cosmological 21 cm Lightcone Emulation

author.name: Bin Xia, John H. Wise

entry.summary: This work applies three-dimensional conditional diffusion models to emulate cosmological 21cm lightcones, handling the harder 3D setting with small micro-batches and highly skewed voxel distributions. It conducts controlled comparisons across preprocessing, compression, architecture depth, and training duration.

entry.title: Kernel-based potential mean-field games with unbiased random Fourier $U$-statistics

author.name: Yumiharu Nakano

entry.summary: This paper studies a subclass of potential mean-field games where costs are expressed via kernel maximum mean discrepancy penalties, using unbiased random Fourier U-statistics for linear-cost estimation. It proves almost-sure convergence and explicit rates for a neural-network-parametrized drift trained by SGD.

entry.title: SAHG: Sector-Anisotropic Hyperbolic Graph Model for Social Bot Detection

author.name: Hanning Lu, Yingguang Yang, Jinwei Su, Yang Liu, Zhaoqian Yao, Yaoming Li, Taoran Liang, Ziyi Zhang, Ran Ran, Kefu Xu, Bin Chong

entry.summary: SAHG is a sector-anisotropic hyperbolic graph model for social bot detection that addresses Euclidean distortion of scale-free social graphs and the unreliability of relational evidence against LLM-driven bots. It uses adaptive anisotropic curvature to assign varying geometric resolution to structural directions with different densities.

entry.title: Enhancing LLM Medical Coding with Structured External Knowledge

author.name: Yidong Gan, David D. Nguyen, Yang Lin, Peter Zhong, Thanh Vu, Long Duong, Yuan-Fang Li

entry.summary: RAG-Coding is a training-free agentic method for medical coding that augments LLMs with the ICD tabular list as a knowledge graph plus distilled guideline summaries. It introduces MDACE-2025 expert re-annotations under updated ICD guidelines.

entry.title: Can Hallucinations Be Useful? Solving Multi-Hop Questions With SLMs By Chaining System-I/II Reasoning

author.name: Saptarshi Sengupta, Suhang Wang

entry.summary: This work argues that for small language models, the think-first-then-retrieve strategy is unnecessary and that hallucinations can actually help converge on correct multi-hop answers. It inverts the standard pipeline by chaining System-I and System-II reasoning.

entry.title: Cultural Fidelity in English-to-Hindi Translation: A Preservation-Fluency Frontier for Gender Recoverability

author.name: Samyak Savi, Chavi Gupta, Shreyas Gantayet, Tanay Sodha, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: This work studies cultural fidelity in English-to-Hindi translation, focusing on preserving recoverability of gender cues that ergative and honorific constructions often erase. It introduces a 37K-instance benchmark and inference-time interventions including a Source-Aware Reranker.

entry.title: UniMaia: Steering Chess Policies with Language for Human-like Play

author.name: Sherman Siu (University of Waterloo), Lesley Istead (University of Waterloo)

entry.summary: UniMaia steers a frozen Lc0-based chess policy network with natural language using a parameter-efficient text encoder and ControlNet-style conditioning. It adds semantic controllability to strong domain policies without large multimodal training.

entry.title: KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, and KMMAU: Agent-Driven Korean Speech Benchmarks for Evaluating SpeechLMs

author.name: Haechan Kim, Seungjun Chung, Inkyu Park, Jihoo Lee, Jonghyun Lee

entry.summary: This work introduces three agent-driven Korean speech benchmarks (KVoiceBench, KOpenAudioBench, KMMAU) and two human-agent frameworks for constructing them, addressing English-centric SpeechLM evaluation. It preserves language-specific instructions and paralinguistic properties that naive transfer corrupts.

entry.title: KSAFE-MM: A Multimodal Safety Benchmark via Localized Contextualization for Korean Cultural Risks

author.name: Yongwoo Kim, Sojung An, Yunjin Park, Jungwon Yoon, Dujin Lee, HyunBeom Cho, Jaewon Lee, Wonhyuk Lee, Youngchol Kim, JeongYeop Kim, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: KSAFE-MM is a Korean multimodal safety benchmark covering both general risks and culture-specific vulnerabilities, split into globally-shared (KSAFE-MM-G) and culture-specific (KSAFE-MM-C) parts. It addresses English-centric and culturally-generic limitations of current MLLM safety tools.

entry.title: Risk-aware Selective Prompting for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuang Huang, Yafeng Zhang, Yu Zilan

entry.summary: This study analyzes when verification prompting helps mitigate hallucinations in vision-language models, finding it is a risk-bearing intervention that helps hard inputs but can harm easier ones. It proposes risk-aware selective prompting and links the behavior to attention shifts from visual to instruction tokens.

entry.title: Building Community-Centred NLP Resources for Puno Quechua

author.name: Elwin Huaman, Adrian Gamarra Lafuente, Johanna Cordova, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: This paper builds the first dedicated ASR resources for Puno Quechua, an under-resourced language, including the largest single-variety Quechua speech corpus (66 hours), the first systematic ASR benchmark, and open-released fine-tuned models. The corpus was collected via participatory community design.

entry.title: CIRF: Tokenizing Chain-of-Thoughts into Reusable Functional Units for Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Yukyung Lee, Yumeng Shen, Jinhyeong Park, Hyein Yang, Jun-Hyung Park

entry.summary: CIRF performs implicit chain-of-thought by tokenizing reasoning into reusable discrete functional units, assigning a functional token per coherent reasoning step from explicit traces. The model is fine-tuned to autoregressively generate functional tokens for efficient latent reasoning aligned with explicit rationales.

entry.title: FABSVer: Faster Training and Better Self-Verification for LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haihui Pan, Junwei Bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang Song

entry.summary: FABSVer fuses solution generation and self-verification into a single generation pass for mathematical reasoning, reducing training overhead. It also identifies and addresses a convergence bottleneck where the reward plateaus due to a fixed reference model.

entry.title: Sense Representations Are Inducible Interfaces

author.name: Jan Christian Blaise Cruz, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: ACROS induces an explicit sense pathway into a frozen pretrained decoder LM via gated residual addition, enabling sense representations without pretraining sense structure in. The same induced variables support zero-shot word-sense disambiguation, low-KL lexical steering, and cross-lingual adaptation.

entry.title: VLMs May Not Globally Enhance Human Alignment over LLMs During Natural Reading

author.name: Jinzhou Wu, Zhengwu Ma, Jixing Li, Baoping Tang, Zitong Lu

entry.summary: This study compares tightly matched LLM and VLM pairs under text-only conditions to isolate whether multimodal training makes text representations more human-like during natural reading, using fMRI and eye-tracking data. It finds vision-language pretraining may not confer a uniform global advantage in human alignment.

entry.title: Agentic Separation Logic Specification Synthesis

author.name: Tarun Suresh, David Korczynski, Julien Vanegue

entry.summary: Presents Spec-Agent, an agentic system for synthesizing validated formal separation-logic specifications across large C++ codebases, targeting a ladder of specification languages with systematic validation. It tackles a hard, real-world program verification problem. Matters for automated software verification and refactoring.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content

author.name: Ruoqi Guo, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Yiheng Xiong, Yuekang Li, Ying Zhang, Leo Yu Zhang, Lida Zhao, Ji Jie, Yuxiao Lu

entry.summary: Presents MIRAGE, a pipeline that injects context-aware adversarial prompts into user-generated content regions of mobile screenshots to attack GUI agents without modifying the app or OS. It exploits agents' inability to separate trusted UI from untrusted content. Matters for GUI agent security.

entry.title: Cultural Binding Heads in Language Models

author.name: Avrile Floro, Luca Benedetto

entry.summary: Uses mechanistic interpretability to identify 2-3 mid-layer attention heads per model that causally drive cultural binding (associating cultural items with appropriate identities) across eight models, showing knockout reduces binding strength and that heads transfer from instruct to base. It links cultural difference-awareness to pretraining. Matters for cultural fairness and interpretability.

entry.title: GeRaF: Neural Geometry Reconstruction from Radio Frequency Signals

author.name: Jiachen Lu, Hailan Shanbhag, Haitham Al Hassanieh

entry.summary: Presents GeRaF, the first neural implicit method for near-range 3D geometry reconstruction from radio frequency signals, with filter-based rendering, physics-based RF volumetric rendering, and modeling of specular reflections. It addresses RF's lensless, noisy, see-through-occlusion nature. Matters for RF-based sensing and reconstruction.

entry.title: ParCo-SDF: Learning Prior-Free Partial-to-Complete Signed Distance Fields of Deformable Objects

author.name: Deokmin Hwang, Minseok Song, Daehyung Park

entry.summary: Formulates multimodal agent memory as an Action-World Interaction Loop and introduces WorldMemArena to evaluate writing, maintenance, retrieval, and use of memory in long-horizon multimodal agents tracking an evolving world. It enables comparing hand-designed pipelines with self-managing memory. Matters for benchmarking agent memory rigorously.

entry.title: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents

author.name: Tianpeng Bu, Xin Liu, Qihua Chen, Hao Jiang, Shurui Li, Hongtao Duan, Lu Jiang, Lulu Hu, Bin Yang, Minying Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GUI-RobustEval with 1,216 executable test cases measuring error recovery across realistic error modes, plus Robustness-driven Trajectory Synthesis creating 800k training examples via a tree-based pipeline discovering errors and recovery steps, yielding improved RoTS-7B and RoTS-32B GUI agents. It addresses agents' inability to recover from their own errors. Matters for deployable robust GUI agents.

entry.title: Mitigating State Aliasing in Vision-Language-Action Models via Inverse Dynamics Learning

author.name: Kyujin Lee, Injae Kim, Jihwan Park, Yejun Ju, Minseok Joo, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: This paper addresses state aliasing in Vision-Language-Action models, where VLM representations fail to distinguish visually similar states requiring different actions. It uses inverse dynamics learning to explicitly shape the vision encoder for low-level control.

entry.title: Fairness Beyond Demographics: Optimizing Performance Across Appearance-Based Hidden Cohorts in Medical Imaging

author.name: Milad Masroor, Cuong Nguyen, Kevin Wells, Gustavo Carneiro

entry.summary: This paper proposes label-free hidden-cohort fairness training for medical imaging, optimizing performance across appearance-based latent subgroups rather than visible demographic attributes. It aims to uncover deeper sources of model error and scale where demographic subgroups are sparse.

entry.title: Veda: Scalable Video Diffusion via Distilled Sparse Attention

author.name: Shihao Han, Hao Yang, Xinting Hu, Xiaofeng Mei, Yi Jiang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Veda is a distilled sparse attention framework for scalable video diffusion that formulates tile selection as explicit reconstruction from full attention, showing alignment with full-attention geometry matters more than sparsity ratio. It uses a hardware-efficient tile-skipping kernel for aggressive sparsity.

entry.title: Deep Binarized Photonic Reservoir Computing for Ultrafast Multimedia Signal Processing

author.name: Muhammad Waqar Iqbal, Mohamad Alassir, Nicolas Marsal, Damien Rontani

entry.summary: Presents a deep photonic reservoir computing architecture using binary optical modulation, random-medium scattering, and CMOS photodetection to process multimedia signals at gigabit-per-second rates. It reports state-of-the-art performance on video, image, and speech tasks for this paradigm.

entry.title: We Should Study the Analogy Between Inoculation Prompting Non-Robustness, Negation Neglect, and Backdoor Non-Robustness

author.name: Vladimir Ivanov

entry.summary: Proposes studying the analogy between non-robustness of inoculation prompting, negation neglect, and backdoor non-robustness as instances of a shared phenomenon, arguing transfer of findings could improve inoculation prompting robustness. It connects three reward-hacking and training-related failure modes.

entry.title: Atomically precise mechanosynthesis of carbon structures on hydrogenated Si(100) by inverted-mode STM

author.name: Matrice Jacobine

entry.summary: Reports demonstration of atomically precise mechanosynthesis of carbon structures on hydrogenated Si(100) using inverted-mode STM, achieving simultaneous spatial and chemical control over fabrication. It advances atomically precise nanoscale manufacturing.

entry.title: Diagnosing Harmful Continuation in Answer-Correct Long-CoT Training Traces

author.name: Chen He, Yuhao Wu, Lei Wang, Wenxuan Zhang, Fumin Shen

entry.summary: Studies harmful post-conclusion continuation in answer-correct long chain-of-thought SFT data, showing that removing reasoning that continues after a sufficient answer improves fine-tuning outcomes. It uses a delete-only editor to construct answer-preserving suffix removal.

entry.title: DeepSurvey: Enhancing Analytical Depth and Citation Reliability in Automated Survey Generation

author.name: Ziyue Yang, Da Ma, Hanqi Li, Zijian Wang, Tiancheng Huang, Zijian Hu, Chenrun Wang, Yunzhe Zhang, Xiaobao Wu, Kai Yu, Lu Chen

entry.summary: Presents DeepSurvey, an agentic automated survey-generation system that extracts structured keynotes from full texts, models cross-paper relationships, integrates code-repository analysis, and uses citation-graph expansion for reliable grounding. It improves analytical depth and citation reliability over abstract-reliant systems.

entry.title: Battery-Sim-Agent: Leveraging LLM-Agent for Inverse Battery Parameter Estimation

author.name: Jiawei Chen, Xiaofan Gui, Shikai Fang, Shengyu Tao, Shun Zheng, Weiqing Liu, Jiang Bian

entry.summary: Introduces Battery-Sim-Agent, the first framework deploying an LLM agent in closed loop with a high-fidelity battery simulator to solve inverse parameter estimation by forming physics-grounded hypotheses. It reframes black-box optimization as a reasoning task mimicking a scientist's workflow.

entry.title: Citation-Closure Retrieval and Per-Rule Attribution for Real-World Regulatory Compliance Question Answering

author.name: Yeong-Joon Ju, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: This work formalizes regulatory compliance QA with RegOps-Bench (an operational knowledge graph from national R&D regulations) and proposes RefWalk, a framework for citation-closure retrieval and per-rule attribution. It addresses traceability needs across multi-tiered authority structures that standard RAG handles poorly.

entry.title: Persona Conditioning of Brand Recommendations in Retrieval-Augmented Commercial Chat: A Prominence-Stratified Cross-Provider Audit

author.name: Will Jack, Noah Lehman, Keller Maloney, Sarah Xu

entry.summary: This audit measures how strongly user-persona context reshapes which brands LLM assistants recommend in retrieval-augmented commercial chat, sampling 2,000 runs across personas, prompts, and model configurations from OpenAI and Anthropic. It finds prefixing a persona significantly drops recommendation-set similarity.

entry.title: Continuity and Ordinality Matter: Constraining Time Series Tokens for Effective Time Series Analysis with Large Language Models

author.name: Musheng Li, Ziying Zhang, Cheng jin, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: COM proposes continuity- and ordinality-aware geometric constraints for time series token embeddings in TS-LLMs, addressing the overlooked numeric properties of time series tokens. The method improves token-based time series LLM performance across benchmarks.

entry.title: LoRe: Adaptive Interaction-Evaluation Routing with Per-Step Interaction Budgets for Iterative Graph Solvers

author.name: Jintao Li, Yong-Yi Wang, Zheng-An Wang, Heng Fan

entry.summary: LoRe is a training-free inference-time wrapper for diffusion-based combinatorial optimization solvers that budgets per-step interaction evaluations, dynamically routing compute to high-conflict interactions. Inspired by many-body physics, it improves scalability on problems like Maximum Independent Set.

entry.title: Causal Label Recovery in Payment Networks

author.name: Gaurav Dhama

entry.summary: This paper formalizes fraud-detection label bias in payment networks as a sequential missing-data problem with three propensity stages plus a corruption layer, and constructs a Sequential Triply Robust estimator to recover causal labels. It seeks to achieve a previously proven minimax detection bound.

entry.title: SURGENT: A Surgical Multi-Agent Assistance System Across the Perioperative Workflow

author.name: Dongsheng Shi, Yue Li, Xin Yi, Yongyi Cui, Huawei Feng, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: SURGENT is a surgical multi-agent assistance system combining a Tree-of-Thought planner, multi-department collaboration agents, and retrieval-augmented reasoning over clinical guidelines and literature. It addresses LLM limitations in surgical applications like input length, memory, and traceability.

entry.title: SkillBrew: Multi-Objective Curation of Skill Banks for LLM Agents

author.name: Wentao Hu, Zhendong Chu, Yiming Zhang, Junda Wu, Ming Jin, Xiangyu Zhao, Yilei Shao, Yanfeng Wang, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: Introduces SkillBrew, framing skill bank curation for LLM agents as a constrained multi-objective Pareto-aware optimization balancing usefulness, diversity, and query coverage. It addresses inefficient append-only skill repositories that accumulate redundant or harmful entries.

entry.title: COMET: Concept Space Dissection of the Modality Gap in Audio-Text Multimodal Contrastive Embeddings

author.name: Yonggang Zhu, Liting Gao, Aidong Men, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: Introduces COMET, a concept-space dissection of the modality gap in audio-text contrastive embeddings (CLAP), challenging the cone-effect explanation and examining information imbalance and dimensionality collapse. It analyzes why correcting mean embeddings alone yields limited improvement.

entry.title: Before the Shutter: Aesthetic and Actionable Portrait Photography Planning in 3D Scenes

author.name: Ruixiang Jiang, Chang Wen Chen

entry.summary: Introduces 3D aesthetic portrait planning, generating pose, camera, lighting, and exposure plans for compelling portraits within a 3D scene using a Photographic Scene Graph of affordances. Shifts focus from 2D post-production editing to pre-capture planning.

entry.title: A Triple-Modal Contrastive Learning Framework with Sequence, Graph, and 3D Features for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction

author.name: Le Xu, Xi Zhang, Dan Luo, Ting Wang, Xuan Lin

entry.summary: TriMod-DTI is a triple-modal contrastive learning framework integrating 1D sequences, 2D graphs, and 3D structures of drugs and proteins for drug-target interaction prediction. Incorporates often-overlooked 3D structural features.

entry.title: Ridge Regression from Poisson Resetting: A Renewal Perspective on Spectral Regularization

author.name: Petar Jolakoski

entry.summary: Connects stochastic resetting from non-equilibrium physics to ridge regularization, showing Poisson resetting of linear gradient flow yields exactly the ridge estimator and extending this to general renewal reset laws. Offers a renewal-process perspective on spectral regularization.

entry.title: RightNow-Arabic-0.5B-Turbo: An Open Sub-1B Arabic Language Model via Vocabulary Injection and Edge-First Deployment

author.name: Jaber Jaber, Osama Jaber

entry.summary: RightNow-Arabic-0.5B-Turbo is a 518M-parameter Arabic-specialized decoder LLM built on Qwen2.5-0.5B via vocabulary injection of 27K Arabic tokens, continued pretraining, and instruction tuning for edge deployment. It targets the gap between multilingual sub-1B models that neglect Arabic and large server-bound Arabic models.

entry.title: TraceCodec: A Compiler-Backed Neural Codec for Stateful Multi-Flow Network Traffic Traces

author.name: Junhui Ding, Xinchen Zhang, Xiaohui Xie, Shinan Liu

entry.summary: TraceCodec is a compiler-backed neural codec for synthesizing stateful multi-flow network traffic traces, identifying the direct decode-to-raw-fields interface as the bottleneck in prior packet generators. It lifts packets into timed packet actions with explicit flow slots to avoid post-hoc heuristic repair.

entry.title: PAST2HARM: A Simple Adaptive Past Tense Attack for Jailbreaking Multimodal AI

author.name: Snehasis Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: PAST2HARM is an adaptive jailbreak framework that exploits past-tense reformulations to bypass refusal training in multimodal text-to-image models. It uses temporal deepening with historical anchoring to erode refusal boundaries across models.

entry.title: Learning to Translate from Soft to Hard LLM Prompts

author.name: Pitipat Kongsomjit, Suryansh Goyal, Jacob Whitehill

entry.summary: This paper trains a model to translate soft prompts into natural-language prompts, improving both interpretability and translation quality over training-free methods. It suggests soft prompts optimized on small models could be ported to larger ones.

entry.title: MERIT: Matching Expertise via Rubric-Informed Training for Reviewer Assignment

author.name: Zixuan Yang, Yibo Zhao, Weicong Liu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: MERIT is a two-stage framework for reviewer assignment that converts criterion-level expertise matching into scalable suitability supervision, training a reviewer assessor via RL with LLM-judge rewards guided by paper-specific rubrics. It targets the gap between general relatedness and true reviewer suitability.

entry.title: ESC-Skills: Discovering and Self-Evolving Skills for Emotional Support Conversations

author.name: Jie Zhu, Huaixia Dou, Shuo Jiang, Junhui Li, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang, Fang Kong

entry.summary: ESC-Skills is a skill-centric framework for emotional support conversations that discovers and self-evolves executable support skills by modeling localized interactions as Intervention Units capturing state-action-outcome dynamics. It builds a bank of executable skills from successful and failed dialogues.

entry.title: Integrated and Cross-Architecture Interpretation of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Leonardo Matthew Yauw, Wei-Bin Kou, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: The IAR framework provides integrated cross-architecture interpretation of LLM reasoning, combining bandwidth-calibrated Mutual Information Peak with Tukey IQR peak-detection to isolate reasoning-crucial tokens and overlap analysis with Deep-Thinking Ratio tokens. It unifies multiple probes to avoid underestimating inferential structure.

entry.title: Prompting Is All You Need: Multi-view Prompting Large Language Models for Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Nils Constantin Hellwig, Niklas Donhauser, Jakob Fehle, Udo Kruschwitz, Christian Wolff

entry.summary: LLM-MvP adapts the multi-view principle of considering multiple element orderings to LLM prompting for aspect-based sentiment analysis, combining schema-constrained decoding with a context-free grammar and prefix batching. It achieves performance competitive with or superior to fine-tuned approaches.

entry.title: When Confidence Misleads: Suffix Anchoring and Anchor-Proximity Confidence Modulation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jungwon Park, Jimyeong Kim, Jungmin Ko, Nojun Kwak, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: This paper studies when model confidence misleads position selection in diffusion language model decoding, identifying that EOT tokens can get high confidence causing incomplete generation and that suffix anchors introduce local overconfidence. It proposes suffix-anchored confidence modulation to improve non-autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: The Harder Text Embedding Benchmark (HTEB): Beyond One-dimensional Static Robustness

author.name: Manuel Frank, Haithem Afli

entry.summary: HTEB argues embedding robustness is multidimensional and introduces a dynamic evaluation that stochastically transforms inputs along lexical/stylistic, length, and language axes using an LLM. It evaluates 16 open-weight embedding models across 42 languages with human-validated transformations.

entry.title: The Cases LJP Never Sees: Prosecution Decision Prediction for More Complete Criminal Liability Assessment

author.name: Junyu Lu, Qi Wei, Peishuo Zheng, Jie Zhang, Hui Huang, Qianru Wang, Chuan Xiao, Jianbin Qin, Shuyuan Zheng

entry.summary: This paper proposes Prosecution Decision Prediction, a new legal AI task built around prosecutorial review that classifies cases into prosecution or three non-prosecution outcomes, filling a blind spot in legal judgment prediction. It captures cases LJP never sees, such as insufficient evidence or exempted guilt.

entry.title: Measuring Form and Function in Language Models

author.name: H\'ector Javier V\'azquez Mart\'inez, Charles Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces quantitative child-language-acquisition metrics to evaluate LLMs on formal syntactic and functional discourse properties of English determiners, proposing a Contextual Alternative Choice prompting method. It enables direct comparison of models against children and established statistical benchmarks.

entry.title: Skill-Conditioned Gated Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Jiazhen Huang, Xiao Chen, Xiao Luo, Yong Dai, Senkang Hu, Yuzhi Zhao

entry.summary: SGSD reformulates skill-based on-policy self-distillation as teacher hypothesis validation rather than unconditional imitation, handling potentially irrelevant or misleading retrieved skills. It retrieves skill-mistake pairs, builds a multi-teacher pool, and gates which skill-conditioned teachers supervise the student.

entry.title: Soro: A Lightweight Foundation Model and Chatbot for Tajik

author.name: Stanislav Liashkov, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Azizjon Azimi, Khushbakht Shoymardonov, Shuhratjon Khalilbekov, Bonu Boboeva

entry.summary: Soro is a family of lightweight Tajik-specialized conversational LLMs built from Gemma 3 via Tajik-only continual pretraining on a 1.9-billion-token corpus and instruction tuning. It introduces and open-sources Tajik benchmarks covering general knowledge, linguistic competence, and exam domains for a low-resource language.

entry.title: Long Live the Librarian! A Persistent Search Sub-Agent for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Software Engineering Systems

author.name: Seunghyuk Cho, Sunghyun Choi, Jaeseung Heo, Youngbin Choi, Saemi Moon, MoonJeong Park, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: Identifies redundant output tokens as the dominant energy cost in multi-agent software engineering systems and proposes Librarian, a persistent search sub-agent that tracks repository-search history to suppress redundant re-exploration. It reports output tokens cost 30-1000x more energy than cached tokens. Matters for sustainable, efficient multi-agent coding systems.

entry.title: SNARE: Adaptive Scenario Synthesis for Eliciting Overeager Behavior in Coding Agents

author.name: Yubin Qu, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Yanjun Zhang, Yuekang Li, Ying Zhang, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SNARE, an adaptive scenario synthesis pipeline that composes benign tasks to elicit overeager out-of-scope behavior in coding agents that complete tasks while quietly exceeding authorized scope. It addresses a gap missed by both task-completion and jailbreak benchmarks. Matters for coding agent safety.

entry.title: Interpretability-Guided Layer Selection over Subspace Projection: SAEs as Stethoscopes, Not Scalpels, for Raw Task Vector Model Editing

author.name: Li Lei, Madalina Ciobanu, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: Rigorously evaluates an SAE-guided model editing pipeline for math reasoning on Gemma-3-4B and uncovers that projecting task vectors onto SAE feature subspaces acts as an information bottleneck discarding ~97% of modification energy with no significant gains. It argues SAEs are better diagnostic stethoscopes than editing scalpels. Matters for realistic expectations of SAE-based interventions.

entry.title: LoMo: Local Modality Substitution for Deeper Vision-Language Fusion

author.name: Feng Han, Zhixiong Zhang, Zheming Liang, Yibin Wang, Jiaqi Wang

entry.summary: LoMo identifies carrier sensitivity in VLMs, where replacing a text question with its rendered-image counterpart causes large performance drops due to asymmetric text/image roles in training data. It proposes local modality substitution to encourage deeper vision-language fusion.

entry.title: REST3D: Reconstructing Physically Stable 3D Scenes from a Single Image

author.name: Xiaoxuan Ma, Jiashun Wang, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Yehonathan Litman, Kris Kitani

entry.summary: REST3D reconstructs physically stable 3D scenes from a single RGB image, producing simulation-ready assets that avoid object floating and penetration. It balances matching the input image with physical plausibility unlike prior methods reliant on strong scene priors.

entry.title: ARC's "Outperforming Random Sampling" explained

author.name: mfatt

entry.summary: Provides an intuitive explainer of ARC's 'Competing with Random Sampling' work, which reframes the goal of mechanistic interpretability around what explanations are actually needed for rather than vague reverse-engineering aims. It aims to make ARC's formalism accessible.

entry.title: The Importance of Out-of-Band Metadata for Safe Autonomous Agents: The Redpanda Agentic Data Plane

author.name: Tyler Akidau, Tyler Rockwood, Johannes Br\"uderl, Marc Millstone

entry.summary: Presents the Redpanda Agentic Data Plane, an architecture using out-of-band metadata channels to carry access policies and data classifications that autonomous agents cannot reliably propagate themselves. It addresses enterprise security risks of agents acting as digital employees.

entry.title: Better Later Than Sooner: Neuro-Symbolic Knowledge Graph Construction via Ontology-grounded Post-extraction Correction

author.name: Lorenzo Loconte, Timothy Hospedales, Cristina Cornelio

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic knowledge-graph construction method that performs ontology-grounded correction after LLM extraction to enable reliable SQL-like querying for multi-hop and symbolic QA. It improves over textual graph-based RAG that lacks structure for symbolic operations.

entry.title: DenseSteer: Steering Small Language Models towards Dense Math Reasoning

author.name: Yang Ouyang, Shuhang Lin, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces DenseSteer, a training-free inference-time steering method that modulates small models' internal representations toward dense reasoning patterns (fewer but more information-dense steps). It improves small-model math reasoning without increasing token usage.

entry.title: ConMoE: Expert-Pool Consolidation via Prototype Reassignment for MoE Compression

author.name: Yilun Yao, Jiaming Pan, Elsie Dai, Peizhuang Cong, Yaoming Li, Tong Yang

entry.summary: Introduces ConMoE, a training-free post-training MoE compression method that consolidates the expert pool by remapping each original expert to a smaller set of retained prototypes while preserving the router interface. It reduces memory footprint without retraining.

entry.title: Opt-Verifier: Unleashing the Power of LLMs for Optimization Modeling via Dual-Side Verification

author.name: Haoyang Liu, Jie Wang, Boxuan Niu, Xiongwei Han, Yian Xu, Mingxuan Ye, Zijie Geng, Fangzhou Zhu, Tao Zhong, Mingxuan Yuan, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: Proposes Opt-Verifier, an LLM-based optimization-modeling framework with dual-side verification checking both structural rationality of constraints/variables and solution validity. It improves the reliability and accuracy of automated mathematical optimization model generation.

entry.title: TRACE: Toulmin-based Reasoning Assessment through Constructive Elements for LLM CoT Evaluation

author.name: Yundong Kim, Heyoung Yang

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a metric that evaluates chain-of-thought reasoning structure by integrating Toulmin's argumentation theory with Flavell's metacognitive framework rather than judging final answers. It correlates strongly with benchmark accuracy and works as a reinforcement signal.

entry.title: BitTP: The Lightweight Trajectory Prediction Model with BitLLM for Edge-Devices

author.name: Mincheol Kang, Hyunjin Lim, Bomin Kang, Daehee Park

entry.summary: BitTP converts an LLM-based trajectory predictor into a lightweight bitlinear architecture using 1.58-bit weight-only quantization for deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in autonomous systems. It demonstrates extreme compression while preserving trajectory prediction capability.

entry.title: From GPS Points to Travel Patterns: Flexible and Semantic Trajectory Generation with LLMs

author.name: Silin Zhou, Chenhao Wang, Yuntao Wen, Shuo Shang, Lisi Chen, Panos Kalnis

entry.summary: HTP hierarchically generates travel patterns first and then GPS points using LLMs, rather than directly generating points, to synthesize realistic and flexible-length urban trajectories while mitigating privacy risks. It addresses limitations of fixed-length, single-condition trajectory generation.

entry.title: PrismFlow: Residual Dynamics for Flow Matching in Time-Series Generation

author.name: Junru Zhang, Lang Feng, Jinbo Wang, Xu Guo, Yucheng Wang, Han Yu, Min Wu, Yabo Dong, Duanqing Xu

entry.summary: PrismFlow introduces residual dynamics into flow matching for time-series generation, addressing how a single global vector-field estimator over-smooths heterogeneous temporal regimes. It targets multimodal, multiscale signals with oscillations and high-frequency variation.

entry.title: Toward User Preference Alignment in LLM Recommendation via Explicit Context Feedback

author.name: Weizhi Zhang, Wooseong Yang, Yuxin Cui, Zhaohui Guo, Hins Hu, Liangwei Yang, Henry Peng Zou, Qifei Wang, Hanqing Zeng, Jiayi Liu, Yinglong Xia, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: This paper proposes aligning LLM recommendations with user preferences using explicit textual context feedback (comments, reviews) rather than only implicit signals like clicks. It aims to reduce misaligned preferences and filter bubbles by capturing semantic reasons behind user choices.

entry.title: UA-Legal-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Ukrainian Legal Reasoning

author.name: Volodymyr Ovcharov

entry.summary: UA-Legal-Bench is a five-task benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Ukrainian legal reasoning, built from one of the world's largest open judicial corpora (99.5M decisions). It addresses the English-centrism of legal NLP benchmarks and evaluates 11 LLMs from 3B to 675B.

entry.title: SCOPE: A Lightweight-training LLM Framework for Air Traffic Control Readback Monitoring

author.name: Qihan Deng, Minghua Zhang, Yang Yang, Zhenyu Gao

entry.summary: Introduces SCOPE, a lightweight-training LLM framework for monitoring air traffic control pilot readbacks, where anomalies are implicated in roughly 80% of aviation incidents. It targets generalization across variable controller-pilot phraseology under deployment constraints.

entry.title: A unified deeplearning framework for contrast-phase-specific virtual monochromatic imaging

author.name: Antony Jerald, Hemant K Aggarwal, Brian Nett, Avinash Gopal, Phaneendra K Yalavarthy, Bipul Das, Rajesh Langoju

entry.summary: Proposes a unified deep learning framework that synthesizes contrast-phase-specific virtual monochromatic 50 keV images from single-energy CT by conditioning on contrast phase priors. It aims to deliver dual-energy CT benefits without dual-energy hardware.

entry.title: Mitigating Stethoscope-Induced Shortcuts in Respiratory Sound Classification under Federated Domain Generalization with Causality-Inspired Interventions

author.name: Heejoon Koo, Yoon Tae Kim, Miika Toikkanen, June-Woo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a causality-inspired federated domain generalization framework for respiratory sound classification that mitigates stethoscope-induced shortcuts via content-preserving style interventions and counterfactual augmentation. It targets robust deployment across heterogeneous and unseen recording devices.

entry.title: xModel-KD: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for 3D Scene Perception using LiDAR

author.name: Thenukan Pathmanathan, Kanchan Keisham, Thangarajah Akilan

entry.summary: Presents xModel-KD, a cross-modal knowledge distillation framework transferring 2D image cues to LiDAR point-cloud segmentation to reduce reliance on dense 3D annotations. Targets annotation scarcity and single-modality limitations in 3D scene perception.

entry.title: STAP: A Shuffle-Tokenized App Predictor with Ultra Long Context for Vocabulary-Free Mobile App Prediction

author.name: Chengyu Fan, Hang Liu

entry.summary: STAP predicts the next mobile app launch without a fixed vocabulary by shuffling app identities to virtual indices and compensating with ultra-long-context behavioral sequences, enabling cross-ecosystem generalization. Addresses cold-start and vocabulary-free app prediction.

entry.title: Q-ANCHOR: Federated Quantum Learning with ZNE-guided Correction

author.name: Hoang M. Ngo, Quan Nguyen, Wanli Xing, My T. Thai

entry.summary: Q-ANCHOR is a quantum federated learning framework that analyzes FedAvg's persistent error floor from quantum hardware bias under non-IID data and adds zero-noise-extrapolation-guided correction. Addresses the double-drift problem on noisy quantum hardware.

entry.title: Adapting Automotive Aerodynamics Surrogates to New Vehicle Families via Transfer Learning

author.name: Seunghwan Keum, Alok Warey

entry.summary: This paper studies transfer learning for automotive aerodynamics CFD surrogates, adapting a 61M-parameter Transformer pretrained on four vehicle families to a held-out fifth with only 20 samples. It compares full finetuning, lightweight finetuning, and LoRA, finding geometry encoders learn transferable representations across topologically distinct shapes.

entry.title: Manifold-based Algorithms for the Hadamard Decomposition

author.name: Nicolas Gillis, Subhayan Saha, Stefano Sicilia, Arnaud Vandaele

entry.summary: This paper develops manifold-based algorithms for the Hadamard decomposition, factorizing a matrix into the element-wise product of two low-rank matrices that can be more expressive than truncated SVD. It provides theoretical reformulations and Riemannian optimization methods.

entry.title: BrahmicTokenizer-131K: An Indic-Capable Drop-In Replacement for o200k_base

author.name: Rohan Shravan

entry.summary: BrahmicTokenizer-131K is a 131K-vocabulary byte-level BPE tokenizer that closes the Brahmic-script compression gap while preserving English, EU-language, and code compression of OpenAI's o200k_base. It is built via script pruning and surgical retrofit of dead vocabulary slots as a drop-in replacement.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Subspace Decoupling ViT for Mitigating Multi-Task Negative Transfer in Histological Scoring

author.name: Youhan Huang, Jiajun Li, Yilin Fang, Shuai Wang, Chuheng Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes a subspace-decoupled multi-task Vision Transformer with orthogonality-constrained task-specific adapters to mitigate negative transfer in NAFLD histological scoring. It constructs independent feature subspaces for steatosis, ballooning, and inflammation and provides a curated mouse NAFLD dataset.

entry.title: EVL-ECG: Efficient ECG Interpretation With Multi-Aspect Heterogeneous Knowledge Distillation

author.name: Dang Hong Nguyen, Nhi Ngoc-Yen Nguyen, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: EVL-ECG is a cross-architecture heterogeneous knowledge distillation framework for efficient ECG interpretation, transferring cardiac diagnostic logic from massive foundation models to edge-deployable models. It introduces multi-head cross-attention alignment and optimal-transport-based feature transfer to preserve spatio-temporal ECG dependencies.

entry.title: Privacy-Enhanced Zero-Order Federated Learning via xMK-CKKS over Wireless Channels

author.name: Anthony Ayli, Khalil Harris, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad

entry.summary: Privacy-Enhanced Zero-Order Federated Learning proposes a four-phase protocol enabling multi-key homomorphic encryption aggregation over shared wireless channels, providing stronger client-level security than single-key schemes. It combines zero-order optimization with xMK-CKKS for privacy-preserving over-the-air federated learning.

entry.title: OralAgent: Integrating Reasoning, Tools, and Knowledge for Interactive Dental Image Analysis

author.name: Jing Hao, Siyuan Dai, Yongxin Zhang, Yuci Liang, Jiamin Wu, Jiahao Bao, Yuxuan Fan, Zanting Ye, Yanpeng Sun, Xinyu Zhang, Ming Hu, Liang Zhan, James Kit Hon Tsoi, Linlin Shen, Junjun He, Kuo Feng Hung

entry.summary: OralAgent is a dental-specialized AI agent unifying multimodal reasoning, tool use, and knowledge retrieval, integrating 22 visual tools and 368 dental textbooks. It also introduces the OralCorpus knowledge resource for automated dental image analysis.

entry.title: BioELX: Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking via Alias-based Retrieval and LLM Ranking

author.name: Yi Wang, Corina Dima, Liangyu Zhong, Steffen Staab

entry.summary: BioELX is a two-stage cross-lingual biomedical entity linking framework requiring no task-specific training, enriching SapBERT with Wikidata multilingual aliases and using LLM reranking. It improves linking of non-English biomedical mentions to knowledge base identifiers.

entry.title: ChildEval: When large language models meet children's personalities

author.name: Yanyan Luo, Xue Han, Chunxu Zhao, Ruiqiao Bai, Yaxing Zhang, Qian Hu, Lijun Mei, Junlan Feng

entry.summary: ChildEval is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to infer and follow child-centered preferences in long-context conversations, with 29K synthesized persona profiles of children aged 3-6. Preferences may align, conflict, or be independent of personas, expressed explicitly or implicitly.

entry.title: FinBoardBench: Benchmarking Dynamic Wealth Management and Strategic Financial Reasoning of LLMs via Board Game Simulations

author.name: Xuesi Hu, Peng Wang, Jinpeng Miao, Xilin Tao, Caiwei Li, Yue Ma, Jie He, Qiancheng Zhang, Yuntao Zou, Dagang Li

entry.summary: FinBoardBench evaluates dynamic wealth management and strategic financial reasoning of LLMs using three classic board games (Cashflow, Acquire, Monopoly). It assesses cash-flow management, investment forecasting, and competitive negotiation, revealing gaps in 9 advanced LLMs.

entry.title: BenGER: Benchmarking LLM Systems on Subsumption-Based Legal Reasoning in German Law

author.name: Sebastian Nagl, Ann-Kristin Mayrhofer, Martin Heidebach, Aleyna Ko\c{c}ak, Anne Zettelmeier, Elly Breu, Angelina Greiner, Sofija Milijas, Matthias Grabmair

entry.summary: BenGER is a benchmark for subsumption-based legal reasoning in German law, with exam-style free-text case tasks and doctrinal reasoning tasks. It evaluates 12 LLM systems against timed human baselines using a cross-validated rubric-aligned LLM-as-judge framework.

entry.title: Why We Need Speech to Evaluate Speech Translation

author.name: Maike Z\"ufle, Danni Liu, Vil\'em Zouhar, Jan Niehues

entry.summary: This work argues that text-based metrics cannot evaluate speech-specific phenomena like speaker gender, prosody, and emphasis in speech translation. It trains SpeechCOMET quality-estimation models with speech encoders and finds even speech-access metrics fail to consistently assess such phenomena, diagnosing three causes.

entry.title: PrunePath: Towards Highly Structured Sparse Language Models

author.name: Zhexuan Gu, Zixun Fu, Yancheng Yuan

entry.summary: PrunePath is a budget-adaptive structured sparsification framework for FFN layers built on MoEfication, replacing independent expert thresholding with softmax-normalized routing and a cumulative-mass threshold. It provides a single-checkpoint inference-time sparsity knob with hardware-friendly efficiency gains.

entry.title: Mobile-Aptus: Confidence-Driven Proactive and Robust Interaction in MLLM-based Mobile-Using Agents

author.name: Zheng Wu, Pengzhou Cheng, Zongru Wu, Yuan Guo, Tianjie Ju, Aston Zhang, Gongshen Liu, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: Mobile-Aptus proposes a confidence-driven framework for MLLM-based mobile agents to mitigate both over-execution (attempting unsolvable tasks) and over-soliciting (excessive human intervention). It integrates confidence signals to decide when to act autonomously versus request help.

entry.title: GraphLit: Learning Text-Enriched Dynamic Character Network Representations for Literary Study

author.name: Gaspard Michel, Elena V. Epure, Romain Hennequin, Christophe Cerisara, Mirella Lapata

entry.summary: GraphLit introduces Dynamic Heterogeneous Character Networks that organize novels into temporally localized graphs aligning characters with textual context, and a self-supervised masked graph autoencoder framework. Trained on ~20,000 networks from Project Gutenberg, it improves over text-only and graph-only baselines on 12 character-related literary tasks.

entry.title: Reverse Probing: Supervised Token-level Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models in Clinical Text

author.name: Bushi Xiao, Sarvesh Soni, Daisy Zhe Wang

entry.summary: Reverse Probing is a supervised token-level uncertainty quantification framework for clinical summarization that estimates uncertainty from pre-existing labeled summaries rather than sampling new outputs. It treats text as a probe into model internal activations across four categories and outperforms baselines on two expert-annotated datasets.

entry.title: Human Label Variation as Stable Signal: Learning Annotator-Specific Explanation Behavior via Cross-Annotator Preference Optimization

author.name: Beiduo Chen, Pingjun Hong, Ziyun Zhang, Benjamin Roth, Anna Korhonen, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: This paper studies whether LLMs can learn and reproduce annotator-specific label-explanation behavior, treating human label variation as stable signal. It finds individual patterns are weak per-annotation but detectable after aggregation, and proposes cross-annotator preference optimization to model them.

entry.title: Knowing When to Ask: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for LLM Tool Use

author.name: Abhijit Kumar, Zoey Wu, Mohit Suley

entry.summary: Introduces CARL, a competence-aware RL method that trains a critic on the model's own rollouts to learn segment-level credit for when tool calls help versus when parametric knowledge suffices. It addresses the failure of trajectory-level rewards to isolate useful tool calls. Matters for efficient and accurate LLM tool use.

entry.title: MIRA: A Bilingual Benchmark for Medical Information Response Audit

author.name: Mengyu Xu, Qiaoxin Yang, Qianqian Wang, Xiwei Dai, Weiyi Wu, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces MIRA, a bilingual benchmark auditing whether LLMs provide comparable medical information across user phrasing, register, and health literacy signals, finding low-literacy phrasings get more omissions. It exposes equity gaps in health information delivery. Matters for fair medical AI.

entry.title: Learn from Weaknesses: Automated Domain Specialization for Small Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Suji Kim, Kangsan Kim, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: Introduces LearnWeak, an annotation-free specialization framework that uses a stronger reference agent to identify a small computer-use agent's domain weaknesses, synthesize targeted tasks, and construct supervision automatically. It improves small CUAs more effectively than naive large-scale data synthesis. Matters for practical, cheaper computer-use agents.

entry.title: Embodied3DBench: Benchmarking Low-Level Embodied Spatial Intelligence of Vision Language Models

author.name: Jiyao Zhang, Mingxu Zhang, Yitong Peng, Haoxuan Liu, Chenshuo Wang, Yuxing Long, Haoyang Huang, Dongjiang Li, Nan Duan, Hui Shen, Hao Dong

entry.summary: Introduces Embodied3DBench, a robot-centric benchmark for low-level embodied spatial intelligence of VLMs spanning six task categories across structural understanding and interaction-oriented perception with over 21k QA pairs. It evaluates 13 state-of-the-art models. Matters for assessing VLM readiness for embodied 3D reasoning.

entry.title: Seeing through boxes: Non-Line-of-Sight 3D Reconstruction from Radar Signals

author.name: Jiachen Lu, Hailan Shanbhag, Haitham Al Hassanieh

entry.summary: Tackles non-line-of-sight 3D reconstruction from radar signals inside enclosed environments, leveraging line-of-sight geometry outside the region to stabilize optimization and reduce surface ambiguity in SDF recovery. It improves on prior NLoS neural reconstruction methods. Matters for seeing through occlusions with radar.

entry.title: DMC-CF: Dynamic Multimodal CounterFactual QA benchmark for Causal Reasoning

author.name: Junzhe Zhang, Huixuan Zhang, Guirong Wang, Xingyao Zhang, Pei Liu, Lin Qu, Hu Wei, Xiaojun Wan

entry.summary: Introduces Group Prompting, a training-free paradigm for cell instance segmentation that shifts interactive prompting from per-instance to per-type by exploiting that SAM's frozen encoder already clusters same-type cells, so one click per cell type segments all instances. It makes interactive foundation models tractable for histopathology images with thousands of cells. Matters for efficient pathology segmentation.

entry.title: ReactBench: A Cause-Driven Benchmark for Multimodal Hallucination via Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Shizhe Zhou, Bohan Jia, Kai Wu, Yan Shen, Tongyun Li, Yuyang Wu, Shaohui Lin

entry.summary: ReactBench is a cause-driven benchmark for evaluating multimodal hallucinations in MLLMs, going beyond detecting outcomes to assessing underlying failure causes via adversarial images and hallucination-inducing queries. It uses an exam-style evaluation format across multiple tasks.

entry.title: SuperVoxelGPT: Adaptive and Ordered 3D Tokenization for Autoregressive Shape Generation

author.name: Yuan Li, Congyi Zhang, Xifeng Gao, Xiaohu Guo

entry.summary: SuperVoxelGPT introduces adaptive, deterministically ordered supervoxel tokenization for autoregressive 3D shape generation, resolving the trade-off between set-based representations and redundant voxel grids. It predicts coarse saliency to build a shape-aware token sequence.

entry.title: Train the Agent, Not the Expert: Learning to Harness Heterogeneous Experts for Multi-Turn Visual Reasoning

author.name: Yaowu Fan, Tao Han, Dazhao Du, Andy J. Ma, Jia Wan

entry.summary: VisHarness is a trainable visual agent that learns to orchestrate heterogeneous specialized visual experts (detection, segmentation, counting) rather than solving tasks directly. It decouples high-level reasoning from low-level task execution for general-purpose visual intelligence.

entry.title: FakeVLM-R1: Internalizing Physical Laws via CoT for Synthetic Image Detection

author.name: Leqi Zhu, Junyan Ye, Kaiqing Lin, Zhiyuan Yan, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: FakeVLM-R1 aims to internalize physical laws via chain-of-thought reasoning for synthetic image detection, combining supervised fine-tuning with GRPO reinforcement learning and critical thinking. It targets genuine causal reasoning over imitation learning to reduce explanatory hallucinations.

entry.title: Geometry Matters: 3D Foundation Priors for Learning Semantic Correspondence

author.name: Artur Jesslen, Olaf D\"unkel, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: This work introduces a 3D-aware post-training framework for semantic correspondence that incorporates 3D foundation model priors (SAM3D) to resolve confusions over symmetric sides and repeated parts that 2D features miss. It renders PartField descriptors from reconstructed geometry.

entry.title: Large Depth Completion Model from Sparse Observations

author.name: Zhu Yu, Zhengyi Zhao, Runmin Zhang, Lingteng Qiu, Kejie Qiu, Yisheng He, Siyu Zhu, Zilong Dong, Si-Yuan Cao, Hui-Liang Shen

entry.summary: LDCM is a simple transformer-based Large Depth Completion Model for single-view metric depth estimation from sparse observations, leveraging monocular foundation models and a Poisson-based depth initialization. It outperforms prior methods across diverse datasets and sparsity levels.

entry.title: LiveSVG: Zero-Shot SVG Animation via Video Generation

author.name: Matan Levy, Ran Margolin, Bar Cavia, Dvir Samuel, Yael Pritch, Shmuel Peleg, Alex Rav Acha, Ariel Shamir, Dani Lischinski

entry.summary: LiveSVG is a zero-shot approach for SVG animation using video diffusion models, fitting vector geometry directly to a generated target video via differentiable rendering. It is skeleton-free and handles complex non-rigid deformations that LLM code synthesis and SDS struggle with.

entry.title: Stable-Layers: Fine-Tuning Image Layer Decomposition Models with VLM-Scored Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ciara Rowles, Reshinth Adithyan, Nikhil Pinnaparaju, Vikram Voleti, Mark Boss

entry.summary: Stable-Layers fine-tunes a pretrained image layer-decomposition model using only VLM feedback via Flow-GRPO with LoRA, eliminating the need for paired supervision. It addresses the challenge of VLMs compressing scores into a narrow band with a two-stage structured evaluation pipeline.

entry.title: MonoPhysics: Estimating Geometry, Appearance, and Physical Parameters from Monocular Videos

author.name: Daniel Rho, Jun Myeong Choi, Matthew Thornton, Biswadip Dey, Roni Sengupta

entry.summary: MonoPhysics estimates geometry, appearance, and physical parameters of deformable objects from monocular videos using differentiable MPM simulation and 3D Gaussian Splatting. It introduces visual-physical bridges to resolve scale ambiguity absent in monocular settings.

entry.title: Learning to Feel Materials from Multisensory Tactile Data via Interpretable Models

author.name: Li Zou, Yasemin Vardar

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable computational framework modeling human tactile material perception using multisensory touch data via three linked models mapping interaction features to sensory attributes and material classes. It aims to bridge low-level tactile signals to perceptual representations.

entry.title: Orthogonal Concept Erasure for Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuhao Sun, Lingyun Yu, Haoxiang Xu, Fengyuan Miao, Zhuoer Xu, Hongtao Xie

entry.summary: Presents an orthogonal concept-erasure method for diffusion models that updates neuron directions rather than magnitudes to precisely remove unsafe concepts while preserving generation quality. It addresses limitations of additive-update editing-based erasure approaches.

entry.title: When Models Disagree: Rethinking LLM Evaluation for Public Comment Analysis

author.name: Aisha Najera, Alvin Moon, Vedant Srinivasan, Rajesh Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: Proposes an Interpretive Audit Pipeline that uses multi-model disagreement to flag interpretively complex public comments for human review, analyzing 1,260 USDA docket comments across four LLMs. It argues stance-accuracy evaluation misses divergent categorizations affecting policy.

entry.title: BenchTrace: A Benchmark for Testing Reflection Ability and Controlled Evolution in LLM Agents

author.name: Jiahao Huang, Fei Cheng, Junfeng Jiang, Zefan Yu, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: Introduces BenchTrace, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving LLM agents through a 1,821-episode snapshot-reflection dataset, separately probing reflection quality and whether past failures translate into avoidance behavior. It targets the gap where current evaluation only measures task scores.

entry.title: Rubric-Guided Process Reward for Stepwise Model Routing

author.name: Shenghao Ye, Yu Guo, Zhengheng Li, Shuangwu Chen, Jian Yang

entry.summary: Proposes RoRo, a rubric-guided process-reward framework for stepwise routing of reasoning steps to suitable models, replacing outcome-only rewards with rubric-based process supervision over preference pairs. It improves efficiency and generalization of model routing.

entry.title: VitalAgent: A Tool-Augmented Agent for Reactive and Proactive Physiological Monitoring over Wearable Health Data

author.name: Di Zhu, Yu Yvonne Wu, Hong Jia, Aaqib Saeed, Vassilis Kostakos, Ting Dang

entry.summary: Proposes VitalAgent, a tool-augmented agentic framework for ECG/PPG wearable health data supporting both reactive question answering and proactive monitoring through longitudinal physiological memory. It also introduces VitalBench for longitudinal physiological monitoring evaluation.

entry.title: UI-KOBE: Knowledge-Oriented Behavior Exploration for Lightweight Graph-Guided GUI Agents

author.name: Yuxiang Chai, Han Xiao, Xinyu Fu, Jinpeng Chen, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes UI-KOBE, a framework that improves lightweight on-device mobile GUI agents by building and reusing app-specific graph knowledge to compensate for limited model capacity. It enables more reliable end-to-end planning without large vision-language models.

entry.title: ParaTool: Shifting Tool Representations from Context to Parameters

author.name: Zekai Yu, Qi Meng, Qizhi Chu, Yu Hao, Chuan Shi, Cheng Yang

entry.summary: Proposes ParaTool, which projects tool representations from the context window into model parameters to reduce inference overhead and hallucination as tool catalogs grow. It internalizes previously seen tool details rather than relying on in-context documentation.

entry.title: HiKEY: Hierarchical Multimodal Retrieval for Open-Domain Document Question Answering

author.name: Joongmin Shin, Gyuho Shim, Jeongbae Park, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Proposes HiKEY, a hierarchical tree-based multimodal retrieval framework that elevates document hierarchy to a first-class signal for open-domain document QA over large industrial corpora. It tackles routing failure in locating documents and fragmentation of scattered multimodal evidence like tables and figures.

entry.title: mcp-proto-okn: Natural-language access to open scientific knowledge graphs through the Model Context Protocol

author.name: Peter W. Rose, Benjamin M. Good, Amanda M. Saravia-Butler, Charlotte A. Nelson, James P. Balhoff, Yaphet Kebede, Patricia L. Whetzel, Christopher Bizon, Andrew I. Su, Sergio E. Baranzini

entry.summary: This work presents mcp-proto-okn, a Python Model Context Protocol server enabling AI assistants to discover, inspect, query, and integrate scientific knowledge graphs through natural language, with features like SPARQL execution, ontology expansion, and multi-graph querying. It lowers barriers to cross-domain biomedical knowledge graph analysis.

entry.title: GPF-LiveNews: A Streaming Evaluation Protocol for Group-Conditioned Framing in Large Language Models

author.name: Mohd Ariful Haque, Fahad Rahman, Kishor Datta Gupta, Roy George

entry.summary: GPF-LiveNews introduces a streaming evaluation protocol for auditing group-conditioned framing bias in LLM outputs on fresh news anchors across 42 identity labels. It addresses how static bias benchmarks fail to capture how models frame newly emerging events for different audiences.

entry.title: Pocket-Dentist: On-Device Dental Image Understanding via Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Kai Bian, Xucheng Guo, Bin Chen, Lingyan Ruan, Yiran Shen, Ting Dang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Pocket-Dentist is an efficiency-aware benchmark for on-device dental multimodal QA spanning three datasets, five task types, and seven metrics. It finds that compact 2B-parameter VLMs can outperform larger VLMs in accuracy for privacy-preserving clinical prescreening.

entry.title: DELOS: Detecting Shallow Transits in Kepler Photometry Using a Contrastive-Learning Framework

author.name: Qingtian Liu, Jian Ge, XingChen Yan, Kevin Willis, Xinyu Yao, QuanQuan Hu, Jiapeng Zhu

entry.summary: Presents DELOS, a contrastive-learning framework with GPU-accelerated phase folding to detect shallow planetary transits in Kepler photometry, trained on 20 million synthetic light curves. It targets intermediate-to-long-period exoplanet signals without relying on pre-detected events.

entry.title: Entity-Collision: A Stratified Protocol for Attributing Retrieval Lift in Agent Memory

author.name: Youwang Deng

entry.summary: Proposes entity-collision, a stratified protocol for attributing retrieval lift in agent memory by pinning the BM25 floor (distractors share answer entity tokens) and stratifying queries by tag. It disentangles lexical leakage from embedder contributions in agent-memory benchmarks.

entry.title: REPOT: Recoverable Program-of-Thought via Checkpoint Repair

author.name: Parsa Mazaheri

entry.summary: Introduces RePoT, which augments one-shot Program-of-Thought by deterministically replaying a plan to its first invalid step then resuming with a single LLM call. Achieves modest accuracy gains at minimal extra cost on planning benchmarks.

entry.title: DAMEL: Dual-Axis Multi-Expert Learning for Class-Imbalanced Learning

author.name: Hyuck Lee, Taemin Park, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: Proposes DAMEL, a multi-expert learning method for class-imbalanced long-tailed data that reduces both prediction bias and variance using experts along representation and time axes. Simplifies prior variance-reduction multi-expert procedures.

entry.title: Parallel Adaptive Multi-Objective Evolutionary Learning of Discretized Bayesian Network Classifiers for Clinical Data

author.name: Damy M. F. Ha, Tanja Alderliesten, Peter A. N. Bosman

entry.summary: Improves the multi-objective evolutionary algorithm Baymex for learning discretized Bayesian network classifiers with a parallelization strategy and an overfitting-steering mechanism, evaluating on clinical data. Targets scalability and real-data applicability of interpretable probabilistic models.

entry.title: Probabilistic bias adjustment of seasonal forecasts using generative machine learning: A case study of Arctic sea ice predictions

author.name: Parsa Gooya, Reinel Sospedra-Alfonso

entry.summary: Uses conditional variational generative ML to perform probabilistic bias adjustment of seasonal ensemble forecasts, demonstrated on Arctic sea ice prediction. Aims to reduce computational cost while calibrating forecast biases.

entry.title: NeuroEdge: Real-Time Hand Gesture Recognition with High-Density EMG Using Deep Learning at the Edge

author.name: Peter Chudinov, Zhenyu Lin, Jay Motamarry, Srihita Panati, Xiaorong Zhang, Zhuwei Qin

entry.summary: NeuroEdge implements real-time HD-EMG hand gesture recognition entirely on resource-constrained microcontrollers via custom streaming and lightweight modules. Targets prosthetics and rehabilitation at the edge.

entry.title: Gradient Perturbation: Learning to Perturb Gradients for Adaptive Training

author.name: Hua Li

entry.summary: Establishes a unified framework for gradient perturbation, showing SAM, gradient clipping, and noise injection are special cases, and proposes a learnable perturbation method for adaptive training. Offers a perspective unifying backward-chain perturbations.

entry.title: Open World Autoencoding Drift Detection with Novel Class Recognition in Tabular Non-stationary Data Streams

author.name: Joanna Komorniczak

entry.summary: Proposes an unsupervised concept-drift detection method using autoencoder reconstruction errors for known-class shifts plus density estimation for novel-class recognition in tabular non-stationary streams, with mirrored autoencoders for independent adaptation. Targets open-world streaming learning.

entry.title: A Fully Convolutional Approach to Denoising Structural Dynamics Data from X-Ray Photon Correlation Spectroscopy

author.name: Nisar Nellikunnummel, Andi Barbour, Lutz Wiegart, Tatiana Konstantinova, Anthony DeGennaro

entry.summary: Presents a fully convolutional denoising autoencoder that handles arbitrary input sizes to denoise two-time correlation functions in X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy, trained on NSLS-II beamline data. Recovers dynamical features under low signal-to-noise.

entry.title: TriSearch: Learning to Optimize Triangulations via Bistellar Flips

author.name: Yiran Wang, Guido Mont\'ufar

entry.summary: TriSearch is a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes triangulations of polytopes via bistellar flips using a circuit-supported action representation. It generalizes zero-shot from small to larger instances in 3D and 4D, achieving strong performance on combinatorial geometry objectives.

entry.title: Computational Modeling of Antibody-Antigen Complexes: PLM-Based and MSA-Based Approaches

author.name: Xiao Luo

entry.summary: This thesis investigates why antibody-antigen complex modeling lags general protein-protein interaction prediction, comparing protein language model and MSA-based approaches. It proposes improvements to narrow the persistent accuracy gap for therapeutic antibody design.

entry.title: Audio Deepfake Detection with Half-Truth Localisation Using Cross-Attentive Feature Fusion

author.name: S. Sutharya, Remya K. Sasi

entry.summary: This paper introduces Intrinsic Quality, a validation-free metric estimating a face recognition dataset's potential to produce high-performance models without full training. It combines a neighbor-consistency score for label agreement and effective rank for embedding diversity, enabling rapid dataset diagnosis and curation.

entry.title: StoryMI: Steerable Multi-Agent Therapeutic Dialogue Generation

author.name: Qingyu Meng, Min Chen, Dingming Liu, Yifan Mo, Yue Su, Xin Sun, Koen Hindriks, Jiahuan Pei

entry.summary: StoryMI is a multi-agent framework for controllable motivational interviewing dialogue generation, expanding questionnaire-based client profiles into situational stories and coordinating therapist/client agents via MI codes. It proposes a two-level evaluation with lexical and MI-specific clinical metrics.

entry.title: GRADE: Generalizable Reasoning-Aware Dialogue Evaluation for AI Tutors

author.name: Parth Bhalerao, Jeromy Chang, David Chou, Oana Ignat

entry.summary: GRADE is a systematic study of open-source models for assessing AI tutor pedagogical ability in student-tutor dialogues, evaluating 120 configurations across five models with LoRA, augmentation, and CoT. It finds Gemma3-12B best for single-task and Gemma3-27B-8bit for multitask evaluation.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Approach for Designing Stable and Highly Expressible Low-Immunogenicity Therapeutic mRNA Sequences

author.name: Dhawa Sang Dong, Mausam Gurung, Suraj Kandel

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-stage in-silico framework combining a pretrained CodonTransformer with a genetic algorithm for designing stable, highly expressible, low-immunogenicity therapeutic mRNA sequences. The GA evolves candidates via codon-aware crossover and synonymous mutation guided by human codon usage.

entry.title: Personality, Role, and Expressive Style in Large Language Models: An Interactionist Analysis

author.name: Moe Nagao, Koichiro Terao, Mikio Nakano, Naoto Iwahashi

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the mismatch between specifying Big Five traits in prompts and their actual expression in LLM dialogue from an interactionist perspective. Using a factorial design over personality, dialogue roles, and expressive styles, it shows personality expression is a context-dependent outcome shaped by situational factors.

entry.title: PromptEmbedder:: Efficient and Transferable Text Embedding via Dual-LLM Soft Prompting

author.name: Yu-Che Tsai, Kuan-Yu Chen, Yuan-Hao Chen, Yu-Han Chang, Ching-Yu Tsai, Yu-Hsiang Chuang, Shou-De Lin

entry.summary: PromptEmbedder proposes a dual-LLM framework that decouples text embedding knowledge from backbone weights by using a prompting LLM to generate soft prompts for a frozen embedding LLM. This aims to enable transferability across architectures without costly retraining when new backbones emerge.

entry.title: IFMTBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multilingual Translation Instruction Following

author.name: Mingrui Sun, Mao Zheng, Zheng Li, Mingyang Song

entry.summary: IFMTBench benchmarks multilingual translation instruction following across seven languages, covering single- and multi-constraint items spanning schema preservation, glossaries, context, and register. It addresses the gap left by semantic-fidelity metrics and English-centric instruction benchmarks.

entry.title: When Seekers Are Hard to Help: Evaluating Emotional Support Dialogue Systems in Worst-Case Interactions

author.name: Jiajie Yang, Yangchun Li, Guanyi Chen, Rui Fan, Xin Bai, Tingting He

entry.summary: This paper evaluates emotional support dialogue systems under worst-case interactions where seekers are resistant, low-engagement, or emotionally volatile, contrasting with overly cooperative simulated seekers. It uses an expert simulation study with eight counseling professionals to expose optimistic-evaluation problems.

entry.title: Revisiting Anthropomorphic Reflection Markers in Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Yahan Yu, Noa Nakanishi, Fei Cheng

entry.summary: This paper revisits anthropomorphic reflection markers like wait and hmm in LLM reasoning, examining whether they are necessary for performance. Through prompt- and token-level suppression across four benchmarks and two scales, it finds these markers are not uniformly necessary, with implications for overthinking.

entry.title: HardMTBench: Stress-Testing Chinese-English Translation on Knowledge-Intensive Domains

author.name: Zheng Li, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Tianxiang Fei

entry.summary: HardMTBench is a difficulty-aware Chinese-English translation benchmark for knowledge-intensive domains like finance, healthcare, law, and science, addressing saturation of FLORES-200. It contains 10,000 hand-curated source sentences across 12 domains packaged as 20,000 directional test items.

entry.title: Aligning LLMs with Human Uncertainty: A Beta-Bernoulli Calibrator for LLM Forecasting

author.name: Hui Dai, Ryan Teehan, Parsa Torabian, Mengye Ren

entry.summary: Proposes the Beta-Bernoulli Calibrator that converts a point-estimate LLM forecast into a distribution using supervision from both binary outcomes and aggregated human forecast distributions, capturing crowd agreement. It improves probabilistic forecasting calibration in LLMs. Matters for uncertainty-aware LLM predictions.

entry.title: VCap: Hypergeometric Rewards for Weak-to-Strong Visual Captioning

author.name: Xingyu Lu, Jinpeng Wang, Yi-Fan Zhang, Yankai Yang, Yancheng Long, Yiyang Fan, Xuanyu Zheng, Haonan Fan, Kaiyu Jiang, Tianke Zhang, Changyi Liu, Bin Wen, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao, Han Li, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces VCap, a Witness-Adjudicator reward for visual captioning RL that pairs reference captions with the visual signal to verify factual consistency, providing fine-grained reward signals to reduce hallucination and omission. It improves weak-to-strong captioning via better reward design. Matters for faithful multimodal generation.

entry.title: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution

author.name: Yanqiu Zhao, Dongying Zheng, Kaibo Huang, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang, Linna Zhou

entry.summary: Presents MaskClaw, an edge-side privacy arbitrator for GUI agents that decides Allow, Mask, or Ask on screenshots using local visual evidence and task-specific policy memory before raw screens leave the trusted environment, with behavior-driven skill evolution. It addresses context-dependent privacy that static PII detectors miss. Matters for privacy-preserving GUI agents.

entry.title: Code as a Weapon: A Consensus-Labeled Prompt Bank for Measuring Coding-Model Compliance with Malicious-Code Requests

author.name: Richard J. Young, Gregory D. Moody

entry.summary: Constructs a consensus-labeled prompt bank to measure coding-model compliance with malicious-code requests, separating executable weapon requests from harmful security knowledge to enable comparable refusal-rate measurement. It argues coding-specialized models should clear a higher refusal bar. Matters for coding model safety evaluation.

entry.title: EarthShift: a benchmark for measuring robustness to real-world distribution shifts in Earth observation

author.name: Kelsey Doerksen, Hannah Kerner

entry.summary: Introduces EarthShift, the first public testbed for benchmarking robustness of Earth observation models across realistic distribution shifts including new time periods, geographies, scales, and sensors, evaluating 8 geospatial foundation models. It moves beyond in-distribution generalization. Matters for reliable remote sensing deployment.

entry.title: DefSynUS: Real-time Patient-specific Intrahepatic Vessel Identification via Deformation-Aware CT-US Domain Adaptation

author.name: Karl-Philippe Beaudet (MIMESIS, UNISTRA), Yordanka Velikova (TUM), Sidaty El Hadramy (MIMESIS, Unibas), Nassir Navab (TUM), Philippe Cattin (Unibas), Juan Verde (MIMESIS, UNISTRA, IHU Strasbourg), St\'ephane Cotin (MIMESIS, UNISTRA)

entry.summary: DefSynUS enables real-time patient-specific intrahepatic vessel identification by generating synthetic ultrasound from preoperative CT annotations via physics-based rendering and domain adaptation, robust to tissue deformation. It eliminates the need for preoperative ultrasound in liver surgery.

entry.title: DiffSpot: Can VLMs Spot Fine-Grained Visual Differences in Web Interfaces?

author.name: Linhao Zhang, Aiwei Liu, Yuan Liu, Xiao Zhou

entry.summary: DiffSpot is a code-driven benchmark testing whether VLMs can spot fine-grained visual differences in rendered web interfaces by mutating single CSS properties. It serves as both a diagnostic of fine-grained perception and a practical test for GUI agents.

entry.title: SAFE-Pruner: Semantic Attention-Guided Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Manipulation

author.name: Shilin Ma, Chubin Zhang, Changyuan Wang, Yuji Wang, Yue Wu, Zixuan Wang, Jingqi Tian, Zheng Zhu, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: SAFE-Pruner is a plug-and-play token pruning framework for Vision-Language-Action models that incorporates attention cues from future layers into pruning decisions. It exploits semantic attention consistency across execution steps to avoid discarding tokens needed by deep layers.

entry.title: Native Audio-Visual Alignment for Generation

author.name: Longbin Ji, Guan Wang, Xuan Wei, Chenye Yang, Xiangrui Liu, Zhenyu Zhang, Shuohuan Wang, Yu Sun, Jingzhou He

entry.summary: NAVA is a native audio-visual alignment framework for joint audio-video generation that establishes audio-video correspondence in a dedicated interaction space before semantic conditioning. It avoids weaknesses of dual-tower posterior alignment and fully unified tri-modal designs.

entry.title: AnomalyAgent: Training-Free Agentic Models for Zero-/Few-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yi Zhang, Jiawen Zhu, Lele Fu, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: AnomalyAgent is a training-free agentic framework using MLLM reasoning for zero/few-shot anomaly detection, avoiding the substantial auxiliary-dataset training of prior CLIP-based methods. It adds reasoning to detect complex anomalies requiring contextual understanding.

entry.title: SAM3D-Phys: Towards Multi-Object Interactive Simulation in Real World

author.name: Xin Dong, Weijian Deng, Lihan Zhang, Tianru Dai, Wenfeng Deng, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: SAM3D-Phys recovers complete, simulatable object geometry from real-world multi-view scenes by integrating reconstruction with SAM3D generative 3D priors to fill occlusions. This enables physics-based interaction with objects that are otherwise incomplete and unsuitable for simulation.

entry.title: Ambient-robust Inverse Rendering using Active RGB-NIR Imaging

author.name: Hoon-Gyu Chung, Jinnyeong Kim, Hyunwoo Kang, Seung-Hwan Baek

entry.summary: This work presents ambient-robust inverse rendering using active RGB-NIR imaging, leveraging imperceptible NIR flash to obtain stable shading invariant to ambient light. It combines ambient-lit RGB and NIR-flash images for accurate geometry and reflectance reconstruction.

entry.title: UniNote: A Unified Embedding Model for Multimodal Representation and Ranking

author.name: Jinghan Zhao, Wenwei Jin, Anqi Li, Jintao Tong, Luya Mo, Jiawei Li, Bin Li, Yao Hu

entry.summary: UniNote is a unified multimodal embedding model for industrial item-to-item retrieval that combines global representation with fine-grained local retrieval and merges embedding-and-ranking into one pipeline. It targets efficiency and precision trade-offs in content platforms.

entry.title: Decoupled Thrust-Axis Attitude Control Using Quaternions for Chandrayaan-3 Lunar Landing Mission

author.name: Aditya Rallapalli, Suraj Kumar, Rijesh M P, Ashok Kumar Kakula, Bharat Kumar GVP
