entry.summary: Describes a quaternion-based decoupled thrust-axis attitude control approach used in the Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing mission, aligning the thrust axis with required acceleration while constraining rotation about that axis. It documents the navigation, guidance, and control design behind a successful soft landing.

entry.title: AI #170: Lack of Executive Order

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI roundup covering the cancellation of a planned US AI executive order, Illinois SB 315 (a SB 53 variant with third-party auditing), and analysis of the Magnifica Humanitas document. It synthesizes recent AI policy developments and commentary.

entry.title: Tailoring the Curriculum: Student-Centered Reasoning Distillation via Dynamic Data-Model Compatibility

author.name: Jiahao Huang, Fei Cheng, Junfeng Jiang, Akiko Aizawa

entry.summary: Proposes a Data-Model Compatibility metric that jointly considers data quality, difficulty, and student capability to select training data for reasoning distillation to smaller models. It shows DMC correlates with distillation performance and improves outcomes when used for data selection.

entry.title: Entropy-KL Divergence-based Token Masking: A Novel Approach for Selective Fine-tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Qi Liu, Mingdi Sun, Yongyi He, Zhi Zheng, Tong Xu, Yi Zheng, Zhefeng Wang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes an entropy-KL divergence-based token-masking method for selective fine-tuning that focuses SFT on task-relevant tokens to avoid distribution shift before RL in low-data regimes. It aims to preserve exploration capacity for subsequent RL training.

entry.title: Xetrieval: Mechanistically Explaining Dense Retrieval

author.name: Zhixin Cai, Jun Bai, Yang Liu, Jiaqi Li, Yichi Zhang, Taichuan Li, Zhuofan Chen, Zixia Jia, Zilong Zheng, Wenge Rong

entry.summary: Proposes Xetrieval, an embedding-level mechanistic framework that explains dense-retriever relevance scores beyond lexical matches, including a lightweight reasoning internalizer approximating chain-of-thought in embedding space. It aims to reveal latent factors shaping retrieval behavior.

entry.title: No Reader Left Behind: Multi-Agent Summaries Everyone Can Understand

author.name: Jimin Jung, MyoungJin Kim, Jaehyung Seo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: NRLB is a multi-agent plain-language summarization framework simulating three reader groups (elementary students, non-native readers, readers with attention deficits) and combining template-based planning with iterative reader-oriented refinement. It targets accessibility barriers in line with the US Plain Writing Act.

entry.title: GrowLoop: Self-Evolving Conversation Evaluation Seeded by Human

author.name: Yihang Lin, Yunze Gao, Zeyang Lin, Dongbo Li, Kun Peng, Chenglong Song, Yue Liu

entry.summary: GrowLoop is a self-evolving framework for evaluating conversational human-likeness, seeded by human judgments and adapting as model capability and expectations evolve. It addresses the tacit, evolving nature of human-likeness criteria.

entry.title: TIMEGATE: Sustainable Time-Boxed Promotion Gates for Continual ML Adaptation Under Resource Constraints

author.name: Abhijit Chakrabroty, Suddhasvatta Das, Kevin A. Gary, Yash Shah

entry.summary: TIMEGATE is a policy layer for sustainable continual ML adaptation that budgets time, labeling, training, and evaluation, emitting a metric-availability signal for partial-vs-full evaluation decisions. It achieves substantial evaluation-compute savings without silent mis-promotions across tabular and LLM fine-tuning settings.

entry.title: Beyond MSE: Improving Precipitation Nowcasting with Multi-Quantile Regression

author.name: Gijs van Nieuwkoop, Siamak Mehrkanoon

entry.summary: Reformulates deterministic precipitation nowcasting as multi-quantile regression using pinball loss to better capture heavy rainfall versus smoothing pointwise losses. Reports an 8.6 percent MSE reduction with SmaAt-UNet over the Netherlands.

entry.title: Learning to Perturb Hidden Representations for Generalizable Deep Learning

author.name: Hua Li

entry.summary: Establishes a unified framework for hidden-activation perturbation, showing Dropout, Manifold Mixup, and adversarial feature perturbation are instances, and conjectures expansive vs contractive perturbations act as positive/negative augmentation. Companion to the gradient-perturbation paper by the same author.

entry.title: Fairness-Aware Federated Learning with Trajectory Shapley Value

author.name: Daniel Kuznetsov, Ziqi Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Trajectory Shapley Value, a contribution metric for federated learning that evaluates how each client influences the global model's optimization trajectory using a validation-based temporally consistent utility. The resulting FedTSV adaptive aggregation aims to improve fairness and stability over fixed-weight schemes.

entry.title: Syllabic-Structure Decoder for Automatic Speech Recognition in Vietnamese

author.name: Nghia Hieu Nguyen, Quan Ngoc Hoang, Long Hoang Huu Nguyen, Kiet Van Nguyen, Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Syllabic-Structure Decoder for Vietnamese ASR that models speech at the phoneme level to explicitly capture syllabic phonological composition. It generates valid syllabic structures from a compact phonemic inventory instead of large orthographic vocabularies.

entry.title: LegalGraphRAG: Multi-Agent Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Legal Reasoning

author.name: Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Zhishang Xiang, Zhimin Wei, Linfeng Gao, Xiao Huang, Zhihong Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: LegalGraphRAG is a multi-agent graph RAG framework for legal reasoning that handles heterogeneous, multi-granular legal corpora and adds verification for transparent evidence-based reasoning. It structures cases, articles, and interpretations distinctly to improve retrieval accuracy.

entry.title: Beyond One Path: Evaluating and Enhancing Divergent Thinking in Interactive LLM Agents

author.name: Jihyeong Park, Ingeol Baek, Jeonghyun Park, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: MUTATE is an interactive benchmark evaluating agentic divergent thinking at path-level (multiple alternative paths to a goal) and action-level (non-typical mechanism-shifting object uses). It scores both completed paths and off-path attempts, revealing structural blind spots in frontier LLMs' creative reasoning.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Multilingual LLMs-as-a-Judge: An Empirical Study

author.name: Irune Zubiaga, Aitor Soroa, Rodrigo Agerri

entry.summary: This empirical study explores strategies for building reliable multilingual LLM-as-a-judge evaluators across high, mid, and low-resource languages (English, Spanish, Basque). It analyzes instruction translation, monolingual versus multilingual supervision, and model size, with and without in-domain fine-tuning data.

entry.title: Revealing Algorithmic Deductive Circuits for Logical Reasoning

author.name: Phuong Minh Nguyen, Tien Huu Dang, Naoya Inoue

entry.summary: Uses mechanistic interpretability to localize attention heads responsible for individual logical reasoning steps under symbolic-aided chain-of-thought prompting, characterizing information transfer among heads. It probes whether LLMs genuinely understand abstract algorithmic reasoning. Matters for understanding reasoning circuits.

entry.title: MemCog: From Memory-as-Tool to Memory-as-Cognition in Conversational Agents

author.name: Zihan Li, Xingyu Fan, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Proposes MemCog, shifting agent memory from Memory-as-Tool one-shot retrieval to Memory-as-Cognition with a navigable memory store, associative link graphs, and proactive reasoning-driven traversal. It integrates memory access into the reasoning process. Matters for long-term conversational agents.

entry.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: Targeted Routing Hijacking in Federated RAG

author.name: Junjie Mu, Qiongxiu Li

entry.summary: Introduces Routing Hijacking, an attack on federated RAG where a malicious client forges its semantic profile to attract target queries despite holding irrelevant data, causing misrouting and downstream failures. It reveals a new attack surface in privacy-preserving federated retrieval. Matters for secure FedRAG deployment.

entry.title: GraphSteal: Structural Knowledge Stealing from Graph RAG via Traversal Reconstruction

author.name: Jinze Gu, Qinghua Mao, Xi Lin, Jun Wu

entry.summary: Presents GraphSteal, a structure-oriented reconstruction attack that turns Graph RAG systems into structural oracles, recovering substantial portions of hidden knowledge graphs through adaptive black-box interactions. It exposes a privacy attack surface unique to structured retrieval. Matters for Graph RAG security.

entry.title: Personal Visual Memory from Explicit and Implicit Evidence

author.name: Viet Nguyen, Thao Nguyen, Vishal M. Patel, Yuheng Li

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark and VisualMem architecture for personal visual memory targeting both explicit (recurring user-associated entities) and implicit (latent user facts from visual cues) evidence that text-only memory systems miss. It moves beyond text-centric memory benchmarks. Matters for truly multimodal personalized agents.

entry.title: WorldMemArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agent Memory Through Action-World Interaction

author.name: Chengzhi Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Sophia Xiao Pu, Yepeng Liu, Lin Long, Yichen Guo, Nuo Chen, Zhaotian Weng, Elena Kochkina, Simerjot Kaur, Charese Smiley, Xiaomo Liu, James Zou, Sheng Liu, Yuheng Bu, Songyou Peng, Xin Eric Wang

entry.summary: Introduces DMC-CF-Static, a large-scale real-world video benchmark for multimodal causal counterfactual reasoning, addressing prior datasets being small or built from synthetic and cartoon sources. It probes whether MLLMs truly understand causal relationships beyond statistical learning. Matters for evaluating causal reasoning in multimodal models.

entry.title: Orthogonal Negative Guidance in Attention Feature Space for Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Jungmin Ko, Jungwon Park, Jimyeong Kim, Changin Choi, Wonseok Lee, Wonjong Rhee

entry.summary: Proposes Orthogonal Negative Guidance, a training-free method operating in the attention output space of MM-DiT text-to-image transformers that orthogonalizes negative-prompt features against positive features and subtracts only the orthogonal component for explicit concept suppression. It improves removal without degrading image quality. Matters for controllable T2I generation.

entry.title: AgentCVR: Active Multi-Agent Cross-Video Reasoning via Script-Simulated Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yilun Qiu, Jiahe Wang, Cilin Yan, Jiayin Cai, Xiaolong Jiang, Yao Hu, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: AgentCVR is a multi-agent framework for cross-video reasoning treating it as active evidence acquisition, with a Master Agent coordinating Visual and Audio Agents. It introduces Script-Simulated RL for efficient policy training without expensive rollouts.

entry.title: S2MDF: A Plug-And-Play Layer for Intersection-Free Multi-Object Signed Distance Fields

author.name: Deniz Sayin Mercadier, Federico Stella, Aurel Bizeau, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: S2MDF is a lightweight plug-and-play module enforcing a hard constraint to guarantee intersection-free multi-object signed distance fields, eliminating interpenetration without soft penalty terms. It works with any object-compositional SDF representation at negligible cost.

entry.title: Masked Diffusion Vision-Language Models for Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Fengshun Wang, Zhengbo Zhang, Zhigang Tu

entry.summary: This work adapts masked diffusion vision-language models to temporal action localization, keeping semantic and boundary tokens editable throughout iterative denoising via bidirectional attention. This lets later evidence revise earlier timestamp predictions, unlike autoregressive decoders.

entry.title: Future Forcing: Future-aware Training-free KV Cache Policy for Autoregressive Video Generation

author.name: Jiayi Luo, Qiyan Liu, Tengyang Wang, JunHao Liu, Jiayu Chen, Cong Wang, Hanxin Zhu, Chen Gao, Xiaobin Hu, Qingyun Sun, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Future Forcing is a training-free KV cache policy for autoregressive video generation that assesses token importance using future-aware signals rather than short-horizon historical context. It mitigates memory growth and error accumulation for long video synthesis.

entry.title: GenClaw: Code-Driven Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Junyan Ye, Jun He, Zilong Huang, Dongzhi Jiang, Xuan Yang, Rui Chen, Weijia Li

entry.summary: GenClaw is a code-driven agentic image generation paradigm that empowers an LLM agent to construct images like a human artist by conceptualizing, sketching, then coloring through direct canvas manipulation rather than repeated prompt rewriting. It overcomes the black-box limitation of underlying image models.

entry.title: Differentiable Belief-based Opponent Shaping

author.name: Aarav G Sane, Karthik Sivachandran, Rohan Paleja

entry.summary: Proposes D-BOS, a differentiable belief-based opponent-shaping method that treats observer beliefs as the shaped state and differentiates through k-step softmax-Bayes belief dynamics. It enables influencing others' beliefs without hard-coded deception objectives in multi-agent settings.

entry.title: Indexing the Unreadable: LLM-Native Recursive Construction and Search of Service Taxonomies

author.name: Wei Zheng, Yang Yan, Yiyang Shao, Jinyang Li, Zeze Chang, Yukuang Jia, Qiming Mao, Chihyung Wang, Jingbin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-native recursive method to construct and search service taxonomies for the Internet of Agents, addressing context-window overflow and lost-in-the-middle problems when orchestrating thousands of MCP/A2A services. It treats service discovery as context management.

entry.title: CoHyDE: Iterative Co-Training of LLM Rewriter & Dense Encoder for Tool Retrieval

author.name: Vaishali Senthil, Ashutosh Hathidara, Sebastian Schreiber

entry.summary: Introduces CoHyDE, an iterative co-training framework that jointly trains an LLM query rewriter and a dense encoder for tool retrieval, bridging colloquial queries and technical API vocabulary. It combines the complementary strengths of fine-tuned encoders and HyDE-style expansion.

entry.title: EvoMD-LLM: Learning the Language of Species Evolution in Reactive Molecular Dynamics

author.name: Zhichen Tang, Zhengzheng Dang, Yulin Chen, Jixin Wu, Haiwen Li, Yanming Wang

entry.summary: Presents EvoMD-LLM, which reformulates reactive molecular dynamics as a symbolic temporal language-modeling task, discretizing trajectories into species events with persistence durations for autoregressive learning. Temporal scaffolding treats event duration as an explicit linguistic token.

entry.title: Towards Human-Like Interactive Speech Recognition With Agentic Correction and Semantic Evaluation

author.name: Zixuan Jiang, Yanqiao Zhu, Peng Wang, Qinyuan Chen, Xinjian Zhao, Xipeng Qiu, Wupeng Wang, Zhifu Gao, Xiangang Li, Kai Yu, Xie Chen

entry.summary: Reformulates ASR as a multi-turn interactive refinement task and proposes Agentic ASR, a closed-loop system combining single-pass recognition with semantic evaluation and agentic correction. It targets meaning-critical errors that token-level metrics like WER miss.

entry.title: VikingMem: A Memory Base Management System for Stateful LLM-based Applications

author.name: Jiajie Fu, Junwen Chen, Mengzhao Wang, Aoxiang He, Maojia Sheng, Xiangyu Ke, Yifan Zhu, Yunjun Gao

entry.summary: Introduces VikingMem, a Memory Base management system for stateful LLM applications that performs selective extraction of high-value memories to overcome finite context windows. It aims for generalizable, task-agnostic memory beyond single-purpose chatbot extraction prompts.

entry.title: FHRFormer: A Self-Supervised Masked Transformer Framework for Fetal Heart Rate Time-Series Inpainting and Forecasting

author.name: Kjersti Engan, Neel Kanwal, Anita Yeconia, Ladislaus Blacy, Yuda Munyaw, Estomih Mduma, Hege Ersdal

entry.summary: FHRFormer is a self-supervised masked transformer for fetal heart rate time-series inpainting and forecasting, addressing sensor displacement gaps in wearable fetal monitors. It aims to predict the risk of newborns needing breathing assistance from continuous FHR data.

entry.title: Compass: Navigating Global Marine Lead Data Integration through Expert-Guided LLM Agent

author.name: Yiming Liu, Bin Lu, Meng Jin, Ziyuan Sang, Shuo Jiang, Lei Zhou, Xinbing Wang, Chenghu Zhou, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: Compass is an expert-guided LLM agent framework for extracting marine lead and isotope data from unstructured academic papers without fine-tuning, addressing data silos in oceanography. It embeds domain knowledge to avoid hallucinations and scientifically invalid outputs.

entry.title: Learning to Choose: An Empowerment-Guided Multi-Agent System with semantic communication for Adaptive Method Selection

author.name: Geremy Loacham\'in-Suntaxi, Robert Lazar, Dimitrios G. Giovanis, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Eleni D. Koronaki

entry.summary: This work introduces an empowerment-guided multi-agent system with semantic communication for adaptive computational method selection in scientific computing workflows, addressing semantic drift where executed procedures diverge from selected strategies. It ensures outcomes remain causally attributable to decisions.

entry.title: Anchorless Diversification for Parallel LLM Ideation

author.name: Fares Nabil Ibrahim, Nafis Saami Azad, Raiyan Abdul Baten

entry.summary: This work studies inference-time controls for diversifying parallel LLM candidate-idea pools, comparing anchorless methods (independent generation, semantic direction stratification) against seed-dependent anchor baselines across three creative task families. It finds population-referential divergence is a strong low-cost baseline.

entry.title: Modularizing Educational LLM-Agency for Fostering Responsible Learning Assistance

author.name: Julius Gabelmann, Felix Jahn, Kevin Baum, Sophie van Rossum, Emely Wuenscher, Timo P. Gros, Verena Wolf

entry.summary: This work introduces a modular agentic AI chatbot architecture for education that assists students with exercise solving while adhering to pedagogical concepts, based on identified desiderata for responsible educational LLM systems. It aims to avoid harms like loss of transfer, critical thinking, and creativity.

entry.title: LogDx-CI: Benchmarking Log Reduction Tools for LLM Root-Cause Diagnosis

author.name: Bowen Qin

entry.summary: LogDx-CI benchmarks 11 log-reduction tools for feeding noisy CI failure logs to LLM debuggers, scored across multiple LLM families on 35 real GitHub Actions cases. It finds hybrid grep+tail routers dominate the cost-quality frontier.

entry.title: CA-AC-MPC: CUDA-Accelerated Actor-Critic Model Predictive Control

author.name: Antoonio Buo, Vittorio Cammarota, Michele Avagnale, Pierluigi Arpenti, Vincenzo Lippiello, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: CA-AC-MPC is a CUDA-accelerated variant of actor-critic model predictive control that reduces the training and inference latency of the differentiable MPC layer while preserving control performance. It demonstrates state-of-the-art lap times on an agile drone racing task.

entry.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly of Markov Boundary for Tabular Prediction

author.name: Shu Wan, Abhinav Gorantla, Huan Liu, K. Sel\c{c}uk Candan

entry.summary: Empirically tests whether the Markov boundary, the theoretically minimal sufficient feature set, actually helps tabular prediction using a large synthetic SCM benchmark and six regressors. Findings are nuanced, showing benefits are conditional rather than guaranteed.

entry.title: Temporal Motif-aware Graph Test-time Adaptation for OOD Blockchain Anomaly Detection

author.name: Runang He, Tongya Zheng, Huiling Peng, Yuanyu Wan, Bingde Hu, Jiawei Chen, Canghong Jin, Mingli Song, Can Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TEMG-TTA, a temporal motif-aware graph test-time adaptation framework for out-of-distribution blockchain anomaly detection that captures 3-node temporal motif distributions. It addresses adversarial pattern evolution and distribution shift across cryptocurrency transaction graphs.

entry.title: Evolving Features vs Evolving Entire Trees with GP for Interpretable Survival Analysis

author.name: Thalea Schlender, Peter A. N. Bosman, Tanja Alderliesten

entry.summary: Compares evolving features versus evolving entire trees using genetic programming for interpretable survival analysis on censored medical data. Aims to balance accuracy and interpretability against greedy survival trees.

entry.title: Pre-Registering the Detectable Effect: A Paired-MDE Budget for 4-bit Quantization Benchmarks, with a Pilot Audit

author.name: Zexin Zhuang, Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan

entry.summary: Adapts classical paired-binary sample-size calculations to quantization benchmarks, providing a minimum-detectable-effect bound that lets benchmark designers pre-commit to a reliability budget. Includes a small pilot audit across four models and benchmarks.

entry.title: Robust Frequency-Calibrated Virtual EEG Channel Generation from Four Frontal Electrodes for Wearable EEG Augmentation

author.name: Minghao Xiao

entry.summary: FAVC-Net generates 13 virtual EEG channels from just four frontal electrodes using frequency-calibrated multi-scale encoding and graph attention, targeting wearable low-channel EEG. Aims to expand spatial coverage for long-term monitoring.

entry.title: MMTM: Tri-Modal Topic Modeling for Long-Form Video via Similarity-Gated Fusion

author.name: Ali Abusaleh, Bhuvanesh Verma, Alexander Mehler

entry.summary: MMTM is a modular tri-modal (speech, audio, visual) topic-modeling pipeline for long-form video using similarity-gated fusion and BERTopic, evaluated cross-lingually on German and English news. Improves topic coherence and stability over unimodal approaches.

entry.title: Neural Operator-Based Surrogate Model for CFD:Helical Coil Steam Generator in Small Modular Reactor

author.name: Minseo Lee, Seongmin Oh, Chaehyeon Song, Bumjin Cho, Shilaj Baral, Sangam Khanal, Minseop Song, Joongoo Jeon

entry.summary: This paper develops a neural operator-based surrogate combined with reduced-order modeling for CFD transient analysis of a helical coil steam generator in small modular reactors. It enables real-time thermal-hydraulic simulation for digital twin applications where full CFD is too costly.

entry.title: Lightweight Complementary-Cue Fusion for Robust Video Face Forgery Detection

author.name: Sunghwan Baek, Tariq Anwaar, Karanveer Singh, Rita Singh

entry.summary: This paper shows that a single lightweight fusion of two handcrafted cues can outperform wide dual-stream backbones for video face forgery detection. Building on Xception, the proposed LFWS and LFWL add only 292 parameters yet improve accuracy over larger models.

entry.title: Mixing Vector Model for Copolymer Inference via Mixed Integer Linear Programming

author.name: Jianshen Zhu, Raveena Rai, Taiyo Sohkawa, Naveed Ahmed Azam, Kazuya Haraguchi, Liang Zhao, Tatsuya Akutsu

entry.summary: This work extends the mol-infer MILP molecular inference framework to copolymers via a mixing vector model representing copolymer features as convex combinations of monomer descriptors. It enables inverse design of copolymers with desired properties without explicit sequence modeling.

entry.title: Visual Spatial Learning: Single-Field Spatial Interpolation Using Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Daniel Tinoco, Raquel Menezes, Carlos Baquero, Alexandra Silva

entry.summary: This paper proposes a CNN-based spatial interpolation method trained and applied on a single partially observed field, predicting complete spatially correlated fields from sparse observations without external data. It offers an alternative to Kriging that avoids Gaussian process assumptions and variography in non-stationary settings.

entry.title: Unlocking Fine-Grained and Within-Utterance Speaking Style Control in Prompt-Based Text-to-Speech Models

author.name: Jaehoon Kang, Yejin Lee, Yoonji Park, Kyuhong Shim

entry.summary: This paper enables fine-grained and within-utterance speaking style control in prompt-based TTS using direction vectors between contrastive style prompts for interpolation and intra-utterance transitions. It expands controllability of existing TTS models without retraining.

entry.title: ConRAG: Consensus-Driven Multi-View Retrieval for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Yikai Zhu, Kunfeng Chen, Qihuang Zhong, Juhua Liu, Bo Du

entry.summary: ConRAG is a consensus-driven multi-view RAG framework for multi-hop QA that optimizes both query and corpus sides, leveraging relation, entity, and text signals. It aims to outperform prior decomposition-only or knowledge-graph-only approaches on complex reasoning.

entry.title: PubMedCausal: A Span-Level Annotated Corpus for Causal Relation Extraction in Biomedical Text

author.name: Ifeoluwa Kunle-John, Josiah Paul, Oluwatosin Agbaakin, Peter Aina, Ikenna Odezuligbo, Sydney Anuyah

entry.summary: PubMedCausal is a span-level annotated corpus for biomedical causal relation extraction built from PubMed abstracts, distinguishing causation from broader association and capturing implicit cues. It contains 30,000 paragraph-level rows including thousands of adjudicated cause-effect pairs with full spans and causality types.

entry.title: Roles with Rails: Contract-Preserving Role Evolution in Multi-Agent Structured Reasoning

author.name: Ling-Yue Ge, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: This paper formulates contract-preserving role evolution for multi-agent structured reasoning, requiring committed edits to preserve five structural contracts like capability coverage and output protocols. It instantiates this in SERO, a self-evolving system that adapts roles without breaking answer contracts.

entry.title: A Fixed-Budget, Cluster-Aware Standard for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation: A Multi-Hop RAG Stress Test

author.name: Camilo Chac\'on Sartori, Jos\'e H. Garc\'ia

entry.summary: Proposes a minimum measurement standard for LLM-as-a-judge comparisons in multi-hop RAG, fixing candidate pools, evidence budgets, prompts, and requiring pre-registered hypotheses and cluster-aware inference. It exposes how evaluation choices confound judgments. Matters for reproducible and trustworthy RAG evaluation.

entry.title: OphIn-500K: Curating Web-Scale Visual Instructions for Scaling Ophthalmic Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xuanzhao Dong, Wenhui Zhu, Xiwen Chen, Hao Wang, Xin Li, Yujian Xiong, Jiajun Cheng, Jingjing Wang, Xiaobing Yu, Haiyu Wu, Shao Tang, Zhipeng Wang, Langechuan Liu, Shan Lin, Oana Dumitrascu, Yalin Wang

entry.summary: Introduces OphIn-500K, a web-scale ophthalmology visual instruction dataset built via the OphIn-Engine curation pipeline to scale ophthalmic multimodal LLMs beyond limited public benchmark images. It addresses data scarcity in specialized medical conversational AI. Matters for clinical multimodal assistants.

entry.title: SilentRetrieval: Hijacking Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Semantically-Preserving Adversarial Data Poisoning

author.name: Jiachen Qian

entry.summary: Presents SilentRetrieval, a two-stage RAG poisoning attack using coordinated beam search and context-adaptive trigger generation to craft fluent yet adversarial documents that hijack retrieval with high hit rates. It exposes corpus integrity vulnerabilities in RAG. Matters for RAG security.

entry.title: Satisfiability Solving with LLMs: A Matched-Pair Evaluation of Reasoning Capability

author.name: Leizhen Zhang, Shuhan Chen, Sheng Chen

entry.summary: Provides a matched-pair systematic study of LLMs on 2-SAT and 3-SAT plus reductions to Vertex Cover and 3D packing, showing conventional metrics are misleading and models over-predict satisfiability and fail at the phase transition. It probes representation-invariant reasoning limits. Matters for understanding LLM logical reasoning.

entry.title: Activation Steering for Synthetic Data Generation: The Role of Diversity in Downstream Safety Detection

author.name: Vijeta Deshpande, Tootiya Giyahchi, Veena Padmanabhan, Leman Akoglu, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Investigates whether activation steering can generate diverse synthetic training data for downstream safety classifiers detecting HHH-violating outputs, introducing sample- and set-level diversity as a quality axis. It evaluates intrinsic and extrinsic quality across concepts, models, and steering methods. Matters for data-efficient safety detection.

entry.title: GAP3D: Generative Alignment of VLM Latents to Patch-Level Embeddings for 3D Generation

author.name: Polytimi Anna Gkotsi, Andrii Zadaianchuk, Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani

entry.summary: Proposes GAP3D, a modular diffusion-based approach that aligns VLM-generated latents to the dense patch-level feature space of a pretrained image encoder, letting a frozen generative model use a VLM as prompt encoder while preserving spatial structure for 3D asset generation. It avoids expensive end-to-end training and large 3D datasets. Matters for geometry-aware generative conditioning.

entry.title: ESAM++: Efficient Online 3D Perception on the Edge

author.name: Qin Liu, Lavisha Aggarwal, Saptarashmi Bandyopadhyay, Vikas Bahirwani, Marc Niethammer, Ehsan Adeli, Andrea Colaco

entry.summary: ESAM++ is a lightweight alternative to EmbodiedSAM for online 3D scene perception on edge devices, replacing the expensive 3D sparse UNet that dominated inference time. It targets real-time 3D instance segmentation for robotics and AR/VR with limited resources.

entry.title: Optimizing Latent Representations for Robust Building Damage Assessment Onboard Earth Observation Satellites

author.name: Thomas Goudemant, Benjamin Francesconi

entry.summary: This work proposes an onboard-satellite AI system for object-level building damage assessment from pre/post-disaster imagery, optimizing compact latent representations to overcome data downlink constraints. It aims to reduce latency for emergency response.

entry.title: Improving CLIP Adaptation by Breaking Tail Alignment for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning

author.name: Shuai Yi, Yixiong Zou, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: This paper improves CLIP adaptation for source-free cross-domain few-shot learning by deliberately pushing away low-similarity tail tokens from their text embeddings, a counterintuitive finding that boosts target-domain performance. It provides an interpretation tied to domain shift.

entry.title: DGSG-Mind: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Scene Graphs for Long-Term Scene Understanding and Grounding

author.name: Luzhou Ge, Xiangyu Zhu, Jinyan Liu, Xuesong Li

entry.summary: DGSG-Mind is a dynamic 3D Gaussian scene graph system with an embodied reasoning agent for long-term scene understanding and grounding, handling object-level topological changes and open-vocabulary semantics. It couples a probabilistic voxel grid with explicit 3D Gaussians.

entry.title: EarlyTom: Early Token Compression Completes Fast Video Understanding

author.name: Hesong Wang, Xin Jin, Lu Lu, Chenhaowen Li, Jian Chen, Qiang Liu, Huan Wang

entry.summary: EarlyTom performs early token compression inside the vision encoder of Video-LLMs to reduce time-to-first-token, showing vision encoding is a major latency contributor. It moves compression earlier rather than only after the encoder during prefilling.

entry.title: GenEraser: Generalizable Video Object Removal via Balanced Text-Mask Guidance and Decoupled Locator-Preserver

author.name: Yuqing Chen, Lin Liu, Haisu Wu, Xiaopeng Zhang, Yaowei Wang, Yujiu Yang, Qi Tian

entry.summary: GenEraser is a generalizable video object removal framework that eliminates both objects and associated physical effects (smoke, reflections, ripples) using balanced text-mask guidance and decoupled locator-preserver design. It resolves the conflict between semantic generalization and pixel-level background preservation.

entry.title: Cycle Consistency in Video Object-Centric Learning

author.name: Rongzhen Zhao, Zhiyuan Li, Ruonan Wei, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen

entry.summary: This work investigates cycle consistency in self-supervised video object-centric learning, showing that explicit cycle consistency on stochastic slots causes feature collapse unlike in deterministic tracking. It proposes a resolution that respects the ambiguity of scene decompositions.

entry.title: How to Relieve Distribution Shifts in Semantic Segmentation for Off-Road Environments

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Daeyoung Kim, Hyung-Suk Yoon, Dong-Wook Kim, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: ST-Seg relieves distribution shifts in off-road semantic segmentation through style expansion and texture regularization to broaden the source distribution. It targets robustness to domain gaps and sensor corruption in autonomous off-road navigation.

entry.title: Decentralized LLM-Driven Coordination of Acoustic Robots for Contactless Object Manipulation

author.name: Yingying Wang, Narsimlu Kemsaram, Sriram Subramanian

entry.summary: Presents a decentralized framework coordinating ultrasonic phased-array acoustic robots for contactless object manipulation via natural language, using Whisper speech recognition and LLM semantic parsing into structured task plans. It targets healthcare and lab automation applications.

entry.title: Does Claude care about others the same way humans do?

author.name: Simon Lermen

entry.summary: Argues that the persona-selection alignment approach producing warm, caring AI personas works in the current regime but likely won't extrapolate to more powerful systems, because human empathy has origins (kin selection, mental-state mirroring) that AI lacks. It frames AI 'caring' as predicting what humans want to hear rather than genuine concern.

entry.title: Black Boxes for Low-Stakes, Interpretable AI for High-Stakes

author.name: Logan Riggs

entry.summary: Argues for a two-tier AI deployment strategy: general black-box models for low-stakes settings and narrow, robust, interpretable models for high-stakes domains like banking, grids, and medicine, using historical mammography accreditation as a regulatory template. It frames interpretable narrow models as a regulatable safer alternative.

entry.title: Glasswing exposed a governance gap

author.name: callumzc

entry.summary: Argues that Anthropic's Glasswing/Mythos access-control decisions set an overlooked governance precedent in which the company became the de facto arbiter of who can access strategically powerful AI without agreed criteria or accountability. It examines the governance risks of labs gatekeeping high-capability models.

entry.title: ReasonLight: A Multimodal Foundation Model-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning Framework for Zero-Shot Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Aoyu Pang, Maonan Wang, Yuejiao Xie, Chung Shue Chen, Zhiwei Yang, Man-On Pun

entry.summary: Proposes ReasonLight, a multimodal foundation-model-enhanced RL framework for zero-shot traffic signal control that fuses structured traffic measurements, multi-view camera observations, and RL-proposed phase decisions. It improves adaptability to open-world events absent from training data.

entry.title: Think Fast, Talk Smart: Partitioning Deterministic and Neural Computation for Structured Health Text Generation

author.name: Kai-Chen Cheng, Haejun Han, David Q. Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Think Fast, Talk Smart, a structured health-text pipeline where deterministic code handles recurring analysis before a single bounded LLM writer call to ensure faithfulness, grounding, and cheap repeated use. It examines which responsibilities should be deterministic versus LLM-driven.

entry.title: CosmicFish-HRM: Adaptive Reasoning via Hierarchical Recurrent Mechanisms in Compact Language Models

author.name: Venkat Akhil Lakkapragada

entry.summary: CosmicFish-HRM is a compact language model with a Hierarchical Reasoning Module that dynamically allocates compute via high-level and low-level reasoning cycles, learning when to halt based on input complexity. It combines adaptive reasoning with modern transformer components.

entry.title: Benchmarking Large Vision-Language Models on CFMME: A Comprehensive Chinese Financial Multimodal Evaluation Dataset

author.name: Qian Chen, Xianyin Zhang, Yanzhi Liu, Lifan Guo, Feng Chen, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CFMME, a Chinese financial multimodal benchmark with 6,052 instances across eight financial image modalities and four tasks to evaluate vision-language models across the financial workflow. It provides thorough evaluation of current LVLMs in this domain.

entry.title: Momentum Based Reward Design for Low Emission Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Chinmay Mundane, Amith Manoharan, Arun Singh

entry.summary: Proposes a momentum-based reward for deep RL traffic-signal control that encourages vehicles to keep moving rather than only penalizing congestion, evaluated in SUMO. Aims for more stable, far-sighted low-emission signal policies.

entry.title: Gated Graph Attention Networks with Learnable Temperature

author.name: Zhongtian Ma, Hao Wu, Yexin Zhang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Adds gated attention and learnable temperature to graph attention networks to filter unreliable feature dimensions and adapt attention sharpness, improving robustness on homophilic and heterophilic graphs. A targeted enhancement of GAT mechanisms.

entry.title: HELEA: Hard-Negative Benchmark and LLM-based Reranking for Robust Entity Alignment

author.name: Yoonjin Jang, Junwoo Kim, Youngjoong Ko

entry.summary: HELEA introduces a same-name hard-negative augmentation strategy for entity alignment that produces both evaluation benchmarks and augmented training corpora by mining same-name but distinct entity pairs. It adds a two-stage retrieval-plus-LLM-reranking framework to reject confusing same-name entities.

entry.title: On Compositional Learning Behaviours in Formal Mathematics

author.name: Kevin Yandoka Denamgana\"i

entry.summary: This paper studies compositional learning behaviors in formal mathematics, adapting a Symbolic Behaviour Benchmark to remove numerical confounds and add chain-of-thought scaffolding. Cross-evaluating ten Lean 4 theorem provers, it finds search-heavy models cover tractable problems without detectable compositional behaviors.

entry.title: IPO-Mine: A Toolkit and Dataset for Section-Structured Analysis of Long, Multimodal IPO Documents

author.name: Michael Galarnyk, Siddharth Lohani, Vidhyakshaya Kannan, Sagnik Nandi, Aman Patel, Liqin Ye, Arnav Hiray, Rutwik Routu, Prasun Banerjee, Siddhartha Somani, Sudheer Chava

entry.summary: IPO-Mine provides an open-source toolkit and dataset for section-structured analysis of long, multimodal IPO filings that often exceed 500,000 tokens and lack consistent structure. It standardizes downloading, parsing into sections, and extracting images for studying these documents with modern models.

entry.title: FPMoE: A Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Approach to Functional Code Generation

author.name: Loc Pham, Lang Hong Nguyet Anh, Thanh Le-Cong

entry.summary: Presents FPMoE, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts model for functional programming code generation with language-specific routed experts for Haskell, OCaml, and Scala plus a shared expert to capture common abstractions. It addresses underexplored functional languages where frontier models underperform. Matters for code generation diversity.

entry.title: AI, Take the Wheel: What Drives Delegation and Trust in Human-Computer Cooperative Question Answering?

author.name: Maharshi Gor, Yoo Yeon Sung, Yu Hou, Eve Fleisig, Irene Ying, Tianyi Zhou, Jordan Boyd-Graber

entry.summary: Studies delegation versus adoption reliance decisions in human-AI cooperative question answering, distinguishing when humans let AI act autonomously versus how they evaluate AI suggestions. It uses a competitive QA game with the same users to study both patterns together. Matters for human-AI collaboration design.

entry.title: Resolving Endpoint Underfitting in Diffusion Bridges via Noise Alignment

author.name: Yurong Gao, Zicheng Zhang, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Xinmin Qiu

entry.summary: Identifies an underfitting phenomenon near the target endpoint in diffusion bridge models caused by large noise-level discrepancy between input and regression target, and proposes Noise-Aligned Diffusion Bridge to resolve it. It improves image restoration and translation. Matters for diffusion-based generative modeling quality.

entry.title: CapTalk: Text-Guided Stylization and Speech-Driven 3D Head Animation

author.name: Xuangeng Chu, Yuan Gan, Ziteng Cui, Shuhong Liu, Jian Wang, Bing Zhou, Tatsuya Harada

entry.summary: Presents CapTalk, a framework for text-guided stylization and speech-driven 3D head animation that disentangles style and emotion using a large dataset with textual style and emotion descriptions, enabling separate control. It addresses fixed-style animation that ignores emotional content of audio. Matters for controllable talking head generation.

entry.title: Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation Facilitates Model Understanding

author.name: Xiaoyan Yu, Lisa Mais, Jannik Franzen, Peter Hirsch, Nick Lechtenb\"orger, Andreas Mardt, Dagmar Kainm\"uller

entry.summary: This work uses unsupervised semantic segmentation as an intuitive tool for understanding self-supervised vision transformers, highlighting differences between contrastive and masked-image-modeling representations. It aims to make model understanding accessible to a broader audience.

entry.title: Not All Inputs Are Valid: Towards Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval Using Language

author.name: Xiang Fang, Wanlong Fang, Daizong Liu, Xiaoye Qu, Jianfeng Dong, Pan Zhou, Renfu Li, Zichuan Xu, Lixing Chen, Panpan Zheng, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: This work introduces Open-Set Video Moment Retrieval, where out-of-distribution video-irrelevant queries must be rejected rather than wrongly retrieved, important for high-risk scenarios. It moves beyond the closed-set assumption of prior VMR methods.

entry.title: FRUC: Feedforward Dynamic Scene Reconstruction from Uncalibrated Collaborative Driving Views

author.name: Yihang Tao, Yu Guo, Zhengru Fang, Haonan An, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: FRUC is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting framework for dynamic scene reconstruction from uncalibrated collaborative driving views, removing the need for precise calibration and per-scene optimization. It enhances ego-centric occluded geometry through collaboration without degrading visible geometry.

entry.title: DocRetriever: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Multimodal Document Retrieval with Comprehensive Benchmark

author.name: Ruofan Hu, Menghui Zhu, Jieming Zhu, Bo Chen, Shengyang Xu, Minjie Hong, Xiaoda Yang, Sashuai Zhou, Li Tang, Tao Jin, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: DocRetriever is a plug-and-play framework for multimodal document retrieval handling tables, figures, and layouts, addressing limitations of dense embeddings and supervised rerankers. It comes with a comprehensive benchmark with diverse assessment dimensions.

entry.title: IP-Adapter Is All You Need: Towards Fine-Tuning-Free Diffusion-Based Talking Face Generation

author.name: Hao Wu, Xiangyang Luo, Hao Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Yi Zhang, Jinwei Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a fine-tuning-free diffusion-based talking face generation method using pretrained Stable Diffusion and IP-Adapter weights, mining lip-related semantics without task-specific training or large audiovisual datasets. It addresses identity drift, synchronization, and temporal consistency.

entry.title: Distributed Non-Uniform Scaling Control of Multi-Agent Formation with Dynamic Agent Joining

author.name: Tao He, Gangshan Jing

entry.summary: Introduces a distributed control framework enabling multi-agent formations to incorporate new agents during non-uniform scaling maneuvers in arbitrary dimensions while preserving graph Laplacian spectral properties. It extends formation maneuvering to dynamic team expansion.

entry.title: Frontier LLM-based agents can overcome the ontology curation bottleneck for natural phenotypes

author.name: James P. Balhoff, Hilmar Lapp

entry.summary: Revisits a phenotype-annotation gold standard benchmark using five frontier LLM agents, showing they can match or exceed prior tools and approach human inter-curator consistency. It argues LLM agents can relieve the ontology curation bottleneck in comparative biology.

entry.title: Harmonizing Real-Time Constraints and Long-Horizon Reasoning: An Asynchronous Agentic Framework for Dynamic Scheduling

author.name: Shijie Cao, Yuan Yuan, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Proposes RACE-Sched, an asynchronous agent framework that decouples fast policy execution from slower LLM reasoning to handle dynamic flexible job-shop scheduling under millisecond decision cycles. It reconciles real-time reactivity with long-horizon optimization.

entry.title: When Does Persona Prompting Actually Help? A Retrieval and Metric Analysis of Expert Role Injection in LLMs

author.name: Shuai Xiao, Su Liu, Weikai Zhou, Jialun Wu, Xinjie He, Zhiyuan Lin, Qiyang Xie

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled retrieval-and-metric analysis of expert persona prompting across 1,140 questions, 38 roles, and six domains, finding only small aggregate differences but dimension-specific shifts in quality. It clarifies when expert-role injection actually helps versus merely reshaping responses.

entry.title: CrystalXRD-Bench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for XRD Peak Indexing Across Diverse Crystalline Materials

author.name: Chengliang Xu, Xiaogang Li, Peiyao Xiao, Beng Wang, Hu Wei, Bing Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces CrystalXRD-Bench, a 250-sample benchmark testing vision-language models on Miller-index identification from powder XRD patterns requiring visual peak reading plus crystallographic reasoning. The best model (GPT-5.4) reaches only a 0.59 Jaccard score, revealing significant gaps.

entry.title: PTCG-Bench: Can LLM Agents Master Pok\'emon Trading Card Game?

author.name: Dongdong Hua, Yifei Sun, Renhong Huang, Feng Gao, Chunping Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Presents PTCG-Bench, a benchmark on the Pokemon Trading Card Game evaluating LLM agents both on single-environment decision-making and on self-evolving through accumulated experience, with a harness ablation to separate harness from model capability. It tests strategic, evolving decision-making.

entry.title: Notation Matters: A Benchmark Study of Token-Optimized Formats in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Lorenz Kutschka, Bernhard Geiger

entry.summary: This benchmark study tests whether token-optimized serialization formats (TOON, TRON) that reduce overhead versus JSON actually help inside end-to-end agentic loops across four benchmarks. It probes a practical efficiency question that prior work only evaluated on isolated tasks.

entry.title: Meta-Programming for Linear-time Temporal Answer Set Programming

author.name: Susana Hahn, Amade Nems, Javier Romero, Torsten Schaub

entry.summary: This work proposes a flexible meta-programming framework operationalizing the semantics of various temporal Answer Set Programming logics (linear-time, dynamic, metric) through a unified declarative approach extending clingo. It includes a semantically-correct transformation pipeline for nested modal expressions.

entry.title: Physics Is All You Need? A Case Study in Physicist-Supervised AI Development of Scientific Software

author.name: Nhat-Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: This single-physicist case study (N=1) documents supervising an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Sonnet and Opus) over 12 days to build a differentiable perturbation-theory module in JAX, classifying 15 supervision events and finding the agent treated symptom reduction as root-cause resolution in cases evading oracle tests. It examines whether AI agents are tools, co-authors, or researchers.

entry.title: Beyond Recall: Behavioral Specification as an Interpretive Layer for AI Personalization

author.name: Aarik Gulaya

entry.summary: This paper introduces representational accuracy to measure how faithfully an AI system captures a person's interpretation, operationalized as a Behavioral Specification serving compressed interpretive patterns as context. It is benchmarked against commercial memory systems.

entry.title: Multi-Resolution End-to-End Deep Neural Network for Optimizing Latency-Accuracy Tradeoff in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Qitao Weng, Heechul Yun

entry.summary: A multi-resolution end-to-end DNN for autonomous driving in CARLA that optimizes the latency-accuracy tradeoff, supporting multiple input resolutions via per-resolution batch norm. It adapts the latency-optimal configuration to scene context and compute availability.

entry.title: Adaptive Interviewing for Persona Simulation in LLMs: Evidence-Grounded Reasoning Improves Decision Alignment

author.name: Ruoxi Su, Yuhan Liu, Jingyu Hu

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive interview framework that gathers persona information through structured multi-stage dialogue to better simulate individual decisions in moral dilemmas with LLMs. Dynamic interview transcripts improve decision alignment over static persona descriptions.

entry.title: GiPL: Generative augmented iterative Pseudo-Labeling for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection

author.name: Jiacong Liu, Shu Luo, Yikai Qin, Yaze Zhao, Yongwei Jiang, Yixiong Zou

entry.summary: Proposes GiPL, a two-branch framework for cross-domain few-shot object detection using iterative pseudo-label self-training and generative augmentation to better exploit sparse support data and reduce overfitting. It leverages vision-language foundation models for zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Energy-Aware NECO for Single-Pass Pixel-wise Out-of-Distribution Detection in Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Boyuan Zhang, Huanshan Huang, Yifei Cao

entry.summary: Proposes Energy-Aware NECO, a single-pass pixel-wise out-of-distribution detector for semantic segmentation that combines a centered NECO geometric ratio with a logit-based energy score. It targets efficient OOD detection deployable on edge robotics platforms.

entry.title: Traditional machine learning vs. deep learning from dynamic graph representations of proteins' 3D folds in the task of protein structure classification

author.name: Aydin Wells, Francis A. Gatsi, Aaron Striegel, Tijana Milenkovi\'c

entry.summary: Compares traditional ML on engineered dynamic protein-graph features versus deep learning for protein structure classification into CATH/SCOP classes. Continues a line of work on dynamic protein structure networks.

entry.title: A Geometric View of SRC: Learning Representations for Stable Residual Inference

author.name: Vangelis P. Oikonomou

entry.summary: Provides a geometric analysis of Sparse Representation Classification used as a fixed test-time rule, formalizing residual-ordering stability via margins and characterizing geometric obstructions like span overlap. Offers theory for stable reconstruction-based inference.

entry.title: Reducing Experimental Testing in Space Propulsion Film Cooling Analyses by Pixelwise Generative Image Interpolation

author.name: Adam T. M\"uller, Philipp J. Teuffel, Konstantin Manassis, Nicolaj C. Stache

entry.summary: Uses a lightweight feed-forward network with positional encoding for pixelwise image regression from sparse experimental film-cooling measurements, reducing physical tests in space propulsion development. Includes a knowledge-informed extension for local adaptability.

entry.title: Statistical Embeddings for Similarity, Retrieval, and Interpretable Alignment of Numeric Tabular Datasets

author.name: M. Ross Kunz, John Merickel, Keith Wilson

entry.summary: This work proposes statistical embeddings for numeric tabular datasets by characterizing them with exploratory data analysis descriptors, embedding via a sentence transformer, and measuring cross-dataset similarity using Canonical Correlation Analysis. It enables interpretable dataset-level retrieval and alignment across heterogeneous feature spaces.

entry.title: Constructing efficient channels for ideal observers using the conjugate gradient method

author.name: Weimin Zhou

entry.summary: This work presents a conjugate gradient method to construct efficient channels for approximating Bayesian Ideal Observer and Hotelling Observer performance in medical imaging quality assessment. It addresses the computational intractability of ideal observers on high-dimensional image data via dimensionality reduction.

entry.title: A Domain-Informed Multi-Objective Framework for EEG Channel Selection in Motor Imagery BCIs

author.name: Dekka Muni Kumar, Dhruba Jyoti Kalita, Yogesh Kumar Meena

entry.summary: This paper proposes a domain-informed multi-objective optimization framework for EEG channel selection in motor imagery BCIs, balancing spatial relevance via a Gaussian kernel and functional discriminability via task-related desynchronization. It employs NSGA, MOPSO, and MOEA/D to avoid single-objective limitations and local optima.

entry.title: ICG: Improving Cover Image Generation via MLLM-based Prompting and Personalized Preference Alignment

author.name: Zhipeng Bian, Jieming Zhu, Qijiong Liu, Wang Lin, Guohao Cai, Zhaocheng Du, Jiacheng Sun, Zhou Zhao, Zhenhua Dong

entry.summary: ICG generates personalized cover images by combining MLLM-based prompting with preference alignment, extracting semantic features from item titles and refining them with user embeddings before injecting into a diffusion model. A multi-reward strategy compensates for lack of labeled supervision.

entry.title: Evaluating the Realism of LLM-powered Social Agents: A Case Study of Reactions to Spanish Online News

author.name: Alejandro Buitrago L\'opez, Alberto Ortega Pastor, Javier Pastor-Galindo, Jos\'e A. Ruip\'erez-Valiente

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether LLM-generated reactions to Spanish online news reproduce measurable properties of real audience discourse, pairing thousands of real reactions with matched synthetic ones from five LLMs. It compares hate speech, sentiment, and semantic alignment to assess social-agent realism.

entry.title: Identifying and Understanding Human Values in Text: A Tailorable LLM-based Architecture

author.name: Eduardo de la Cruz Fern\'andez, Marcelo Karanik, Sascha Ossowski

entry.summary: This paper introduces a tailorable LLM-based architecture to detect and quantify the intensity of human values in text, avoiding reliance on specific value theories or complex prompt engineering. It targets value-aligned decision-making in autonomous systems.

entry.title: Grounded Cache Routing for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: When Is It Safe to Reuse an Answer?

author.name: Syed Huma Shah (Duke University)

entry.summary: Reframes RAG answer caching from how to reuse faster toward when reuse is safe, proposing GroundedCache that guards against evidence drift and adversarial collision attacks. It addresses a practical reliability gap in production RAG serving stacks. Matters for cost-efficient and safe RAG deployment.

entry.title: Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents

author.name: Xinze Li, Yuhang Zang, Yixin Cao, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Skill-as-Pseudocode, automatically converting free-form markdown skill libraries into typed pseudocode with deterministic verification to reduce LLM agents' confused-re-retrieve loops. It gives agents explicit input schemas and invocation syntax. Matters for reliable agent skill use.

entry.title: SalsaAgent: A multimodal embodied language model for interactive dance generation

author.name: Payam Jome Yazdian, Zoe Stanley, Angelica Lim

entry.summary: Presents SalsaAgent, a multimodal embodied language model that generates expressive full-body salsa dance motions reacting to a human leader and music, formulating interaction as nonverbal motion token passing with new motion and relation tokens and a token-to-diffusion pipeline. It targets socially aware interactive agents. Matters for human-robot nonverbal interaction.

entry.title: One Click per Cell Type Suffices: Training-free Group Interaction for Cell Instance Segmentation

author.name: Sanghyun Jo, Seo Jin Lee, Seohyung Hong, Yoorim Gang, Hyeongsub Kim, Hyungseok Seo, Kyungsu Kim

entry.summary: Introduces ParCo-SDF, a prior-free two-stage partial-to-complete signed distance field reconstruction framework for deformable objects using temporal geometry encoding and FiLM-conditioned SDF prediction. It avoids object-specific shape priors to improve generalization for deformable object manipulation. Matters for robotic perception of deformables.

entry.title: FedSmoothLoRA: Toward Smoother and Faster Convergence in Federated Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Zehao Wang, Guanglei Yang, Yihan Zeng, Hang Xu, Hongzhi Zhang, Wangmeng Zuo, Chun-Mei Feng

entry.summary: FedSmoothLoRA tackles convergence issues when combining federated averaging with LoRA fine-tuning of foundation models, addressing limited update space, inter-round state mismatch, and client-agnostic starting states. It aims for smoother and faster federated low-rank adaptation.

entry.title: KGEdit: Ambiguity-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Training-Free Precise Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Mingshu Cai, Miao Zhang, Chenghe Yang, Yixuan Li, Osamu Yoshie, Yuya Ieiri

entry.summary: KGEdit introduces an ambiguity-aware knowledge graph to disambiguate complex text prompts into structured semantics (identity, relation, attribute, negative constraints) for training-free text-to-video generation and editing. It injects these signals into diffusion transformer layers to improve concept binding and cross-frame consistency.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Modeling of Foundation Features Enables Generalizable Object Shape Deformation Learning

author.name: Yiyao Ma, Kai Chen, Zhongxiang Zhou, Zhuheng Song, Dongsheng Xie, Zelong Tan, Rong Xiong, Qi Dou

entry.summary: This paper presents a generalizable deformation-learning framework for monocular 3D shape recovery that explicitly deforms a category-level template to match observations, using geometry-guided foundation feature modeling. It aims for robust generalization across viewpoints and unseen categories.

entry.title: GeoMag: Geometric-Aware Video Motion Magnification via State Space Model

author.name: Kecheng Han, Yuchen Zhang, Bingqing Liu, Boqiang Guo, Wenbin Zheng, Shiyuan Pei

entry.summary: GeoMag is a geometric-aware video motion magnification framework built on State Space Models for globally consistent amplification with linear complexity. It introduces a large synthetic dataset (Geo-200K) with rich geometric transformations to address training-data limitations.

entry.title: OmniCD: A Foundational Framework for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection Guided by Multimodal Semantics

author.name: Chenhao Sun

entry.summary: OmniCD is a foundational framework for remote-sensing change detection guided by multimodal semantics (text, semantic maps, geospatial metadata), supporting tasks from binary to zero-shot semantic change understanding. It includes hierarchical scene retrieval and style disentanglement for cross-domain robustness.

entry.title: Runtime Analysis of a Compact Genetic Algorithm on a Truly Multi-valued OneMax Function

author.name: Martin S. Krejca, Carsten Witt

entry.summary: Provides a rigorous runtime analysis of a multi-valued compact genetic algorithm on a truly multi-valued OneMax function depending on all categories, improving prior theoretical bounds. It advances theory for multi-valued estimation-of-distribution algorithms.

entry.title: A Progress-Aware Leader-Follower Midair Docking System for Dual-Drone Aerial Manipulation

author.name: Yifan Cai, Jan Ming Kevin Tan, Xiangqi Li, Chenzhe Jin, Narsimlu Kemsaram, Valerio Modugno

entry.summary: Presents a dual-drone midair docking platform with leader-follower formation, passive magnetic latching, and a progress-aware mission supervisor managing approach, alignment, capture, and settle phases. It provides a full hardware-software stack for benchmarking aerial docking.

entry.title: How can the middle powers avoid getting trounced during the intelligence explosion? A plan.

author.name: Tom Davidson

entry.summary: Outlines a strategic plan for how middle powers (UK, Europe, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) could avoid being economically and militarily eclipsed during a US-led intelligence explosion by leveraging US dependence on them to compete with China. It argues they need a credible alternative to remaining US supplicants.

entry.title: Architecture-Sensitive Supervised Fine-Tuning for Screen-Conditioned Action Prediction: A PiSAR Benchmark

author.name: Rahul Bissa, Abhishek Vyas, Yash Jain

entry.summary: Benchmarks supervised fine-tuned models against frontier zero-shot baselines on PiSAR, a screen-anchored behavioral-rationale corpus, finding a fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B vastly outperforms Claude Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5 on semantic similarity. It highlights that small fine-tuned models can dominate frontier models on specialized screen-action prediction.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Transfer Learning for Cross-Building Energy Forecasting: Toward Robust and Scalable District-Level Energy Management

author.name: Shadmehr Zaregarizi, Khashayar Yavari

entry.summary: This work presents an uncertainty-aware transfer learning framework based on Temporal Fusion Transformers for cross-building energy forecasting, with a new Transfer Robustness Index metric and layer-freezing ablations on real sub-meter datasets. It targets scalable district-level energy management with minimal target data.

entry.title: TaxDistill: Improving Metagenomic Taxonomic Annotation via Distilled Genomic Foundation Models

author.name: Rongye Ye, Lun Li, Zheng Luo, Yiran Zhan, Shuhui Song

entry.summary: TaxDistill is a knowledge distillation framework for metagenomic taxonomic annotation using genomic foundation models, aiming to reduce label noise from similarity-search-derived training labels. It improves microbial DNA fragment classification representations.

entry.title: Forget Less, Generalize More: Unifying Temporal and Structural Adaptation for Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Qian Chang, Ciprian Doru Giurcaneanu, Runsong Jia, Xia Li, Guoping Hu, Xiufeng Cheng, Jinqing Yang, Mengjia Wu, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Scale Retentive Dynamics, a unified recurrent framework for dynamic graph representation learning that jointly models temporal memory and structural context with adaptive decay kernels. It aims to generalize across graphs with diverse interaction frequencies and topologies.

entry.title: Learning Context-Conditioned Predicate Semantics via Prototype Feedback

author.name: NamGyu Jung, Chang Choi

entry.summary: Proposes AlignG for scene graph generation, learning context-conditioned predicate semantics via prototype feedback to handle polysemous predicates whose meaning shifts across contexts. It recalibrates relation representations using image-specific evidence rather than static prototypes.

entry.title: SigmaMedStat: Temporal Signal Modeling for ICU False Alarm Reduction

author.name: Arunkumar Ramachandran

entry.summary: SigmaMedStat is an ML system to evaluate trustworthiness of ICU physiological alarm signals to reduce false-alarm fatigue, using temporal chunking of recordings on the PhysioNet 2015 challenge data. Addresses a real patient-safety problem.

entry.title: BuilDyn: Excitation-Driven Data Generation for Building Thermal Dynamics Modeling and Control

author.name: Felix Koch, Thomas Krug, Fabian Raisch, Benjamin Sch\"afer, Benjamin Tischler

entry.summary: BuilDyn is a package providing customizable excitation strategies for control-oriented data generation in building thermal dynamics modeling. It addresses the limited state-space exploration in existing datasets that reflect only stationary operation under fixed control policies.

entry.title: StoryLens: Preference-Aligned Story Rewriting via Context-Aware Narrative Enrichment

author.name: Hanwen Cui, Yuting Mei, Yuhang Fu, Dingyi Yang, Qin Jin

entry.summary: StoryLens tackles preference-aligned story rewriting, arguing that context-aware narrative enrichment matters more than surface style transfer, supported by a pilot study showing substantially higher reader satisfaction gains. It introduces a large-scale benchmark with story books, reader profiles, and ranked rewrites.

entry.title: When Discourse Pressures Conflict: Information Structure in Vision-Language Model Outputs

author.name: Marcell Fekete, Johannes Bjerva, Tam\'as K\'aldi

entry.summary: This paper tests whether vision-language models express visual content in discourse-appropriate form, using Hungarian's dedicated Topic and Focus syntactic positions to make information-structure choices observable. It finds VLMs produce IS-relevant constructions but over-regularize sensitivity under conflicting discourse pressures.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Handle Discourse Particles? A Case Study of Colloquial Malay

author.name: Mariah Al Giptiah Binte Yusoff, Jakin Tan, Bocheng Chen, Guangliang Liu, Xi Chen

entry.summary: MalayPrag is a benchmark for systematically evaluating LLMs' handling of discourse particles in colloquial Malay, with five linguistically grounded attributes. It addresses the lack of understanding of LLM pragmatic competence, especially for under-studied Southeast Asian languages.

entry.title: Show, Don't TELL: Explainable AI-Generated Text Detection

author.name: Aldan Creo, Suraj Ranganath

entry.summary: Proposes TELL, an explainable AI-generated text detection architecture that surfaces the specific tells indicating AI versus human authorship rather than just a numeric score. It aims to align detector outputs with real user needs like professors. Matters for trustworthy deployment of AI text detection.

entry.title: Explaining is Harder Than Predicting Alone: Evaluating Concept-based Explanations of MLLMs as ICL Visual Classifiers

author.name: Carmen Quiles-Ram\'irez, Leticia L. Rodr\'iguez, Nicol\'as Martorell, Natalia D\'iaz-Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates concept-based explainability of frozen multimodal LLMs as few-shot in-context visual classifiers across five conditions of increasing formal rigor up to Description Logic axiom generation. It finds explaining is genuinely harder than predicting. Matters for trustworthy multimodal reasoning.

entry.title: Trajectory Constraints for Imaging Inverse Problems

author.name: Chaoyan Huang, Haijie Yuan, Saiprasad Ravishankar

entry.summary: Introduces TRACE, a training-free trajectory-constrained reconstruction framework for imaging inverse problems that couples adjacent states along the reconstruction path, interpretable as proximal updates approximated by a neural mapping. It stabilizes diffusion-based and iterative reconstruction. Matters for stable image restoration.

entry.title: Motion-guided sparse correction enables expert-quality point tracking across diverse microscopy regimes

author.name: Leonidas Zimianitis, Pasindu Thenahandi, Kai Buckhalter, Dineth Jayakody, Julian O. Kimura, Xinyue Liang, Karen Cunningham, Azeem Ahmad, Balpreet S. Ahluwalia, Sampath Jayarathna, Nikos Chrisochoides, Brandon Weissbourd, Dushan N. Wadduwage

entry.summary: Develops RIPPLE, a motion-guided sparse-correction point tracking tool that recasts microscopy annotation as sparse correction where users intervene only where proposed trajectories drift, validated on five challenging biological microscopy datasets. It addresses the lack of scalable expert annotation. Matters for scientific microscopy analysis.

entry.title: FlowSeg: Dynamic Semantic Guidance for LLM-Conditioned Segmentation

author.name: Zekang Zhang, Guangyu Gao, Youyun Tang, ChengJing Wu, Xiaochao Qu, Chi Harold Liu, Jianbo Jiao, Yunchao Wei, Luoqi Liu, Ting Liu

entry.summary: FlowSeg improves LLM-conditioned segmentation by injecting dynamic semantic guidance into the iterative mask generation process rather than using language only as static prompts. It addresses semantic misalignment failures in propose-then-select pipelines.

entry.title: From General Vision to Reliable Traversability Estimation: Adapting Vision Foundation Models for Unstructured Outdoor Environments

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Jisung Bae, Dong-Wook Kim, Yeonkyu Lee, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: ViTA adapts vision foundation models (instantiated on SAM2) for reliable traversability estimation in unstructured outdoor environments using learnable traversability prompts. It addresses gaps between semantic labels and physical safety in off-road navigation.

entry.title: Non-Forgetting Knowledge Allocation with Bi-level Competition for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Xiang Tan, Run He, Yawen Cui, Mengchen Zhao, Yan Wu, Tianyi Chen, Huiping Zhuang, Xiaonan Luo, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: NoFA-BC tackles class-incremental learning with pre-trained models by introducing a non-forgetting allocator with bi-level competition to dynamically allocate task-specific adapters during inference. It addresses suboptimal uniform knowledge allocation and allocator forgetting.

entry.title: Building and Road Recognition in Dense Urban Informal Settlements: A Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Hongyu Long, Jiaxuan Liu, Rui Cao

entry.summary: DenseUIS is the first high-resolution remote-sensing dataset for building and road extraction in extremely dense urban informal settlements, covering 126 urban villages in Shenzhen and Guangzhou. It includes a benchmark of state-of-the-art methods.

entry.title: BullingerDB: A Dataset for Handwritten Text Recognition and Writer Retrieval

author.name: Marco Peer, Anna-Scius Bertrand, Patricia Scheurer, Andreas Fischer

entry.summary: BullingerDB is a large-scale historical document benchmark of 20,898 pages and ~500K text lines from 796 writers spanning the 16th-century Bullinger correspondence, multilingual and time-annotated. It evaluates handwritten text recognition and writer retrieval with a temporal nDCG metric.

entry.title: Human-in-the-Loop Swarms: A Bionic Swarm Approach to Real-World Soil Mapping

author.name: Petras Swissler, Mohammadali Rashidioun, Nicholas Sahu, Raaid Kabir, Ayodeji Aderibigbe, Oladoyin Kolawole

entry.summary: Introduces the Bionic Swarm, a human-in-the-loop system where humans execute hard-to-implement robot tasks directed by a central swarm algorithm via a smartphone app, lowering barriers to swarm field validation. It is demonstrated on geotechnical soil mapping.

entry.title: Bayesian Multiplicity Correction in the Probabilistic Forward Stepwise Framework

author.name: Andrew Womack, Daniel Taylor-Rodriguez

entry.summary: Develops a Bayesian multiplicity-correcting prior within the probabilistic forward stepwise framework for regression model space priors, analogous to the Holm procedure and aligned with the Matryoshka doll prior. It argues adequate multiplicity correction requires more sparsity than many recommended priors provide.

entry.title: Benchmarking Positional Encoding Strategies for Transformer-Based EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Ayse Betul Yuce, Sebastian Stober

entry.summary: This study benchmarks five positional encoding strategies within the CBraMod backbone for transformer-based EEG foundation models, addressing how spatially distributed electrode positions should be encoded versus textual tokens. It evaluates under linear probing and fine-tuning regimes.

entry.title: Transcribing Children's Speech: ASR Performance and Obtaining Reliable Orthographic Transcriptions

author.name: Gus Lathouwers, Lingyun Gao, Catia Cucchiarini, Helmer Strik

entry.summary: This study evaluates nine ASR models from three families (Whisper, Parakeet, Wav2Vec2) on two Dutch child speech datasets, investigating performance and methods for obtaining reliable orthographic transcriptions in a low-resource setting. It addresses the challenge of automating child speech annotation.

entry.title: Domain-Informed Representation for Evolutionary Sieving in Integral and Module Lattices

author.name: Ahmad Tashfeen, Qi Cheng

entry.summary: This work enhances evolutionary (genetic algorithm) sieving for the Shortest Vector Problem in post-quantum cryptography with domain-informed representations and crossover, extending to module lattices. It targets the backbone hardness assumption of quantum-safe cryptography.

entry.title: Beyond Bilingual Transfer: Multilingual Code-Switching in Instruction Tuning

author.name: Shunta Asano, Jeonghun Baek, Toshihiko Yamasaki

entry.summary: Investigates multilingual code-switching instruction tuning across English, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese, going beyond prior bilingual-only studies. Sentence-level multilingual code-switching consistently improves average multilingual understanding.

entry.title: CRB-Guided Framework Design and Resource Allocation for Indoor mmWave ISCC Systems

author.name: Zhonghao Liu, Yahao Ding, Yinchao Yang, Mohammad Shikh-Bahaei

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Cramer-Rao bound guided resource allocation framework for indoor mmWave integrated sensing, communication, and computation systems to minimize human pose prediction error. It uses an adaptive-depth Mamba-based pose prediction model under communication, latency, and energy constraints.

entry.title: Analyzing Quality-Latency-Resource Trade-offs in a Technical Documentation RAG Assistant Using LoRA Adaptation

author.name: Evgenii Palnikov, Elizaveta Gavrilova

entry.summary: This study analyzes quality-latency-resource trade-offs in a documentation RAG assistant using LoRA, building a 5,144-pair Kubernetes QA benchmark and ablating 20 LoRA configurations on two Llama models. It reports F1, groundedness, latency, memory, and training cost with confidence intervals.

entry.title: ClinicalEncoder26AM: A Multlilingual Diagnosable ColBERT Model; Evidences from the MultiClinNER Shared Task

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois Remy

entry.summary: ClinicalEncoder26AM is a multilingual diagnosable ColBERT model for clinical and biomedical text that aligns token-level semantics to a clinical latent space, built on BGE-M3 with multi-adapter distillation. It is evaluated as a BIO tagger in the MultiClinNER shared task.

entry.title: CAREF: Calibration-Aware Regularization for Explanation Faithfulness Without Rationale Supervision

author.name: Naphat Nithisopa, Teerapong Panboonyuen

entry.summary: Introduces CAREF, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework that jointly optimizes accuracy and explanation faithfulness via a unified calibration-aware sparsity loss without rationale supervision. It achieves strong accuracy and explanation alignment using few trainable parameters on Flan-T5. Matters for efficient faithful explanations.

entry.title: V2XCrafter: Learning to Generate Driving Scene Across Agents

author.name: Yihang Tao, Yu Guo, Senkang Hu, Yanan Ma, Zihan Fang, Sam Kwong, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: V2XCrafter generates synthetic multi-agent driving scenes across vehicles for V2X collaborative perception, addressing data scarcity in real-world V2X datasets. It tackles consistency of physical attributes across agents observing shared objects.

entry.title: MARTIAN: A Rendering Framework for Aerial Mars Imagery from HiRISE Orbital Data

author.name: Dario Pisanti, Georgios Georgakis

entry.summary: MARTIAN is an open-source Blender-based rendering framework that synthesizes realistic aerial Mars views from real HiRISE orbital data with controllable lighting and accurate pose annotations. It addresses the scarcity of training data for vision-based Mars navigation.

entry.title: SLAD : Shared LoRA Adapters for Task Specific Distillation

author.name: Reda Bensaid, Yassir Bendou, Vincent Gripon, Fran\c{c}ois Leduc-Primeau

entry.summary: SLAD proposes shared LoRA adapters for task-specific distillation, where larger and smaller versions of the same foundation model are both adapted to a task to transfer knowledge efficiently. It targets resource-constrained embedded deployment.

entry.title: VFEAgent: A Multimodal Agent Framework for End-to-End Automated Finite Element Analysis

author.name: Jiachen Zhang (Peking University, China Agricultural University), Junyi Lao (Peking University), Chenghao Liu (Peking University), Siyuan Liu (Peking University), Shixin Wu (Peking University), Linsen Zhang (Peking University), Boyu Wang (Peking University), Songfang Huang (Peking University)

entry.summary: Introduces VFEAgent, a multimodal multi-agent system that automates finite-element analysis modeling directly from images and problem descriptions using ReAct-driven reasoning and a verification component. It targets the expertise-heavy engineering simulation workflow.

entry.title: FinVerBench: Benchmark Validity and Calibration in Large Language Model Financial Statement Verification

author.name: Silu Panda

entry.summary: Introduces FinVerBench, a benchmark and validity study for financial-statement verification built from SEC 10-K XBRL filings with a four-category error taxonomy, evaluating fifteen LLMs on numerical consistency. It emphasizes calibration and careful handling of underdetermined instances.

entry.title: Temporal Stability and Few-Shot Prompting in Math Task Assessment

author.name: Danielle S. Fox, Brenda L. Robles, Elizabeth DiPietro Brovey, Christian D. Schunn

entry.summary: This longitudinal study examines whether AI tools (Gemini and education-specific Coteach) maintain stable performance over model updates and respond to few-shot prompting when classifying the cognitive demand of math tasks using the Task Analysis Guide. It addresses temporal stability concerns for educational deployment.

entry.title: Specialty-Specific Medical Language Model for Immune-Mediated Diseases

author.name: Veysel Kocaman, Gursev Pirge, Yigit Gul, Ace Vo, Zhenya Nargizyan, David Talby

entry.summary: A domain-specific NER model for immune-mediated and infectious disease terminology, trained on 371 manually annotated case reports with twelve entity classes. It targets the inconsistency of biomedical terminology that limits general-purpose NLP in clinical settings.

entry.title: Evolutionary Rule Extraction from Corporate Default Prediction Models

author.name: Desir\`e Fabbretti, Matteo Pasquino, Elia Pacioni, Caterina Lucarelli, Davide Calvaresi

entry.summary: Applies explainable AI and evolutionary rule extraction to SME corporate default prediction using a panel of 50,718 Italian firms over 2015-2024, comparing econometric and ML approaches. It aims to balance predictive power with regulatory-compliant interpretability.

entry.title: ExDBSCAN: Explaining DBSCAN with Counterfactual Reasoning -- Additional Material

author.name: Pernille Matthews, Lena Krieger, Tommaso Amico, Artur Zimek, Thomas Seidl, Ira Assent

entry.summary: ExDBSCAN provides counterfactual, density-aware explanations for DBSCAN clustering assignments, addressing the interpretability gap in unsupervised density-based clustering. It offers actionable insight into why points are labeled as inliers or outliers and whether assignments are robust.

entry.title: Gesture-Aware Indoor THz ISAC Systems for Adaptive Resource Allocation
