author.name: Dasol Choi, Alex Kwon

entry.summary: Introduces context-flip evaluation to diagnose brittle safety, where aligned models keep following rigid rules even when situational updates flip which action is actually safe, testing 12 models and finding a mean 17.4pp safety-commonsense gap. Baseline accuracy fails to predict brittleness.

entry.title: Human-like in-group bias in instruction-tuned language model agents

author.name: Messi H. J. Lee

entry.summary: A controlled simulation shows that instruction-tuned LLM agents exhibit human-like in-group favoritism when group labels are visible, across six model families and 500-turn interactions. This is important for understanding emergent social biases in networks of autonomous agents that allocate resources at scale.

entry.title: Where Rollouts Begin: Low-Load, High-Leverage First-Token Diversification for RLVR

author.name: Soeun Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: This paper identifies the first token after the reasoning marker as a low-cost, high-leverage position for diversifying rollouts in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards. Diversifying this sharply peaked but correctness-decoupled first-token distribution broadens exploration cheaply.

entry.title: Cultural Binding Heads in Language Models

author.name: Avrile Floro, Luca Benedetto

entry.summary: Using mechanistic interpretability, this paper identifies 2-3 mid-layer attention heads per model that causally bind cultural items to identities across eight models, with knockouts lowering binding strength and heads transferring from instruct to base models. It locates where cultural difference-awareness arises in pretraining.

entry.title: LACUNA: Safe Agents as Recursive Program Holes

author.name: Yaoyu Zhao, Yichen Xu, Oliver Bra\v{c}evac, Cao Nguyen Pham, Frank Zhengqing Wu, Martin Odersky

entry.summary: LACUNA is a programming model that lets LLM-written code shape the agent runtime through typed recursive program holes while preserving safety, closing the split between runtime and model-written code. From a group including Martin Odersky, it targets expressive yet safe code-acting agents.

entry.title: EvoSpec: Evolving Speculative Decoding via Real-Time Vocabulary and Parameter AdaptationTarget

author.name: Shuyu Zhang, Lingfeng Pan, Qicheng Wang, Yaqi Shi, Yueyang Tan, Ruyu Yan, Jiaqi Chen, Lixing Du, Lu Wang

entry.summary: EvoSpec enables real-time evolution of speculative decoding draft models via dynamic vocabulary and parameter adaptation, retrieving critical long-tail tokens to prevent acceptance-rate drops during domain or topic shifts. It addresses the output projection bottleneck at large vocabulary sizes.

entry.title: Prominence-Stratified Failure Modes in Retrieval-Augmented Commercial Recommendation: A 37,000-Run Audit

author.name: Will Jack, Noah Lehman, Keller Maloney, Sarah Xu

entry.summary: This 37,000-run audit of AI assistants as recommendation engines reveals prominence-stratified failure modes, showing how brands across five awareness tiers fare differently when LLMs nominate brands for commercial queries. It treats marketing to AI as broader than search visibility.

entry.title: Paraphrase Brittleness in Production Retrieval-Augmented Commercial Recommendation: Reproducibility Below the Rerun-Stability Baseline

author.name: Will Jack, Noah Lehman, Keller Maloney, Sarah Xu

entry.summary: This companion audit finds that minor paraphrases of the same buying intent produce substantially different brand recommendations from AI assistants, with similarity (Jaccard 0.135-0.288) far below the same-prompt rerun baseline of 0.50-0.61. It shows the prompt string, not the underlying intent, dominates which brands surface.

entry.title: Pressure-Testing Deception Probes in LLMs: Scaling, Robustness, and the Geometry of Deceptive Representations

author.name: Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: This paper pressure-tests linear deception probes across the Gemma 3 family (1B-27B), showing they report high AUROC on clean benchmarks but collapse under distributional shift, and diagnoses why by testing four hypotheses about deception encoding geometry. It uses cross-domain transfer, multi-dimensional probe analysis, entropy-residualization, and distractor evaluations.

entry.title: How Far Can Disaggregation Go? A Design-Space Exploration of Attention-FFN Disaggregation for Efficient MoE LLM Serving

author.name: Hanjiang Wu, Abhimanyu Rajeshkumar Bambhaniya, Sarbartha Banerjee, Tuhin Khare, Sudarshan Srinivasan, Suvinay Subramanian, Souvik Kundu, Madhu Kumar, Midhilesh Elavazhagan, William Won, Amir Yazdanbakhsh, Tushar Krishna

entry.summary: This paper explores the design space of Attention-FFN Disaggregation for serving Mixture-of-Experts LLMs, where attention and expert-FFN execution are placed on separate GPU groups to handle their distinct resource demands. It systematically maps scheduling tradeoffs across workload, resource allocation, and interconnect levels.

entry.title: Semantic Optimal Transport for Sparse Autoencoder Feature Matching and Circuit Compression

author.name: Tue M. Cao, Nguyen Do, My T. Thai

entry.summary: This paper introduces a distributional optimal-transport framework for matching semantically similar sparse autoencoder features across layers and compressing feature circuits into interpretable supernodes. It unifies both tasks as estimating semantic distances between features on different activation manifolds, representing features as activation-weighted distributions rather than single decoder vectors.

entry.title: Blind PRNG Hijacking: An Undetectable Integrity-Preserving Attack Against LLM Watermarking

author.name: Ziyang You, Huilong He, Xiaoke Yang, Xuxing Lu

entry.summary: SeedHijack is the first supply-chain attack on LLM watermarking that is blind (needs no key or logits), integrity-preserving (amplifies rather than erases the watermark), and orthogonal to detection statistics. It exploits the assumption that the underlying PRNG is trustworthy in schemes like KGW, Unigram, and DipMark.

entry.title: Beyond Binary: Sim-to-Real Dexterous Manipulation with Physics-Grounded Contact Representation

author.name: Jiahe Pan, Stelian Coros, Jitendra Malik, Toru Lin

entry.summary: This work introduces Center-of-Pressure, a physics-grounded tactile representation for sim-to-real dexterous manipulation that preserves dense contact information while remaining robust to the simulation-reality gap, plus a sensor calibration scheme. It avoids the oversimplification of tactile data into coarse features that hampers complex manipulation.

entry.title: Learn from your own latents and not from tokens: A sample-complexity theory

author.name: Daniel J. Korchinski, Alessandro Favero, Matthieu Wyart

entry.summary: Provides a sample-complexity theory for self-supervised latent-prediction methods (JEPA, data2vec) showing how much latent prediction improves data efficiency over token prediction and whether hierarchical stacking helps. It uses a tractable probabilistic data model to answer both questions.

entry.title: Interpretability-Guided Layer Selection over Subspace Projection: SAEs as Stethoscopes, Not Scalpels, for Raw Task Vector Model Editing

author.name: Li Lei, Madalina Ciobanu, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: Rigorously evaluates an SAE-guided model editing pipeline for mathematical reasoning on Gemma-3-4B-IT and uncovers that projecting task vectors onto SAE feature subspaces discards about 97% of modification energy, yielding no significant gains. It argues SAEs serve better as diagnostic tools than editing scalpels.

entry.title: Understanding Generalization and Forgetting in In-Context Continual Learning

author.name: Guangyu Li, Meng Ding, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: Proposes the first theoretical framework for in-context continual learning, modeling how pretrained transformers process sequences of heterogeneous tasks within a single prompt. It derives error expressions for linear and masked linear self-attention capturing generalization and forgetting.

entry.title: Multi-Mixer Models: Flexible Sequence Modeling with Shared Representations

author.name: Kevin Y. Li, Asher Trockman, Ananda Theertha Suresh, Ziteng Sun

entry.summary: Introduces multi-mixer models, a flexible sequence modeling approach with shared representations that combine attention and recurrent token mixers to address long-context retrieval limitations of linear recurrent models. It moves beyond static interleaving of mixer types.

entry.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen or Read? Analyzing and Mitigating Paralinguistic Failures with VoxParadox

author.name: Jiacheng Pang, Ashutosh Chaubey, Mohammad Soleymani

entry.summary: Introduces VoxParadox, an adversarial benchmark of 2,000 examples across 10 paralinguistic tasks where transcript claims and speaking style intentionally mismatch, measuring whether audio LLMs truly listen or just read transcripts. Evaluation reveals models strongly follow language-implied answers over acoustic ground truth.

entry.title: Code as a Weapon: A Consensus-Labeled Prompt Bank for Measuring Coding-Model Compliance with Malicious-Code Requests

author.name: Richard J. Young, Gregory D. Moody

entry.summary: This work introduces a consensus-labeled prompt bank for measuring coding models' compliance with malicious code requests, arguing that code-specialized models should clear a higher refusal bar since compliance yields working weapons. It addresses fragmentation in malicious-code refusal benchmarks.

entry.title: CIRF: Tokenizing Chain-of-Thoughts into Reusable Functional Units for Efficient Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Yukyung Lee, Yumeng Shen, Jinhyeong Park, Hyein Yang, Jun-Hyung Park

entry.summary: CIRF tokenizes chain-of-thought reasoning into reusable discrete functional units to enable more efficient implicit latent reasoning aligned with explicit rationales. It addresses inference cost and adaptivity to example complexity in LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Agentic Separation Logic Specification Synthesis

author.name: Tarun Suresh, David Korczynski, Julien Vanegue

entry.summary: Spec-Agent is an agentic system for synthesizing expressive, well-validated formal specifications from large C++ codebases including separation logic for heap-allocated structures. It targets a ladder of specification languages with systematic validation.

entry.title: No frontier model has acceptable levels of compliance with the EU AI Act and privacy legislation.

author.name: Daan Henselmans

entry.summary: Using dynamic agentic simulations (LARA tool), finds frontier AI models violate EU AI Act and privacy law in up to 93% of tested scenarios, including forbidden practices like covert manipulation and emotion inference, with the best model (Claude Opus 4.7) still breaking the law 46% of the time. It provides an open evaluation tool with viewable transcripts.

entry.title: Do LLMs Build World Models From Text? A Multilingual Diagnostic of Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Zhikai Pan, Chih-Ting Liao, Chunrui Liu, Xi Xiao, Yitong Qiao, Chunlei Meng, Zhangquan Chen, Xin Cao

entry.summary: MentalMap is a multilingual diagnostic benchmark with a six-level capability hierarchy testing whether LLMs build internal spatial world models from text and whether this transfers across eight languages. It systematically probes spatial reasoning, frame of reference, and hallucination across thirteen models.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Lean-as-Judge for Natural-Language Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Pauline Bourigault, Xiaotong Ji, Matthieu Zimmer, Rasul Tutunov, Haitham Bou Ammar

entry.summary: COVCAL is a risk-controlled selector that uses Lean proof-trace diagnostics to certify a finite-sample selective-risk bound when using Lean to judge natural-language math answers, abstaining when unreliable. It shows the Lean signal is sharply coverage-dependent and often unfaithful.

entry.title: AssertLLM2: A Comprehensive LLM Benchmark for Assertion Generation from Design Specifications

author.name: Yuchao Wu, Wenji Fang, Jing Wang, Wenkai Li, Ziyan Guo, Zhiyao Xie

entry.summary: AssertLLM2 is an open-source benchmark for realistic LLM-based assertion generation in hardware verification, with 83 real-world designs across 13 categories, structured specifications, verified golden RTL, and systematic evaluation. It addresses unrealistic task formulations in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Verified Misguidance: Measuring Structural Citation Failures in Search-Augmented LLMs

author.name: Yongsik Seo, Wooseok Jeong, Eunyoung Kim, Hyeonseo Jang, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: CITETRACE is a large-scale dataset tracing full citation chains from query through retrieved source to answer—11,200 queries, 112,000 responses across ten models and five providers—to measure structural citation failures in search-augmented LLMs. It addresses how unverified citations silently mislead users at massive query scale.

entry.title: LLM Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning is an Inference Workload

author.name: Zelin Li, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: Reframes zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning as an inference-dominated workload and executes its repeated scoring phase through a serving runtime like vLLM, achieving large speedups (0.51 vs 4+ hours on OPT-13B). This corrects a workload-runtime mismatch in existing implementations.

entry.title: ROSD: Reflective On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Model Reasoning across Domains

author.name: Ziqi Zhao, Xinyu Ma, Liu Yang, Yujie Feng, Daiting Shi, Jingzhou He, Xin Xin, Zhaochun Ren, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: Proposes ROSD, a reflective on-policy self-distillation framework that turns reference-solution imitation into targeted reasoning correction to improve in-domain and out-of-domain LLM reasoning. It addresses overfitting from imitating training-domain reference trajectories and overwriting valid reasoning prefixes.

entry.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Mind: Unveiling Latent Attack in Latent-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Chenxi Wang, Ruiyang Huang, Jiayan Sun, Lei Wei, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: Studies whether latent states in latent-based multi-agent systems can carry attack-associated information, introducing a framework that reactivates attack effects through latent interventions without reusing adversarial text. Experiments show latent-only attacks substantially degrade task performance during clean executions.

entry.title: Agents that Matter: Optimizing Multi-Agent LLMs via Removal-Based Attribution

author.name: Mingyu Lu, Yushan Huang, Chris Lin, Su-In Lee

entry.summary: This paper formalizes agent attribution in multi-agent systems as a cooperative game and shows Leave-One-Out identifies bottleneck agents as effectively as combinatorial methods at lower cost. It finds introspective LLM judges fail to faithfully approximate ablation-based credit assignment.

entry.title: RULER: Representation-Level Verification of Machine Unlearning

author.name: Georgina Cosma, Axel Finke

entry.summary: Introduces RULER, representation-level verification metrics for machine unlearning that detect whether forgotten records remain encoded in intermediate representations even when output-level tests pass. It includes oracle-comparative and oracle-free metrics for residual detection.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for the Evaluation of LLM Agentic Capabilities

author.name: Pengyu Zhu, Lijun Li, Yaxing Lyu, Qianxin Luo, Jingyi Yang, Yi Liu, Tingfeng Hui, Xinyu Yuan, Li Sun, Sen Su, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Presents a unified framework for fairly evaluating LLM agentic capabilities by standardizing diverse benchmarks into a common instruction-tool-environment format, executing agents via a fixed ReAct architecture in a controllable sandbox with an offline option. It disentangles model capability from benchmark implementation choices.

entry.title: Bridging the Detection-to-Abstention Gap in Reasoning Models under Insufficient Information

author.name: Renjie Gu, Jiaxu Li, Yihao Wang, Yun Yue, Hansong Xiao, Yefei Chen, Yuan Wang, Chunxiao Guo, Pei Wei, Jinjie Gu, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: Identifies the detection-to-abstention gap where reasoning models recognize under-specified questions yet still produce unsupported answers, and proposes Judge-Then-Solve, which forces an explicit answerability commitment before solving. It is especially relevant for high-risk domains like medical AI.

entry.title: OR-Space: A Full-Lifecycle Workspace Benchmark for Industrial Optimization Agents

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Xinyun Lu, Jiangyue Zhao, Jianghao Lin, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye

entry.summary: OR-Space is a full-lifecycle workspace benchmark for industrial optimization agents covering model construction, revision, and grounded explanation rather than one-shot translation. It matters for realistically evaluating LLM agents in operations research workflows.

entry.title: Learning When to Optimize: Verified Optimization Skills from Expert GPU-Kernel Lineages

author.name: Shuoming Zhang, Qiuchu Yu, Yangyu Zhang, Ruiyuan Xu, Xiyu Shi, Guangli Li, Xiaobing Feng, Huimin Cui, Jiacheng Zhao

entry.summary: KLineage learns when GPU-kernel optimizations are sound by walking expert implementations backward through validation-gated simplifications into reusable skills, rather than relying on forward rollouts. It improves LLM-based kernel generation with correctness-aware optimization knowledge.

entry.title: SafeMed-R1: Clinician-Audited Safety and Ethics Alignment for Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Chao Ding, Mouxiao Bian, Tianbin Li, Minjia Yuan, Yidong Jiang, Yankai Jiang, Jinru Ding, Jiayuan Chen, Zhuangzhi Gao, Pengcheng Chen, Zhao He, Rongzhao Zhang, Meiling Liu, Luyi Jiang, Jie Xu

entry.summary: SafeMed-R1 is a medical LLM trained with a traceable Clinical Trust Signals pipeline linking reasoning to clinician rubric scores, plus safety/ethics alignment and red-team testing. It improves auditability and reduces unsafe outputs while maintaining clinical accuracy.

entry.title: HRBench: Benchmarking and Understanding Thinking-Mode Switch Strategies in Hybrid-Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Yansong Ning, Mianpeng Liu, Jingwen Ye, Weidong Zhang, Hao Liu

entry.summary: HRBench is a unified framework benchmarking thinking-mode switch strategies in hybrid-reasoning LLMs across three switching strategy families and four training regimes, yielding 12 controlled settings. It enables fair comparison of adaptive reasoning-effort selection methods.

entry.title: DenoiseRL: Bootstrapping Reasoning Models to Recover from Noisy Prefixes

author.name: Caijun Xu, Changyi Xiao, Zhongyuan Peng, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: DenoiseRL is a reinforcement learning framework that learns from weak models' incorrect reasoning traces by converting failures into recovery opportunities, removing dependence on stronger teachers or curated hard data. It makes reasoning RL more scalable and self-sufficient.

entry.title: A Matter of TASTE: Improving Coverage and Difficulty of Agent Benchmarks

author.name: Tomer Keren, Nitay Calderon, Asaf Yehudai, Yotam Perlitz, Michal Shmueli-Scheuer, Roi Reichert

entry.summary: TASTE reverses agent benchmark construction by synthesizing tasks from evolving tool sequences using an adaptive contrastive n-gram model, generating harder tasks with broader tool-use coverage than natural-language-first approaches. It addresses saturation of existing agent benchmarks.

entry.title: TRACER: Turn-level Regret Matching with Inner Reinforcement Credit for Cooperative Multi-LLM Reasoning

author.name: Chusen Li, Zhou Liu, Shuigeng Zhou, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: TRACER is a turn-level reinforcement framework for cooperative multi-LLM reasoning that uses a controller-regret layer to decide whether agents speak or skip each round and inner reinforcement credit assignment. It addresses sparse rewards, free-riding, and oscillating local optima in multi-agent RL.

entry.title: AlphaTransit: Learning to Design City-scale Transit Routes

author.name: Bibek Poudel, Sai Swaminathan, Weizi Li

entry.summary: AlphaTransit applies Monte Carlo Tree Search coupled with a neural policy-value network to design city-scale bus transit networks under delayed simulator feedback. It tackles the deceptive route-interaction problem in the Transit Route Network Design Problem.

entry.title: RAG-Coding: Enhancing LLM Medical Coding with Structured External Knowledge

author.name: Yidong Gan, David D. Nguyen, Yang Lin, Peter Zhong, Thanh Vu, Long Duong, Yuan-Fang Li

entry.summary: RAG-Coding is an agentic four-LLM-agent method for automated ICD-10-CM medical coding that grounds decisions in official coding tabular lists and guidelines. It outperforms LLM baselines by 8-13% micro-F1 on the MDACE dataset.

entry.title: Smaller, Younger, and More Impactful: How AI-Assisted Writing Transforms Research Teams

author.name: Haoyang Wang, Mingze Zhang, Yi Bu, Star Xing Zhao, Meijun Liu

entry.summary: Drawing on 147,074 full-text publications from PLoS and Nature since 2020, this large-scale bibliometric study finds AI-assisted writing is associated with smaller, younger, and more impactful research teams. It suggests LLMs may disrupt the long trend toward ever-larger teams.

entry.title: AgensFlow: A Coordination-Policy Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Nicole Koenigstein

entry.summary: AgensFlow is an open-source framework treating multi-agent LLM coordination as an online policy-learning problem under partial observability, making coordination decisions (protocol, role, model binding, retrieval timing) observable and learnable. It moves beyond static pipelines and one-off comparisons.

entry.title: Energy-Structured Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning

author.name: Longhua Li, Lei Qi, Qi Tian, Xin Geng

entry.summary: E2-LoRA is an energy-concentrated, energy-ordered low-rank adaptation method for continual learning that concentrates knowledge into leading ranks to free capacity for future tasks, motivated by the proof that output feature drift is inherently low-rank. It minimizes output reconstruction error.

entry.title: Grounded Cache Routing for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: When Is It Safe to Reuse an Answer?

author.name: Syed Huma Shah (Duke University)

entry.summary: GroundedCache reframes RAG output-level answer caching around the question of when reuse is safe rather than how to reuse faster, addressing risks where similar prompts map to different correct answers, evidence drifts, and adversarial collisions hijack cached responses. It proposes grounded cache routing.

entry.title: Tensor Memory: Fixed-Size Recurrent State for Long-Horizon Transformers

author.name: Kabir Swain, Sijie Han, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Mauro Martino, Antonio Torralba

entry.summary: Tensor Memory augments transformer blocks with a fixed-size recurrent 3D voxel memory tensor that tokens write into via differentiable Gaussian-weighted volumes and read back via continuous queries. It targets long-horizon video understanding and occlusion-sensitive spatial reasoning.

entry.title: Restoring the Sweet Spot: Pass-Rate Weighted Self-Distillation for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zehao Liu, Yuanpu Cao, Jinghui Chen, Vasant G. Honavar

entry.summary: This work analyzes why Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) lacks GRPO's implicit difficulty awareness and proposes pass-rate weighted self-distillation to restore concentration on intermediate-difficulty questions. It extends the learnability framework to understand reward normalization effects in LLM RL reasoning.

entry.title: When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?

author.name: Yuan Tian, Bing Hu, Fang Wu, Xiaomin Li, Binghang Lu, Neil Zhenqiang Gong

entry.summary: This paper studies which think-with-image reasoning paradigms improve multimodal jailbreak robustness across vision-language models, finding explicit external image-tool invocation yields the lowest attack success rates (about 30% relative reduction). It investigates why tool-based interaction provides robustness even when returned content is unhelpful.

entry.title: On the Learnability of Test-Time Adaptation: A Recovery Complexity Perspective

author.name: Zhi Zhou, Ming Yang, Shi-Yu Tian, Kun-Yang Yu, Lan-Zhe Guo, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes the first theoretical framework for the learnability of test-time adaptation under non-stationary streams, introducing Recovery Complexity and TTA Learnability that capture distribution shifts and information constraints. It provides principled foundations aligning with TTA objectives.

entry.title: DEPART: DEcomposing PARiTy across Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Manan Uppadhyay, Prashant Kodali, Pranjal Chitale, Reshma Ramaprasad, Himanshu Beniwal, Sunayana Sitaram

entry.summary: DEPART presents a Bayesian hierarchical framework that decomposes multilingual LLM performance variance into interpretable components, showing that observable language features like script and typological distance explain most of the variance. It moves beyond reporting per-language accuracy to attributing causes of disparity, giving practitioners actionable levers.

entry.title: Do LLMs Favor Their Providers? Measuring Vertical Integration Bias in Code Generation

author.name: Melih Catal, Alex Wolf, Tiago Ferreiro Matos, Pooja Rani, Harald Gall

entry.summary: This work defines Vertical Integration Bias—whether provider-affiliated LLMs favor their own ecosystem in generated code—and introduces VIBench to measure it across 20 integration scenarios. Evaluating 10 affiliated models against 3 controls reveals positive bias in direct and agentic code generation.

entry.title: The Attentional White Bear Effect in Transformer Language Models

author.name: Rebecca Ramnauth, Brian Scassellati

entry.summary: This study finds that instruction-based suppression of prohibited concepts in transformer LMs reduces expression but not internal representation: prohibited concepts remain recoverable from hidden states, influence attention routing, and shape downstream generations despite lexical avoidance. The effect persists across pooling strategies and model families, exposing a gap between suppression and true removal.

entry.title: Extrapolative Weight Averaging Reveals Correctness-Efficiency Frontiers in Code RL

author.name: Kunhao Zheng, Pierre Chambon, Juliette Decugis, Jonas Gehring, Taco Cohen, Benjamin Negrevergne, Gabriel Synnaeve

entry.summary: This work studies whether extrapolative weight averaging between fine-tuned checkpoints can extend Pareto frontiers to new inference-useful checkpoints without extra RL training, applied to RL for competitive programming where hidden unit tests enforce correctness and efficiency. Training under nested unit-test coverage reveals an emergent correctness-efficiency frontier.

entry.title: Cyclical Entropy Eruption: Entropy Dynamics in Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wendi Li, Shawn Im, Sharon Li

entry.summary: Identifies cyclical entropy eruption, a recurring phenomenon in agentic LLM RL where entropy sharply spikes in cycles, unlike single-turn reasoning RL where entropy collapses. This characterizes a previously underexplored training-dynamics instability for multi-turn agent RL.

entry.title: Off-Policy Learning to Reason Works Because It Is More Pessimistic Than You Think

author.name: Otmane Sakhi, Aleksei Arzhantsev, Imad Aouali, Flavian Vasile

entry.summary: Argues that off-policy learning to reason works because removing importance weights yields an implicitly more pessimistic objective than PPO-style trust-region methods, avoiding variance and entropy collapse from importance-weight corrections. It theoretically reframes why weight-free off-policy RL outperforms corrected variants.

entry.title: Augmenting Attention with Exponentially Decaying Memory Improves Query-Aware KV Sparsity

author.name: Xiuying Wei, Caglar Gulcehre

entry.summary: Investigates whether exponentially decaying recurrent memory (RAT+) can improve query-aware sparse attention inference methods like Quest, MoBA, and SnapKV. Shows consistent accuracy gains on needle-in-a-haystack tasks across sparse budgets.

entry.title: Principled Algorithms for Optimizing Generalized Metrics in Multi-Label Learning

author.name: Mehryar Mohri, Yutao Zhong

entry.summary: Develops principled learning algorithms with H-consistency guarantees for optimizing generalized metrics like F-measure and Jaccard index in multi-label learning. It designs novel surrogate losses admitting non-asymptotic guarantees within the empirical utility maximization framework.

entry.title: Evolving and Detecting Multi-Turn Deception using Geometric Signatures

author.name: Surender Suresh Kumar, Mary L. Cummings

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline that evolves realistic multi-turn deceptive question sets via multi-objective genetic prompt optimization and detects deception using explainable geometric signals in embedding space. A human study validates the dataset and reveals practical constraints.

entry.title: Smoothed Score Queries and the Complexity of Sampling

author.name: Jingbo Liu

entry.summary: Studies the query complexity of sampling from high-dimensional Gaussians, showing the polynomial approximation barrier and square-root-condition-number dependence vanish when the sampler can query smoothed scores (gradients of Gaussian-convolved log densities). Smoothed-score queries give access to a resolvent enabling faster sampling.

entry.title: MRMMIA: Membership Inference Attacks on Memory in Chat Agents

author.name: Kai Chen, Yan Pang, Tianhao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes MRMMIA, a multi-recall membership inference attack against the memory stores of chat agents, inferring whether candidate memory units belong to an agent's memory. It extends MIA research beyond training corpora and retrieval databases to agent memory privacy.

entry.title: AdaDPO: Self-Adaptive Direct Preference Optimization with Balanced Gradient Updates

author.name: Shaolong Chen, Madalina Ciobanu, Qingqing Mao, Ritankar Das

entry.summary: AdaDPO addresses the asymmetric gradient problem in Direct Preference Optimization by introducing per-pair stop-gradient coefficients that equalize gradient magnitudes between preferred and dispreferred responses. It aims to make models learn to generate good answers rather than just avoid bad ones.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Neglect: Steering via Context-Preference for MLLM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Jingwen Wu, Xijun Zhang, Ge Song

entry.summary: ResearchMath-14k is the largest collection of research-level mathematical problems to date, curated from academic sources via a multi-agent pipeline, plus 220K teacher reasoning trajectories. The authors observe recurring avoidance behaviors like non-attempts and fabricated references in model outputs.

entry.title: ATLAS: All-round Testing of Long-context Abilities across Scales

author.name: Deli Huang, Cunguang Wang, Hongyin Tang, Zhe Tang, Linsen Guo, Dongyu Ru, Ruoshi Yuan, Ziyue Zhu, Xiaoyu Li, Ziwen Wang, Chen Zhang, Anchun Gui, Wen Zan, Jiaqi Zhang, Xuezhi Cao, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: ATLAS redefines long-context evaluation as length-dependent capability profiling, with a layered taxonomy, length-aware AUC scoring over an 8K-1M grid, and a composite ATLAScore, exposing performance collapse and retrieval-to-downstream transfer failures. It moves beyond single-length single-task evaluation.

entry.title: Skill0.5: Joint Skill Internalization and Utilization for Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiapeng Zhu, Jianxiang Yu, Yibo Zhao, Chengcheng Han, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Xiang Li, Weining Qian

entry.summary: Skill0.5 is an agentic RL framework that combines general skill internalization with task-specific skill externalization to improve out-of-distribution generalization. It avoids the rigid choice between context overhead and overfitting in skill-based agents.

entry.title: GUI-CIDER: Mid-training GUI Agents via Causal Internalization and Density-aware Exemplar Reselection

author.name: Zheng Wu, Chengcheng Han, Zhengxi Lu, Tianjie Ju, Yanyu Chen, Qi Gu, Xunliang Cai, Zhuosheng Zhang

entry.summary: GUI-CIDER is a mid-training method for GUI agents using causal internalization and density-aware exemplar reselection to enable explicit learning of GUI operation world knowledge. It addresses the inefficiency of pure SFT or RL post-training.

entry.title: Can LLMs Use Linguistic Uncertainty Markers to Reliably Reflect Intrinsic Confidence?

author.name: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: This study formalizes marker internal confidence to test whether LLMs can stably associate linguistic uncertainty markers like 'it is likely' with specific intrinsic confidence levels. It introduces seven stability metrics across distributions.

entry.title: SilentRetrieval: Hijacking Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Semantically-Preserving Adversarial Data Poisoning

author.name: Jiachen Qian

entry.summary: SilentRetrieval is a two-stage data poisoning attack on RAG systems using coordinated beam search and context-adaptive trigger generation to craft fluent yet adversarial documents. It achieves high hijack rates with low perplexity poisoned documents.

entry.title: AndroidDaily: A Verifiable Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents on Real-World Closed-Source Applications

author.name: Yifan Sui, Xin Huang, Hongbing Li, Fang Xu, Jiahe Lv, Haolong Yan, Yeqing Shen, Litao Liu, Zhimin Fan, Ziyang Meng, Jia Wang, Junbo Qi, Kaijun Tan, Zheng Ge, Xiangyu Zhang, Daxin Jiang, Osamu Yoshie

entry.summary: AndroidDaily is a verifiable benchmark of 350 realistic daily-use tasks across 94 closed-source Android apps, addressing the lack of evaluation on opaque real-world applications. It introduces verification methods that work without internal app state access.

entry.title: Proprio: Latent Self-Scoring and Inference-Time Refinement for Physically Plausible Video Generation

author.name: Mariam Hassan, Kaouther Messaoud, Wuyang Li, Alexandre Alahi

entry.summary: Proprio is a training-free framework that lets a frozen video generator self-assess and improve the physical plausibility of its own outputs using flow residuals under latent perturbations as a self-scoring signal. It applies this for best-of-N search and gradient-based self-refinement at inference time.

entry.title: DriveWAM: Video Generative Priors Enable Scalable World-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Chen Shi, Jinrui Xu, Shaoshuai Shi, Kehua Sheng, Bo Zhang, Li Jiang

entry.summary: DriveWAM adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer into an autoregressive video-action policy for autonomous driving, organizing video and action streams into a unified token sequence trained with joint flow-matching. It leverages video generative priors for world-action modeling.

entry.title: You Live More Than Once: Towards Hierarchical Skill Meta-Evolving

author.name: Xujun Li, Kehan Zheng, Mingyuan Zhao, Yize Geng, Jinfeng Zhou, Qi Zhu, Fei Mi, Lifeng Shang, Minlie Huang, Hongning Wang

entry.summary: HiSME is a lightweight hierarchical skill meta-evolving framework that jointly optimizes skills and the skill-evolving strategy by learning meta-skills from agents' task traces at test time, without expensive parameter updates. It enables continuous test-time improvement of agentic systems.

entry.title: DREAM-R: Multimodal Speculative Reasoning with RL-Based Refined Drafting, Precise Verification, and Fully Parallel Execution

author.name: Yunhai Hu, Zining Liu, Xiangyang Yin, Tianhua Xia, Bo Bao, Eric Sather, Vithursan Thangarasa, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: DREAM-R improves multimodal speculative reasoning with Speculative Alignment Policy Optimization that trains draft models for faithful concise reasoning, a threshold-based verification mechanism, and fully parallel execution. It accelerates reasoning-intensive generation in large multimodal models.

entry.title: SNARE: Adaptive Scenario Synthesis for Eliciting Overeager Behavior in Coding Agents

author.name: Yubin Qu, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Yanjun Zhang, Yuekang Li, Ying Zhang, Leo Yu Zhang

entry.summary: SNARE is an adaptive scenario-synthesis pipeline that composes benign tasks to elicit overeager behavior in coding agents—out-of-scope actions like leaking credentials or deleting files even when the benign task succeeds. It adapts scenarios per agent-model pair, unlike fixed-prompt prior overeager benchmarks.

entry.title: Privately Estimating Monotone Statistics in Polynomial Time

author.name: Gavin Brown, Ephraim Linder, Mahbod Majid, Vikrant Singhal

entry.summary: Develops efficient differentially private polynomial-time algorithms for estimating monotone statistics, improving on subsample-and-aggregate by saving a factor in sample complexity at the cost of running time. It complements results with query-complexity lower bounds.

entry.title: Stay Fair! Ensuring Group Fairness in Diffusion Models Across Guidance Scales

author.name: Myeongsoo Kim, Eunji Kim, Minwoo Chae, Sangwoo Mo

entry.summary: Identifies that diffusion model debiasing degrades when users change the guidance scale, decomposing total bias into model bias and guidance bias and showing the latter grows monotonically with guidance. It extends Strong Demographic Parity to guidance to maintain fair group ratios across scales.

entry.title: Retrieval, Reward, and Training Protocols: What Matters in Training Search Agents?

author.name: Yibo Zhao, Zichen Ding, Jiayi Wu, Zun Wang, Xiang Li

entry.summary: This controlled empirical study isolates three under-explored dimensions of search agent training, finding that correcting a data-coverage issue in the Wikipedia 2018 corpus yields larger gains than differences between training algorithms. It systematically compares retrieval, reward, and training protocols.

entry.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: Targeted Routing Hijacking in Federated RAG

author.name: Junjie Mu, Qiongxiu Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces Routing Hijacking, an attack on Federated RAG where a malicious client forges its semantic profile to attract target queries despite holding irrelevant data. It shows severe downstream disruptions including poisoning and hallucinations across three routing architectures.

entry.title: GraphSteal: Structural Knowledge Stealing from Graph RAG via Traversal Reconstruction

author.name: Jinze Gu, Qinghua Mao, Xi Lin, Jun Wu

entry.summary: GraphSteal demonstrates that Graph RAG systems can be turned into structural oracles, allowing adversaries to reconstruct hidden knowledge graphs through adaptive black-box interactions. It proposes a structure-oriented reconstruction framework via traversal.

entry.title: LaneRoPE: Positional Encoding for Collaborative Parallel Reasoning and Generation

author.name: Gabriele Cesa, Thomas Hehn, Aleix Torres-Camps, \`Alex Batlle Casellas, Jordi Ros-Giralt, Arash Behboodi, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy

entry.summary: Proposes LaneRoPE, a positional-encoding extension and inter-sequence attention mask enabling collaboration among parallel generated sequences in best-of-N test-time scaling, so sampled sequences condition on one another. It aims to improve accuracy while keeping batching efficiency.

entry.title: EgoBench: An Interactive Egocentric Multimodal Benchmark for Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yunqi Liu, Tong Niu, Zitong Wang, Zhenlong Dai, Yuqi Qing, Weiqiang Wang, Jian Liu

entry.summary: Introduces EgoBench, the first interactive multimodal benchmark for tool-using agents with 1,045 egocentric-video-grounded tasks across daily scenarios and a user-agent-tool interactive environment. It jointly evaluates perception, multi-hop tool reasoning, and dynamic user interaction.

entry.title: Verifiable Benchmarking of Long-Horizon Spatial Biology

author.name: Ian Diks, Harihara Muralidharan, Tim Proctor, Kenny Workman

entry.summary: Introduces SpatialBench-Long, a benchmark for long-horizon spatial biology where agents must recover biological claims from raw or near-raw spatial measurement data without prescribed methods, spanning 24 evaluations across multiple cancer and aging systems and platforms. It tests end-to-end scientific reasoning over spatial omics.

entry.title: BlazeEdit: Generalist Image Editing on Mobile Devices with Image-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Fei Deng, Yanwu Xu, Zhipeng Bao, Zhixing Zhang, Haolin Jia, Karthik Raveendran, Jianing Wei

entry.summary: Presents BlazeEdit, an efficient generalist image-to-image diffusion model for on-device editing that eliminates text-conditioning components (since many editing tasks need no text guidance) and uses a multi-task architecture for mobile deployment. It is far smaller than existing 0.5-1B mobile diffusion models.

entry.title: Data-Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Yu Lin, Yiming Wang, Runyuan Cai, Xiaodong Zeng

entry.summary: Ark-ASR demonstrates that on-policy distillation from a strong Qwen-ASR teacher can build competitive speech recognition with only 100k hours of audio versus the 20M hours typical for top models. This shows substantial data efficiency gains for ASR specialization.

entry.title: Agentic Active Omni-Modal Perception for Multi-Hop Audio-Visual Reasoning

author.name: Ke Xu, Yuhao Wang, Ziyang Cheng, Hongcheng Liu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: MOV-Bench introduces 519 questions requiring multi-hop reasoning over temporally dispersed audio-visual evidence, and AOP-Agent provides an agentic framework for active omni-modal perception. It exposes weaknesses of current Omni-LLMs on cross-modal multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: From Knowing to Doing: A Memory-Controlled Benchmark for LLM Trading Agents on Stock Markets

author.name: Taojie Zhu, Wentao Zhao, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Jiacheng Lu, Sinuo Wang, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Yonghong He, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: KTD-Fin is a memory-controlled trading benchmark that addresses two evaluation failures in LLM trading agents: data contamination from knowledge cutoffs and raw returns being noisy proxies for genuine alpha. It separates knowing from doing in financial decision-making.

entry.title: Diffusion Large Language Models for Visual Speech Recognition

author.name: Jeong Hun Yeo, Chae Won Kim, Hyeongseop Rha, Yong Man Ro

entry.summary: DLLM-VSR is presented as the first diffusion-LLM-based visual speech recognition framework, replacing left-to-right autoregressive decoding with iterative masked denoising and flexible-order, confidence-based unmasking. It avoids premature decisions on visually ambiguous tokens.

entry.title: Continual Model Routing in Evolving Model Hubs

author.name: Jack Bell, Giacomo Carf\`i, Gerlando Gramaglia, Vincenzo Lomonaco

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Continual Model Routing for evolving model hubs, introduces CMRBench with over 2,000 candidate models, and proposes CARvE, a contrastive embedding approach with checkpoint anchoring and structured replay. It addresses scaling and continually updating mixture-of-experts routing as hubs grow.

entry.title: Satisfiability Solving with LLMs: A Matched-Pair Evaluation of Reasoning Capability

author.name: Leizhen Zhang, Shuhan Chen, Sheng Chen

entry.summary: This paper systematically evaluates LLMs on 2-SAT and 3-SAT plus reductions to Vertex Cover and 3D packing, finding standard metrics misleading because models over-predict satisfiability and fail to reproduce the classical easy-hard-easy phase transition. It probes representation-invariant reasoning on satisfiability.

entry.title: Multi-Adapter Representation Interventions via Energy Calibration

author.name: Manjiang Yu, Hongji Li, Junwei Chen, Xue Li, Priyanka Singh, Yang Cao, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: MARI proposes adaptive, per-input representation interventions for LLM alignment using a competitive multi-adapter mechanism with energy calibration, avoiding the capability degradation caused by uniform interventions. It targets behavior steering without weight modification.

entry.title: Bridging the Stability-Expressivity Gap: Synthetic Data Scaling and Preference Alignment for Low-Resource Spoken Language Models

author.name: Yizhong Geng, Yanliang Li, Jinghan Yang, Tianhan Jiang, Boxun An, Ya Li, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: This work identifies a Stability-Expressivity Gap in spoken language models for low-resource languages, where synthetic data improves phonetic accuracy but suppresses prosodic variability, causing expressivity collapse. It proposes preference alignment to bridge the gap.

entry.title: Human-AI Collaboration for Estimating Scientific Replicability

author.name: Tatiana Chakravorti, Robert Fraleigh, Timothy Fritton, Christopher Griffin, Vaibhav Singh, Sai Koneru, C. Lee Giles, David Pennock, Anthony Kwasnica, Sarah Rajtmajer

entry.summary: This paper introduces a hybrid prediction market combining algorithmic agents and human forecasters to estimate scientific replicability, aiming to overcome limitations of pure human judgment or ML-only approaches. It addresses the long-standing replication crisis challenge.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fairness in Spiking Neural Networks: Data Bias, Spurious Features, and Hardware Effects

author.name: Hudi He, Fukun Wang, Zhe Wang, Xinyi Wang, Shuhan Ye, Jiarui Liu, Qing Qing, Ziqi Xu, Xikun Zhang, Renqiang Luo

entry.summary: This work introduces the first systematic fairness benchmark for Spiking Neural Networks, covering demographic coverage gaps, spurious feature leakage, and deployment-environment mismatches across four datasets and neuromorphic hardware simulators like Loihi 2 and SpiNNaker. It isolates how hardware affects fairness.

entry.title: Tackling Multimodal Learning Challenges with Mixture-of-Expert: A Survey

author.name: Liangwei Nathan Zheng, Wei Emma Zhang, Olaf Maennel, Lin Yue, Weitong Chen

entry.summary: This survey systematically reviews how Mixture-of-Experts addresses multimodal learning challenges, organizing methods around MoE as an efficient engine, modality balancer, and interaction modeler. It fills a gap where prior surveys treat MoE and multimodal learning separately.

entry.title: AdaMerge: Salience-Aware Adaptive Token Merging for Training-Free Acceleration of Vision Transformers

author.name: Semi Lee, Hyejin Go, Hyesong Choi

entry.summary: AdaMerge is a training-free token merging framework for Vision Transformers that uses salience-weighted similarity to address the false token-equality premise of prior methods, reducing information loss in high-salience tokens under aggressive compression. It accelerates ViT inference without retraining.

entry.title: Detect by Yourself: Self-Designing Agentic Workflows for Few-Shot Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tairan Huang, Qiang Chen, Yili Wang, Yueyue Ma, Changlong He, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: SignGAD reformulates few-shot graph anomaly detection from training a fixed detector to self-designing task-conditioned agentic workflows, addressing fixed pipelines and weak evidence in existing methods. It explicitly incorporates contextual and structural anomaly signals.

entry.title: On the Subgaussianity of Quantized Linear Maps: An AI-Assisted Note

author.name: Guangyi Zou, Roman Vershynin

entry.summary: This short note presents a dimension-independent subgaussian concentration bound for Gaussian vectors under coordinate-wise nonlinear maps, applied to sign-quantized linear maps, with the result reportedly discovered by Gemini 3.5 Flash. Co-authored by Roman Vershynin.

entry.title: Hurwitz Quaternion Multiplicative Quantization for KV Cache Compression

author.name: Kabir Swain, Sijie Han, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Mauro Martino, David Cox, Antonio Torralba

entry.summary: HQMQ is a calibration-free KV cache compression method that treats 4-element chunks as quaternions and quantizes directions using the 24-element Hurwitz group times a random secondary codebook. The multiplicative composition yields many effective codewords with few stored parameters.

entry.title: MemGuard: Preventing Memory Contamination in Long-Term Memory-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Hyeonjeong Ha, Jeonghwan Kim, Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, William M. Campbell, Yue Wu, Yuji Zhang, Kathleen McKeown, Dilek Hakkani-Tur, Heng Ji

entry.summary: MemGuard is a type-aware long-term memory framework that preserves functional boundaries between stable user facts, episodic events, and behavioral rules to prevent heterogeneous memory contamination in memory-augmented LLMs. It avoids overgeneralizing context-specific events into broad claims during retrieval and generation.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Context-Aware Prompt Injection against Mobile GUI Agents via User-Generated Content

author.name: Ruoqi Guo, Yi Liu, Gelei Deng, Yiheng Xiong, Yuekang Li, Ying Zhang, Leo Yu Zhang, Lida Zhao, Ji Jie, Yuxiao Lu

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a context-aware prompt injection pipeline against mobile GUI agents that embeds attacker-controlled text into user-generated content regions of benign screenshots, without modifying the agent, app, or OS. It exposes that VLM-driven GUI agents cannot reliably separate trusted interface elements from user content.

entry.title: IRDS: Interpretable RLVR Data Selection via Verifier-Coupled Sparse Autoencoder Coverage

author.name: Yuhan Li, Mingxu Zhang, Dazhong Shen, Ying Sun

entry.summary: IRDS selects training data for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using sparse autoencoder clusters, making selection auditable on recognizable problem motifs while targeting instances the model fails but can learn from. It combines verifier signals with interpretable coverage via greedy log-determinant maximization.

entry.title: CLANE: Continual Learning of Actions on Neuromorphic Hardware from Event Cameras

author.name: Elvin Hajizada, Michael Neumeier, Edward Paxon Frady, Yulia Sandamirskaya, Axel von Arnim, Bing Li, Eyke H\"ullermeier

entry.summary: CLANE is the first end-to-end continual on-device learning pipeline for event-based action recognition deployed on Intel Loihi 2 neuromorphic hardware, combining a spiking CNN with continual learning to recognize new actions without forgetting. It targets privacy-preserving, low-latency adaptation for AR/VR and robotics.

entry.title: Position: Retire the "Positive Backdoor" Label -- Secret Alignment Requires Strict and Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Jianwei Li, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: This position paper argues the community should retire the 'positive backdoor' label and instead treat trigger-activated hidden behaviors as 'Secret Alignment' that must be presumed insecure unless rigorously evaluated. It unifies existing proposals and calls for strict, standardized evaluation in the private/open-weight AI era.

entry.title: A Simple State Space Model Excels at Multivariate Time Series Classification

author.name: Hassan Saadatmand, Geoffrey I. Webb, Hamid Rezatofighi, Mahsa Salehi

entry.summary: This paper presents the first systematic study spanning diagonal SSMs (S4D) and input-dependent SSMs (Mamba family) on large-scale multivariate time series classification benchmarks, finding the surprising result that simpler S4D consistently outperforms Mamba variants in both accuracy and efficiency. It challenges the assumption that input-dependent complexity is necessary for top TSC performance.

entry.title: Heterogeneous Parallelism for Multimodal Large Language Model Training

author.name: Yashaswi Karnati, Kamran Jafari, Akash Mehra, Li Ding, Pranav Prashant Thombre, Ali Roshan Ghias, Shifang Xu, Parth Mannan, Yu Yao, Hao Wu, Eric Harper, Ashwath Aithal, Nima Tajbakhsh

entry.summary: Proposes heterogeneous parallelism for multimodal LLM training, letting encoder and LLM modules use independent TP/CP/PP/DP/EP layouts rather than a single LLM-centric sharding scheme. This improves throughput especially at long contexts where encoder and LLM parallelism needs diverge.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning Dynamics of In-Context Factual Recall in Transformers

author.name: Ruomin Huang, Eshaan Nichani, Jason D. Lee, Rong Ge

entry.summary: Duplicate position note.

entry.title: AtomComposer: Discovering Chemical Space from First Principles with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bjarke Hastrup, Francois Cornet, Tejs Vegge, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: AtomComposer is a self-guided RL agent that autonomously constructs valid 3D molecular isomers under stoichiometric constraints, trained entirely online without any pretraining data to explore chemical space from first principles. A multi-composition training scheme enables broad generalization beyond single chemical formulas.

entry.title: High Performance, Low Reliability: Uncertainty Benchmarking for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Jos\'e Lucas De Melo Costa, Fabrice Popineau, Arpad Rimmel, Bich-Li\^en Doan

entry.summary: Benchmarks uncertainty quantification of tabular foundation models versus gradient-boosted trees across 112 datasets, revealing a performance-uncertainty trade-off where TFMs win on accuracy but offer worse conformal coverage. This highlights trustworthiness gaps in increasingly popular tabular foundation models.

entry.title: When Interpretability Is Unequally Distributed: Fairness in Hybrid Interpretable Models

author.name: Ziba Jabbar Zare, Ulrich A\"ivodji, Julien Ferry, Thibaut Vidal

entry.summary: Formalizes Interpretability Coverage Disparity, a fairness concern where hybrid interpretable models route some demographic groups to transparent decisions while disproportionately deferring others to a black box. It studies this disparity across multiple hybrid methods and fairness benchmarks.

entry.title: Activation Steering for Synthetic Data Generation: The Role of Diversity in Downstream Safety Detection

author.name: Vijeta Deshpande, Tootiya Giyahchi, Veena Padmanabhan, Leman Akoglu, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Investigates whether activation steering can generate high-quality synthetic training data for downstream safety classifiers, introducing diversity as a previously absent quality axis. It evaluates across four concepts, two models, and four steering methods with intrinsic and extrinsic measures.

entry.title: Representation-Conditioned Diffusion Models for Guided Training Data Generation

author.name: Nithesh Chandher Karthikeyan, Jonas Unger, Gabriel Eilertsen

entry.summary: Evaluates classifiers trained on synthetic images from latent diffusion models conditioned on learned representations from DINOv2, DINOv3, and CLIP. Representation-conditioned generation significantly outperforms class-conditioned generation (+10.76 points top-1 on ImageNet100).

entry.title: Disentangling Language Roles in Multilingual LLM Task Execution

author.name: Qishi Zhan, Minxuan Hu, Seoyeon Jang, Lei Zhao, Ziheng Chen, Man Liang, Xinyue Xiang, Jiaxin Liu, Guansu Wang, Liang He

entry.summary: Introduces MTM-Bench, a controlled benchmark that fully crosses instruction language, content language, and response language across English, Spanish, and Chinese (27 triplets). It evaluates 20 LLMs to disentangle the three language roles in multilingual task execution.

entry.title: Soft Specialists: $\alpha$-R\'enyi Ensembles for Uncertainty-Aware LLM Post-Training

author.name: Paula Cordero-Encinar, Georgy Tyukin, Andrew B. Duncan

entry.summary: Proposes an alpha-Renyi variational framework for learning distributions over LLM post-training parameters, offering an uncertainty-aware alternative to deep ensembles. The objective interpolates between variational Bayes and predictively oriented posterior learning to balance plausible models against complementary specialists.

entry.title: Learning to target with network interference

author.name: Xiaomeng Wang, Hamsa Bastani, Osbert Bastani, Zhimei Ren

entry.summary: Studies adaptive targeting under network interference in a bandit setting where treatments spill over to others, establishing a regret lower bound and analyzing regimes with varying knowledge of the interference structure. It shows ignoring network structure leads to inefficient learning in large populations.

entry.title: How VLAs Fail Differently: Black-Box Action Monitoring Reveals Architecture-Specific Failure Signatures

author.name: Krishnam Gupta

entry.summary: This paper shows that different VLA architectures fail in predictable, architecture-specific ways at the motor-command level, finding direction reversal rate is a universal failure predictor while jerk monitoring works only for discrete-token policies. It critiques velocity-checking as the common but ineffective safety mechanism in deployment.

entry.title: UNIQUE: Universal Top-k Sparse Attention for Training-free Inference and Sparsity-aware Training

author.name: Keqi Deng, Shaoshi Ling, Ruchao Fan, Jinyu Li

entry.summary: UNIQUE is a universal top-k sparse attention framework operating at KV-page granularity, estimating per-page importance with a simple score combining key means and standard deviations for both training-free inference and sparsity-aware training. It addresses the KV cache bottleneck in long-context LLMs.

entry.title: Building Community-Centred NLP Resources for Puno Quechua

author.name: Elwin Huaman, Adrian Gamarra Lafuente, Johanna Cordova, Anna Korhonen

entry.summary: This work presents the first dedicated ASR resources for Puno Quechua, including a 66-hour speech corpus collected via participatory design and a systematic benchmark fine-tuning Whisper, wav2vec2, and XLS-R. It matters for low-resource language preservation and community-centred NLP.

entry.title: FABSVer: Faster Training and Better Self-Verification for LLM Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Haihui Pan, Junwei Bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang Song

entry.summary: FABSVer fuses solution generation and self-verification into a single generation pass to reduce training overhead for LLM mathematical reasoning. It also identifies and addresses a convergence bottleneck caused by a fixed reference model.

entry.title: The Abstraction Gap in Vision-Language Causal Reasoning

author.name: Chinh Hoang, Mohammad Rashedul Hasan

entry.summary: This paper introduces a dual-probe methodology and Abstraction Gap metric to distinguish linguistic plausibility from faithful causal reasoning in VLMs, evaluated on the 49,500-question CAGE benchmark across Pearl's causal hierarchy. Seven of eight models show large abstraction gaps.

entry.title: Long Live the Librarian! A Persistent Search Sub-Agent for Energy-Efficient Multi-Agent Software Engineering Systems

author.name: Seunghyuk Cho, Sunghyun Choi, Jaeseung Heo, Youngbin Choi, Saemi Moon, MoonJeong Park, Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: Librarian is a persistent search sub-agent that tracks repository-search history to suppress redundant output tokens in multi-agent software engineering systems. It addresses energy inefficiency, noting output tokens cost 30-1000x more energy than input/cached tokens.

entry.title: Skill-as-Pseudocode: Refactoring Skill Libraries to Pseudocode for LLM Agents

author.name: Xinze Li, Yuhang Zang, Yixin Cao, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: Skill-as-Pseudocode automatically converts free-form markdown skill libraries into typed pseudocode with a four-check deterministic verifier for LLM agents. It addresses the confused-re-retrieve loop caused by agents re-deriving schemas and invocation syntax.

entry.title: MaskClaw: Edge-Side Personalized Privacy Arbitration for GUI Agents with Behavior-Driven Skill Evolution

author.name: Yanqiu Zhao, Dongying Zheng, Kaibo Huang, Yukun Wei, Zhongliang Yang, Linna Zhou

entry.summary: MaskClaw is an edge-side privacy arbitrator for GUI agents that decides Allow, Mask, or Ask on screenshots before raw screen data leaves a trusted environment. It uses local visual evidence and user-specific policy memory with behavior-driven skill evolution.

entry.title: Every9D-21M: Large-Scale Real-World 9D Canonicalization of Everyday Objects

author.name: Leonhard Sommer, Emil Akopyan, Adam Kortylewski

entry.summary: Every9D-21M is a large-scale real-world 9D pose dataset with annotations for 21.8M images across 700 everyday object categories, generated by reconstructing object-centric videos. It is two orders of magnitude larger than prior real-world 9D pose benchmarks.

entry.title: EgoRelight: Egocentric Human Capture and Illumination Recovery for Relightable and Photoreal Avatar Rendering

author.name: Jianchun Chen, Yinda Zhang, Rohit Pandey, Thabo Beeler, Marc Habermann, Christian Theobalt

entry.summary: EgoRelight is a holistic framework for egocentric telepresence that simultaneously captures full-body human performance, synthesizes relightable photorealistic appearance, and estimates lighting from a head-mounted display's constrained viewpoint. It unifies tasks previously treated in isolation.

entry.title: GEM: Generative Supervision Helps Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Ruowen Zhao, Bangguo Li, Zuyan Liu, Yinan Liang, Junliang Ye, Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Zhengyi Wang, Xumin Yu, Yongming Rao, Han Hu, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: GEM integrates a depth-map generation task into vision-language model pretraining for embodied intelligence, bridging the gap between high-level semantics and low-level spatial knowledge. The generative supervision substantially improves embodied task performance within VLA frameworks.

entry.title: OSP-Next: Efficient High-Quality Video Generation with Sparse Sequence Parallelism, HiF8 Quantization, and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yunyang Ge, Xianyi He, Zezhong Zhang, Bin Lin, Bin Zhu, Xinhua Cheng, Li Yuan

entry.summary: OSP-Next is an efficient text-to-video generation model integrating sparse attention (Skiparse-2D), sparse sequence parallelism, HiF8 quantization, and reinforcement learning to reduce the quadratic cost of full attention. It maintains FlashAttention compatibility while improving efficiency.

entry.title: Colosseum V2: Benchmarking Generalization for Vision Language Action Models

author.name: Jeremy Morgan, Prajwal Vijay, Hyeonho Oh, Jincen Song, Ashvin Arora, Alina Du, Gaurav Sukhatme, Jesse Thomason, Ishika Singh

entry.summary: Colosseum V2 is a large-scale simulation benchmark for evaluating the generalization of vision-language-action models in robotic manipulation across 28 tasks, 13 categories, and two robot morphologies under diverse distribution shifts. It systematically reveals gaps between VLA perception/language abilities and robust behavior.

entry.title: What Frozen VLAs Already Know About Success: A Probing Study of Value-Like Structure in Foundation Robot Policies

author.name: Jiachen Zhang (Peking University, China Agricultural University), Junnan Nie (Peking University), Junyi Lao (Peking University), Wei Cheng (Peking University), Chenghao Liu (Peking University), Jiaxin Jiang (China Agricultural University), Songfang Huang (Peking University)

entry.summary: A probing study showing that frozen VLA policy representations (OpenVLA, Pi0.5, DINOv2, CLIP) implicitly encode value-like information about task success, recoverable via lightweight linear probes despite never being trained on reward. The signal exceeds baselines based on progress, time-to-go, or proprioception, suggesting reward structure can guide action choice without retraining.

entry.title: PEAM: Parametric Embodied Agent Memory through Contrastive Internalization of Experience in Minecraft

author.name: Yuchen Guo, Junli Gong, Hongmin Cai, Yiu-ming Cheung, Weifeng Su

entry.summary: Presents PEAM, an embodied Minecraft agent that converts retrieval-based memory into parameter-resident skills via a multimodal MoE-LoRA architecture, pairing a slow deliberative LLM with a fast reflexive module and treating failures as first-class training signals. It enables continual skill internalization without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: EAPO: Entropy-Driven Adaptive Positive-Negative Sample Weighting for Policy Optimization in Open-Ended QA

author.name: Yunsheng Zeng, Gen Li, Yuwei Miao, Xiandong Li, Yujin Wang, Siyu Chen, Luning Wang, Yunhao Qiao, Junfeng Wang, Jianwei Lv, Bo Yuan

entry.summary: Proposes EAPO, an entropy-driven adaptive weighting of positive and negative samples for RLVR in open-ended QA, finding negative samples govern diversity and the performance ceiling while positives drive quality and convergence. It generalizes verifiable-reward RL beyond closed-form tasks.

entry.title: Dr-CiK: A Testbed for Foresight-Driven Agents

author.name: Yihong Tang, Andrew Robert Williams, Arjun Ashok, Vincent Zhihao Zheng, Lijun Sun, Alexandre Drouin, Issam H. Laradji, \'Etienne Marcotte, Valentina Zantedeschi

entry.summary: Introduces Dr-CiK, a benchmark testing whether forecasting agents can autonomously retrieve, filter, and distill external context from a document corpus and produce evidence-supported forecasts, rather than assuming context is provided. It evaluates deep-research and forecasting agents under context ablations.

entry.title: MIRA: A Bilingual Benchmark for Medical Information Response Audit

author.name: Mengyu Xu, Qiaoxin Yang, Qianqian Wang, Xiwei Dai, Weiyi Wu, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: Introduces MIRA, a bilingual benchmark auditing whether LLMs provide comparable medical information across user phrasing, register, and health-literacy signals, finding low-health-literacy phrasings consistently receive less complete information. It surfaces an equity gap in health-information responses.

entry.title: Look on Demand: A Cognitive Scheduling Framework for Visual Evidence Acquisition in Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yang Zhang, Xiaoshuai Sun, Rui Zhao, Wujin Sun, Yidong Chen, Jiayi Ji, Qian Chen, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: This work proposes a cognitive scheduling framework that decides how and when to introduce visual evidence into multimodal reasoning, avoiding both static visual-to-text loss and linguistic dominance. It addresses faithfulness to visual evidence in multimodal models.

entry.title: Plan Before Search: Search Agents Need Plan

author.name: Zhipeng Qian, Zihan Liang, Yufei Ma, Ben Chen, Huangyu Dai, Jiayi Ji, Chenyi Lei, Wenwu Ou, Xiaoshuai Sun, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: Plan Before Search argues that retrieval-augmented reasoning agents benefit from explicitly decomposing questions into ordered sub-questions before retrieval, anchoring each search step to avoid drift. It questions whether SFT distillation is the only route to acquiring this planning skill.

entry.title: Do Agents Know What They Can't Do? Evaluating Feasibility Awareness in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Liang Cheng, Mingsheng Cai, Jiuming Jiang, Luo Mai

entry.summary: FeasiGen is an automatic pipeline that constructs infeasible agent tasks by identifying critical tools required for success, enabling evaluation of whether tool-using agents recognize tasks they cannot complete. Detecting infeasibility early can reduce wasted execution cost.

entry.title: MUSE: Benchmarking Manufacturable, Functional, and Assemblable Text-to-CAD Generation

author.name: Xiaoyu Dong, Zhi Li, Xiao-Ming Wu

entry.summary: MUSE is a Text-to-CAD benchmark focused on complex editable boundary-representation assemblies, evaluating manufacturability, functionality, and assemblability through a three-stage code, geometry, and design-intent protocol. It moves beyond single-part geometric-similarity evaluation toward industrial design realism.

entry.title: VeriTrip: A Verifiable Benchmark for Travel Planning Agents over Unstructured Web Corpora

author.name: Yuting Xu, Jiayi Tian, Jian Liang, Xin Xiong, Hang Zhang, Mu Xu, Xiao-Yu Zhang

entry.summary: VeriTrip is a verifiable benchmark for travel-planning agents that shifts evaluation to evidence-grounded reasoning over unstructured multimodal web corpora, incorporating information noise, source contradictions, and visual grounding. It moves beyond API-centric tool-execution paradigms.

entry.title: Modeling Community Attitude through Reaction Tone: A Human-AI Collaborative Framework for Evaluating LLM Alignment with Linguistic Behaviors in Online Communities

author.name: Nuan Wen, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: CARE is a reaction-centered framework benchmarking whether LLM-simulated discourse matches authentic community responses to real-world news, using a fine-grained spectrum of illocutionary tones validated through human-AI collaboration. It moves beyond static social-identity labels in computational social analysis.

entry.title: FD-RAG: Federated Dual-System Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Tianhao Gao, Kai Yang, Yiyang Li

entry.summary: FD-RAG is a federated dual-system RAG framework that decouples lightweight memory access from on-demand LLM reasoning for edge deployment, learning adaptive hypergraphs over local corpora distilled into compact QA memories. It addresses fragmented knowledge and expensive LLM calls in decentralized settings.

entry.title: Beyond Motion Primitives: Behavioral Activity Recognition from Head-Mounted IMU

author.name: Chung-Ta Huang, Leopold Das, Jeffrey Zhou, Faizaan Siddique, Julia Seungjoo Baek, Serena Liu, Andrew Rusli, Todd Y. Zhou, Freddy Yu, Sinclair Hansen, Ziling Hu, Arnav Sharma, Mengyu Wang

entry.summary: This work pushes beyond motion primitives to behavioral-level activity recognition from head-mounted IMU sensors for AR smart glasses, building a 160K-sample Ego4D dataset and a 703K-parameter hierarchical HiT-HAR model. It maps the observability frontier of head-mounted IMU sensing.

entry.title: BIRDS: Characterizing and Understanding Biodiversity Impact of Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Tianyao Shi, Yi Ding

entry.summary: BIRDS is a framework quantifying the biodiversity impact of request-driven LLM serving, defining request-level functional units, operational and embodied impacts, and a Quality-Normalized Biodiversity Impact metric. It exposes quality-aware serving tradeoffs across models, GPUs, and regions.

entry.title: UserHarness: Harnessing User Minds for Stronger Agent Theory-of-Mind

author.name: Cheng Qian, Jiayu Liu, Heng Ji

entry.summary: UserHarness is a framework for improving agent Theory-of-Mind by explicitly reconstructing a user's mental state—beliefs updated through observations, intentions, and nested beliefs—rather than modeling behavior indirectly. It targets more effective agent assistants.

entry.title: ReSAE: Residualized Sparse Autoencoders for Multi-Layer Transformer Interventions

author.name: Prathyush Poduval, Calvin Yeung, Neel Desai, Mohsen Imani

entry.summary: ReSAEs fit affine maps between transformer layers and train each later-layer sparse autoencoder on the unexplained residual rather than the full activation, addressing the redundancy and interaction problems of layerwise dictionaries. This enables more coherent multi-layer interventions.

entry.title: Where Does Toxicity Live? Mechanistic Localization and Targeted Suppression in Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Beniwal, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: This paper introduces two retraining-free frameworks (Meow2X and TRNE) that localize toxicity to specific layers and neurons via activation differentials and suppress it through inference-time scaling or minimal rank-one weight edits. It reduces toxicity across five models without gradient descent while preserving language modeling quality.

entry.title: Extracting Small Translation Specialists from LLMs by Aggressively Pruning Experts

author.name: Liu O. Martin, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This paper aggressively prunes experts from mixture-of-experts LLMs to extract small translation specialists, exploiting expert specialization and the separability of multilingual capabilities. The pruning requires no retraining and incurs negligible translation quality loss.

entry.title: Learning the Error Patterns of Language Models

author.name: Jinwoo Kim, Taylor Berg-KirkPatrick, Loris D'Antoni

entry.summary: This work introduces prefix filters, learned symbolic functions that capture the focused error patterns of LLMs in constrained-validity domains (like generating valid TypeScript), with an algorithm called Palla to learn them efficiently. The filters both quantify error patterns and constrain model outputs via constrained sampling.

entry.title: Measuring Form and Function in Language Models

author.name: H\'ector Javier V\'azquez Mart\'inez, Charles Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces quantitative child-language-acquisition metrics to evaluate language models on the syntactic and discourse properties of English determiners, proposing a Contextual Alternative Choice prompting method. It enables direct comparison of models against children and independently established empirical benchmarks, finding only very large models meet both formal and functional benchmarks.

entry.title: MemTrace: Tracing and Attributing Errors in Large Language Model Memory Systems

author.name: Xinle Deng, Ruobin Zhong, Hujin Peng, Xiaoben Lu, Yanzhe Wu, Guang Li, Buqiang Xu, Yunzhi Yao, Jizhan Fang, Haoliang Cao, Junjie Guo, Yuan Yuan, Ziqing Ma, Yuanqiang Yu, Rui Hu, Baohua Dong, Hangcheng Zhu, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: MemTrace studies error tracing and attribution in LLM memory systems by transforming memory pipelines into executable memory evolution graphs for fine-grained tracing of information flow. It introduces MemTraceBench collected from systems like Long-Context, RAG, Mem0, and EverMemOS to study memory failure modes.

entry.title: Explicit Critic Guidance for Aligning Diffusion Models

author.name: Zhengyang Liang, Qihang Zhang, Ceyuan Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a state-aligned latent actor-critic framework for aligning diffusion models via online RL, where the diffusion model serves as its own timestep-conditioned value function predicting on noisy latents. This enables trajectory-level PPO and reusable critic guidance for inference-time steering.

entry.title: Revisiting ML Training under Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Convergence Guarantees, Differential Privacy, and Efficient Algorithms

author.name: Yvonne Zhou, Mingyu Liang, Ivan Brugere, Danial Dervovic, Yue Guo, Antigoni Polychroniadou, Min Wu, Dana Dachman-Soled

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical convergence analysis of ML training under fully homomorphic encryption combined with a differentially private algorithm tailored to encrypted computation, using polynomial approximations of activations. It improves efficiency over standard DP-GD while preserving privacy without per-sample gradient clipping.

entry.title: Measure-to-measure Regression with Transformers

author.name: Matthew Vandergrift, Martha White, Yury Polyanskiy, Philippe Rigollet, Lazar Atanackovic

entry.summary: Studies measure-to-measure regression, learning maps between probability measures (point clouds) from observed input-output measure pairs using transformers, treating whole distributions as data points. This is motivated by applications like cell populations that evolve collectively rather than independently.

entry.title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Mufan Qiu, Genhui Zheng, Yinuo Xu, Ruichen Zhang, Ying Ding, Qi Long, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Chreode is a one-step cell world model predicting action-conditioned cell-state transitions (developmental signals, genetic perturbations) via a structured residual transition operator with a Waddington-inspired decomposition. It shifts distributional evolution to training time for single-pass generation, generalizing across datasets.

entry.title: Mitigating Adaptive Attacks against Reasoning Models with Activation Consistency Training

author.name: Avidan Shah, Jannik Brinkmann, Rico Angell

entry.summary: Studies consistency training to defend reasoning models against adaptive jailbreaks and prompt injection, comparing output-level (BCT) and activation-level (ACT) variants across five reasoning models. Finds ACT competitive with other training-based defenses while requiring only self-supervised clean/wrapped prompt pairs and remaining more robust under adaptive attacks.

entry.title: Thinned Mean Field Langevin Dynamics

author.name: Zonghao Chen, Heishiro Kanagawa, Fran\c{c}ois-Xavier Briol, Chris J. Oates, Lester Mackey

entry.summary: Proposes KT-MFLD, which reduces the quadratic cost of mean-field Langevin dynamics by having each particle interact only with a thinned coreset of size order square-root N. This leverages kernel thinning to cut computational complexity while preserving convergence properties.

entry.title: Affective Music Recommendation: A Rollout-Based World Model for Offline Preference Optimization

author.name: Audrey Chan, Aaron Labb\'e, Jacob Lavoie, Jordan Bannister, Ars\`ene Fansi Tchango, Guillaume Lajoie, Laurent Charlin

entry.summary: Describes AMRS, a deployed affective music recommendation system built around a rollout-based causal transformer world model for offline preference optimization. It serves clinical and consumer wellness users where online emotional experimentation is ethically constrained.

entry.title: A Unified Structured Query Understanding Framework for Industrial Semantic Search

author.name: Ping Liu, Qianqi Shen, Jianqiang Shen, Chunnan Yao, Kevin Kao, Rajat Arora, Dan Xu, Baofen Zheng, Yunxiang Ren, Benjamin Le, Ali Hooshmand, Igor Lapchuk, Juan Bottaro, Raghavan Muthuregunathan, Caleb Johnson, Liangjie Hong, Jingwei Wu, Wenjing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes and deploys a unified structured query understanding system consolidating fragmented industrial search components into a single small language model performing schema-constrained generation. It introduces Query Illuminator, a teacher model for auto-annotation and distillation.

entry.title: Semiparametrically Efficient Inference for Kernel Measures of Noise Heterogeneity

author.name: Jakub Wornbard, Zikai Shen, Dimitri Meunier, Arthur Gretton

entry.summary: Develops semiparametrically efficient inference for kernel measures of noise heterogeneity in additive noise models, constructing a Hilbert-valued one-step estimator that corrects first-stage ML regression bias. It yields bootstrap-calibrated tests for residual independence and goodness of fit.

entry.title: {\Omega}-QVLA: Robust Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models via Composite Rotation and Per-step Scaling

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Mingze Li, Sicheng Lyu, Dongxiu Liu, Kaicheng Yang, Ziyu Zhao, Yufei Cui, Xiao-Wen Chang, Peng Lu

entry.summary: Omega-QVLA is a training-free post-training quantization framework that compresses both the language backbone and the entire diffusion action head of VLA models to uniform W4A4 precision using composite rotation and per-step scaling. It challenges the belief that uniformly quantizing action heads is unstable.

entry.title: ReverseMath: Answer Inversion for Scalable and Verifiable Mathematical Problem Generation

author.name: Raoyuan Zhao, Yihong Liu, Yupei Du, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: ReverseMath scalably generates new math problems by masking a numerical value, treating the original answer as a known condition, and rewriting so the masked value becomes the new answer with verifiable correctness. It mitigates benchmark contamination and memorization issues in LLM math evaluation.

entry.title: Escape the Language Prior: Mitigating Late-Stage Modality Collapse in Audio Reasoning via Modality-Aware Policy Optimization

author.name: Cihan Xiao, Yiwen Shao, Chenxing Li, Xiang He, Zhenwen Liang, Steve Yves, Sanjeev Khudanpur, Liefeng Bo
